records.title: [Flow Control] Guide posture, docs, and validation for flow control (GA, opt-in)
records.body:
Flow control is GA in llm-d-router 0.10 but stays explicitly opt-in; the default flip is deferred (decision: https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d-router/pull/2180#issuecomment-5119639333, router tracker llm-d-router#1187). This issue covers the llm-d side: the surfaces that run the gate on, what the docs need to say for anyone opting in, and how we validate flow control behavior. Router work stays on llm-d-router#1187.

With the gate off by default, nothing changes for the guides that do not set it. Two shipped surfaces run flow control on today: the `flow-control` guide and `workload-autoscaling`'s `keda-epp` path. They are the scope here, together with the shared opt-in note. Nothing below binds on the v0.9.0 code freeze, though the two pre-existing breaks are still worth fixing for the release.

## What changes when the gate is on

Under saturation, requests queue and are admitted by priority instead of being rejected. Sheddable (negative-priority) requests buffer until TTL or a capacity limit.

With zero ready endpoints, requests wait rather than fast-failing; `controller/internal/processor.go:297` calls the empty pool a scale-from-zero waiting room.

`defaultRequestTTL` is 60s (`controller/config.go:33`). An explicit `0s` disables it, and validation rejects only negatives (`config.go:45,127`). Six guides set `requestTimeout: "0s"` via `recipes/router/features/httproute-flags.yaml` (`pd-disaggregation`, `wide-ep-lws`, `flow-control`, `precise-prefix-cache-routing`, `predicted-latency-routing`, `multimodal-serving/e-disaggregation`); if any of those opts in, the TTL is the only shed valve in the stack. The rest inherit the provider's gateway timeout, usually shorter than 60s, so a queued request there surfaces as a 504 before the TTL fires. Both behaviours belong in the shared note.

## Fixes

Four fixes, one PR.

- [ ] The `flow-control` guide's CRD prerequisite 404s. `guides/flow-control/README.md:92` builds the URL from `${ROUTER_CHART_VERSION}`, which `guides/env.sh:8` pins to `v0`, an OCI chart tag being used as a GitHub release tag. That URL returns 404; `v0.9.0` returns 200 and contains `inferenceobjectives.llm-d.ai`. The line can't just be deleted: `guides/flow-control/objectives.yaml` is `apiVersion: llm-d.ai/v1alpha2`, and GAIE v1.5.0's `v1-manifests.yaml` ships only `inferencepools.inference.networking.k8s.io`. So nobody following this guide by hand can create the InferenceObjectives, and the priority bands it exists to demonstrate never get defined. `env.sh` needs a router release version variable; there isn't one today.
- [ ] `workload-autoscaling`'s scale-to-zero docs promise more than the gate delivers. `README.hpa-epp.md:407` says EPP holds incoming requests until a model server becomes Ready. The 60s TTL bounds that hold, and a vLLM cold start doesn't fit inside it. Fix the text and add a cold-start-sized `flowControl.defaultRequestTTL` to the scale-to-zero opt-in.
- [ ] One shared flow-control note in `guides/recipes/router/README.md`. Every guide layers `recipes/router/base.values.yaml`, and that README already has a Values Layering section. There are 28 READMEs under `guides/`, so a per-guide note would be an unreviewable PR.
- [ ] `guides/README.md:29` links to `./rollouts/README.md`, which doesn't exist.

### Where the keda-epp TTL goes

`keda-epp/scaledobject.yaml:30` is `minReplicaCount: 1`, so the shipped path always has a ready endpoint and the empty-pool wait never triggers. Scale-to-zero is optional and lives only in prose at `README.hpa-epp.md:401-417`.

That decides where the fix lands. `defaultRequestTTL: 10m` in `keda-epp/router.values.yaml` would give the default `minReplicaCount: 1` path a ten-minute queue wait under saturation, worse than the 60s it has today. The TTL belongs beside `minReplicaCount: 0` in the opt-in.

Turning the gate off is wrong either way: it would throw away the priority behaviour that path demonstrates, and the KEDA trigger scales on `llm_d_epp_flow_control_queue_size`, which only exists when the gate is on.

### What the shared docs note should cover

- Flow control is GA and opt-in; `featureGates: ["flowControl"]` turns it on
- Requests queue under saturation and are admitted by priority
- With zero ready endpoints requests wait, bounded by `defaultRequestTTL` (60s) or by the gateway timeout where that's shorter
- The six `requestTimeout: "0s"` guides would have the TTL as their only shed valve if they opt in; the rest see a provider 504 first
- Tuning: per-band `maxRequests` and `maxBytes`, `defaultRequestTTL`, priority holdback
- The dependency on model-server scrape health. The saturation detector scores each pod from `WaitingQueue` and `KVCacheUsage`, pulled by the EPP's own poll of the model servers. If that goes stale or empty across all endpoints, everything reads as saturated and dispatch halts (llm-d-router#2100). Separate from the Prometheus-scrapes-the-router path in #1777.

## Validation

- [ ] #1918, restore the bespoke flow-control nightly. With the fleet running the gate-off default, this is the only automated lane that exercises flow control behaviour at all (backpressure, per-band isolation, priority QoS).
- [ ] Write `guide_flow-control_1.yaml`. The one guide whose purpose is queue contention has no workload that produces any, which is why #1918 carries it commented out.
- [ ] A/B at saturating load: `optimized-baseline` first, then `pd-disaggregation`, which is the interesting one because P/D saturation gating (llm-d-router#1186) isn't ready and the saturation signal there is untested. Not time-pressured: the FC-off arm is the shipped default and stays dispatchable indefinitely. This is the operator-facing evidence for opting in (goals 2 and 3) and the baseline for any future default-flip revisit.

| # | Goal | Covered by | State |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Feature completeness: the gate-on surfaces stand up and serve | #1918's lane; `keda-epp` has none (see CI) | gap |
| 2 | Change of behavior: what an operator sees differently after opting in | the A/B | not started |
| 3 | Performance: cost of opting in against published numbers | the A/B | not started |
| 4 | Logging, metrics, tracing: queue state is observable | #1777, llm-d-router#2102 | not started |
| 5 | Reliability: failure modes known and bounded | #1918's lane | in progress |
| 6 | Operations: how to run it, tune it, turn it off | the docs note above, #1519 | not started |

All 34 lanes run `sanity_random.yaml` (#1725, merged Jun 8, described as temporary, with nothing tracking the revert), so there has been no perf signal from CI for six weeks. A sanity workload also never queues, and flow control is work-conserving, so under non-saturating load FC-on and FC-off are identical by construction.

The A/B doesn't need manual standup: per-guide profiles exist in `llm-d-benchmark/workload/profiles/inference-perf/` and every lane still declares a `workload` dispatch input. Six guides publish committed benchmark reports with hardware specified (`optimized-baseline`, `tiered-prefix-cache`, `precise-prefix-cache-routing`, `predicted-latency-routing` and `agentic-serving` under `benchmark-results/`, `pd-disaggregation` inline in its README); where that hardware isn't reproducible, an FC-off control run on whatever is available does the same job.

Goals 4, 5 and 6 are desk work: metrics and tracing coverage (#1777, llm-d-router#2102), the failure-mode enumeration, and the operations guide (#1519). #1918's lane covers the backpressure, per-band isolation and priority-QoS half of goal 5 once it's green.

The 2026-07-25 per-lane pass-rate baseline on llm-d-router#1187 stays the reference point for any future default-flip revisit.

## CI

- [ ] #1918, see above.
- [ ] `keda-epp` has no nightly coverage. `grep -rn keda-epp .github/` returns nothing, and the green OCP lane exercises the FC-off path. Tracked separately in TBD.
- [ ] llm-d-infra's `reusable-ci-nightly-benchmark.yaml` has a flow-control special case that borrows optimized-baseline's modelserver overlay, but it runs after the model-detection step that needs the missing directory. Dead code.

## Related issues

None of these block v0.9.0; they matter to anyone opting in.

- #1777, router monitoring in the well-lit guides. The monitoring sections cover model servers only, so the EPP's own metrics aren't scraped anywhere. With flow control on they're the only view of whether a request is queued or in flight, and a dispatch halt otherwise looks like everything hanging and then 503ing.
- #1519, operational flows documentation. FC state is per-replica, so in active-active mode fairness holds only within each replica's slice and per-band limits multiply by replica count. llm-d-router#2180 documents that in the router's `docs/operations.md`, which guide readers never open.
- #1525, request draining in all guides. Drain semantics and 503 mapping are FC-adjacent; llm-d-router#1187 has an open question on dispatch-until-deadline against immediate evict.
- #1516, migrate CI to nightly images. Because the charts pin EPP to `:main`, a default flip could not have been staged from the router side; pinned nightly images would make a future one controllable.

## Not tracked here

Router hardening, perf numbers, and router-side observability and reliability work all live on llm-d-router#1187. The deferred default flip is llm-d-router#2104.

records.title: [Bug :bug:]: optimized-baseline trtllm decode pods exit Error, startup probe never passes
records.body:
### Contact Details

lukevandrie@google.com

### What happened?

The `optimized-baseline-gke-acc-gpu-trtllm-x` nightly lane is 3/7 over the last week. It is the only nightly lane where the workload starts and then dies, rather than failing to schedule, so it is the only one that currently looks like a product or image problem rather than cluster capacity.

On [run 30272097869](https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d/actions/runs/30272097869) both decode pods reached terminal `Error` at 2m10s. The TRT-LLM server never binds `:8000`, so the startup probe against `/v1/models` fails until the pod is killed.

Two candidate causes appear in the captured container output and I could not separate them:

1. `transformers 5.5.4 is incompatible with nvidia-modelopt` — a version conflict inside the vendor image `nvcr.io/nvidia/tensorrt-llm/release:1.3.0rc18`.
2. `You are sending unauthenticated requests to the HF Hub. Please set a HF_TOKEN` — the job sets both `LLMDBENCH_HF_TOKEN` and `HF_TOKEN`, yet the container is making unauthenticated Hub requests. A rate-limited or failed weight download would explain the server never starting.

The second is the more suspicious. No Python traceback survives in the captured logs, so the fatal line is still unknown.

**Expected:** decode pods become Ready and serve `/v1/models`, as the vllm and sglang variants of the same guide do on the same cluster.

**Actual:** both decode pods exit with `Error` roughly two minutes in, every time the lane gets far enough to deploy.

- Confirm whether `HF_TOKEN` is propagated into the trtllm modelserver pod spec the way it is for the vllm and sglang variants.
- Capture the full decode container log on failure. The current tail cuts off before the fatal error.
- Confirm `1.3.0rc18` is the intended pin — it is a release candidate, and the transformers/modelopt conflict is inside the vendor image.

records.title: The documented router install fails on any cluster without the Prometheus Operator
records.body:
### **The Problem**
The Router Helm chart is designed to render a `ServiceMonitor` (API version `monitoring.coreos.com/v1`, kind `ServiceMonitor`) when Prometheus monitoring is enabled via the `router.monitoring.prometheus.enabled: true` value. 

On any Kubernetes cluster where the Prometheus Operator (or its Custom Resource Definitions) is not already installed, Helm's client-side resource validation fails to resolve this Group/Version/Kind and aborts the entire installation with the following error:

```text
Error: unable to build kubernetes objects from release manifest: resource mapping not found for name: "optimized-baseline-epp-monitor" namespace: "my-namespace" from "": no matches for kind "ServiceMonitor" in version "monitoring.coreos.com/v1" ensure CRDs are installed first
```

#### **Where & Why This Occurs**

1. **`guides/recipes/router/README.md`**
   The canonical/unqualified install commands listed under both **Standalone** (line 15) and **With Kubernetes Gateway API** (line 36) modes hardcode the layering of the monitoring values file:
   ```bash
   helm install <release-name> \
     ${ROUTER_STANDALONE_CHART} \
     -f ${REPO_ROOT}/guides/recipes/router/base.values.yaml \
     -f ${REPO_ROOT}/guides/recipes/router/features/monitoring.values.yaml \ # <--- Included by default
     -f ${REPO_ROOT}/guides/<your-guide>/router/<your-guide>.values.yaml \
     --set provider.name=<gke|istio|none> \
     -n ${NAMESPACE} \
     --version ${ROUTER_CHART_VERSION}
   ```
   A user copying these default instructions onto a clean cluster is blocked immediately.

2. **`guides/optimized-baseline/README.md`**
   While `MONITORING_VALUES` is empty/disabled by default in this guide, a user who proactively uncomments the option in **Step 1** (to deploy the router with monitoring) will hit the same fatal error. This is because the prerequisite monitoring stack (which supplies the required CRDs via `guides/recipes/observability/install-prometheus-grafana.sh`) is not set up or documented until **Step 3**.

---

### **Steps to Reproduce**

1. Provision a clean Kubernetes cluster (e.g. GKE or Kind) without installing any Prometheus Operator or kube-prometheus-stack beforehand.
2. Attempt to install the router chart following the default standalone instructions in `guides/recipes/router/README.md`:
   ```bash
   helm install test-router \
     ${ROUTER_STANDALONE_CHART} \
     -f ${REPO_ROOT}/guides/recipes/router/base.values.yaml \
     -f ${REPO_ROOT}/guides/recipes/router/features/monitoring.values.yaml \
     --set provider.name=none \
     -n test-namespace \
     --version ${ROUTER_CHART_VERSION}
   ```
3. Observe the fatal validation error and the aborted installation.

---

### **Suggested Solutions**

* **Option 1 (Recommended)**: Remove `-f ${REPO_ROOT}/guides/recipes/router/features/monitoring.values.yaml` from the default, canonical install commands in `guides/recipes/router/README.md`. Move it into a dedicated, optional "Enable Monitoring" step that instructs the user to run a `helm upgrade` or add the flag *only after* they have successfully deployed the monitoring stack.
* **Option 2**: Explicitly document the Prometheus Operator CRDs as a prerequisite in the router guides, providing a direct reference/link to `guides/recipes/observability/install-prometheus-grafana.sh` (or suggesting the use of a `--crds-only` installation) before deploying the router.

records.title: [Feature]: Improve readability of the optimized-baseline guide
records.body:
### Feature Area

Documentation / Guides

### Problem Statement

The `guides/optimized-baseline/README.md` is comprehensive but difficult to follow compared to the streamlined `docs/getting-started/quickstart.md`. Users unfamiliar with the project hit several friction points when walking through it manually:

1. **Too many conditional branches inline** — Standalone vs Gateway, GPU vs non-GPU, vllm vs trtllm are all interleaved in the same flow with commented-out blocks. Users must mentally parse which lines apply to their setup.

2. **Environment variables are split across two locations** — Some are set in the README itself, others come from `source guides/env.sh`, but the dependency is not clear until a later command fails with an unresolved variable (e.g. `${GAIE_VERSION}`).

3. **No resource requirements stated upfront** — The default configuration requires 16 GPUs (8 replicas × 2 GPUs). Users with smaller clusters deploy and immediately hit hundreds of failed pods with no prior warning.

4. **Helm values passed via string variables are fragile** — `ROUTER_BASE_VALUES="-f /path/..."` embeds the `-f` flag inside the value; when `MONITORING_VALUES` is empty, shell expansion can break Helm argument parsing in some environments.

5. **No "minimal / smoke-test" path** — There is no guidance for users who want to validate the deployment path with fewer resources before committing to the full 16-GPU configuration.

### Proposed Solution

Use `docs/getting-started/quickstart.md` as a style reference:

- **Linear, single-path flow by default** (Standalone + GPU + vllm), with alternatives in collapsible `<details>` blocks that don't break the reading flow.
- **Source `env.sh` first**, before any variable is referenced, with a brief note listing the key variables it provides.
- **State hardware requirements explicitly** in Prerequisites, linking to the Configuration table.
- **Add a "Minimal setup" note** (1 replica, TP=1) for users who want to verify the path with limited resources.
- **Simplify Helm invocation** by using `-f path` directly instead of embedding flags in variables, or at minimum document the known shell-expansion caveat.

### Alternatives Considered

_No response_

### Willingness to Contribute

Yes, I can submit a PR

### Additional Context

_No response_

records.title: [Observability][Feature]: TPU Observability
records.body:
### Feature Area

Observability / Monitoring

### Problem Statement

#### Problem Statement
- **Hardware Telemetry Gap**: llm-d lacks integration with Google's tpu-metrics-exporter (libtpu / XLA layer), missing MXU duty cycle, VPU utilization, physical HBM usage, PCIe throughput, and ICI interconnect traffic.
- **Comparison to GPU**: On GPUs, hardware metrics (utilization, VRAM, NVLink, PCIe) are already collected via NVIDIA DCGM exporter (DCGM_FI_DEV_*). DCGM is not installed by llm-d by default; rather, it runs at the K8s node infrastructure level and is scraped by llm-d's Prometheus recipes.

##### Missing Metrics
1. **libtpu / Device**
    - MXU Duty Cycle (tpu_mxu_duty_cycle)
    - VPU Utilization (tpu_vpu_duty_cycle)
    - HBM Capacity Utilized (tpu_hbm_memory_used_bytes)
    - HBM Bandwidth Utilized (tpu_hbm_bandwidth_bytes_per_sec)

2. **TPU interconnect**
    - ICI Network Bandwidth (based on tpu_ici_tx_bytes_total)
    - Interconnect Drops (based on tpu_ici_drop_packets_total)
    - Host-to-Device Transfer (based on tpu_pcie_tx_bytes_total) 
    - Device-to-Host Transfer (based on tpu_pcie_rx_bytes_tota)
    - ICI physical link health (tpu_ici_link_status)

3. **TPU Topology and Type**: On GKE, Cloud TPU topology shapes (e.g. 2x4, 2x2x1) and accelerator types (tpu-v6e-slice) exist as Kubernetes node/pod labels (`cloud.google.com/gke-tpu-topology` and `cloud.google.com/gke-tpu-accelerator`). However, these metrics are not surfaced in llm-d stack.

#### Future Work to Consider
- **Goodput**: llm-d cannot differentiate between tokens delivered to users vs. tokens wasted due to TPU slice preemption, bad chip restarts, or cold-start recompilations.
- **Granular Error Codes**: Errors are aggregated at the HTTP level (e.g. 500 status code) without labels for TPU-specific failure modes: HBM_OOM, XLA_COMPILE_FAILURE, ICI_TIMEOUT, or BAD_CHIP_EVICTION.
- **Cost-to-Serve**: No live Prometheus metric calculates $/1k tokens by combining active TPU slice hourly rates with total token's per second.
- **Cluster Fragmentation**: llm-d does not report stranded TPU chips in GKE clusters that fail to form slice topologies.



### Proposed Solution

- **For libtpu / Device / ICI metrics**, these are already exported by the tpu-metrics-exporter component. We will need to add TPU Pod Monitor Component and create a TPU Grafana dashboard (with PromQL query) for the TPU metrics. Make sure observability documentation is up to date.
- **For Topology and TPU types**, since they already exist as node/pod labels and exported by 'kube-state-metrics', it is already scraped by llm-d's prometheus installer. We just need to define the prometheus recording rules and work it into the grafana dashboard.

### Alternatives Considered

_No response_

Yes, I can submit a PR

records.title: Cleanup: duplicated platform-parsing logic in `build-image.yaml`
records.body:
## Summary

The `detect-changes` job in `.github/workflows/build-image.yaml` defines the
`has_platform()` helper and its seven `echo "<platform>=$(has_platform …)"`
lines **twice**, once in each of two steps:

- **`platforms-input`** (~line 85) — guard: `inputs.force_build != true && inputs.platforms != ''` (the `workflow_call` path)
- **`dispatch`** (~line 151) — guard: `github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'`

Both copies are byte-identical and parse the same `inputs.platforms` value with
the same comma-delimited matching logic.

## Why it exists

- The duplication predates PR #2113; the previous `grep -q`-based blocks were
  already duplicated. PR #2113 converted both copies to the `has_platform()`
  form (which also fixed a substring bug — `xpu` matching `sglang-xpu` — and an
  interpolation/injection issue by moving to an `env:` var).
- A bash function defined in one `run:` step does **not** persist into another
  step (each `run:` is a fresh shell), so the helper cannot simply be defined
  once and reused across the two steps as-is.

## Risk of leaving it

- **Drift:** adding a new build platform requires editing both blocks; it's
  easy to update one and forget the other.
- **Redundant execution:** for a `workflow_dispatch` run with the default
  `platforms: "cuda"`, both guards are true, so both steps run and compute
  identical outputs — `platforms-input` just wins `||` precedence in the
  `detect-changes` job outputs. The `dispatch` copy is largely redundant in the
  common case.

## Proposed cleanup

**Collapse the two steps into one.** They parse the same input with the same
   logic; unify the guards and emit the outputs once. Lowest-risk, no new files.
   - Care needed: preserve the existing output-precedence semantics in the
     `detect-changes` job `outputs:` block (`steps.force || steps.platforms-input
     || steps.filter || steps.dispatch`). Verify behavior for all trigger
     paths: `force_build`, `workflow_call` with/without `platforms`, and
     `workflow_dispatch`.

## Acceptance criteria

- Define parsing block in a single place.
- All existing trigger paths produce the same `detect-changes` outputs as today
  (cuda, aws, gb200, rocm, xpu, sglang-xpu, cpu).
- No behavior change for the substring-safe matching introduced in #2113
  (e.g. `platforms: "sglang-xpu"` must NOT set `xpu=true`).

## References

- File: `.github/workflows/build-image.yaml` (job: `detect-changes`)
- Introduced/observed in: PR #2113
- Not a blocker for #2113 — tracked as a follow-up cleanup.

records.title: [RFC]: Community-Driven Infrastructure Provisioning & Conformance Strategy for llm-d
records.body:
### Feature Area

Documentation / Guides

### Problem Statement

Setting up an environment to run **llm-d** involves two distinct operational layers:

1. **Infrastructure Provisioning**: Preparing a Kubernetes cluster with hardware accelerators, high-performance networking, CRDs, etc., so it is fully ready to host `llm-d`. 
2. **Stack Installation**: Deploying `llm-d` software components, which is strictly owned and documented by canonical **well-lit path guides**.

These infrastructure requirements must align across multiple configuration dimensions, including the specific well-lit path guide, infrastructure provider, accelerator, etc..

The llm-d stack installation well-lit path guides are generally well maintained and CI-validated. However [infrastructure provisioning guides](https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d/tree/main/docs/infrastructure) are loosely maintained and lack continuous validation. Multiple infra provisioning methods have evolved in the community such as terraform or AI skills, see [Current Infrastructure Provisioning Approaches](?tab=t.0#heading=h.tjdpp5rwbkzn). 

**The dilemma**

If core `llm-d` attempts to maintain official provisioning scripts, Terraform modules, and AI skills across every cloud provider (GKE, EKS, AKS, On-Prem) and accelerator type (NVIDIA GPU, Google TPU, AMD, Intel XPU), engineering velocity on core inference features will stall. Conversely, without clear standards, third-party provisioning methods may fail silently or produce misconfigured clusters.

### Proposed Solution

To address the diverse requirements of infrastructure provisioning tooling for the stack, and a scalable maintenance structure, we propose that core `llm-d` will adopt the following strategy that clearly separates core `llm-d` vs. community contribution boundaries:



1. **llm-d **
    1. llm-d will NOT maintain tooling/guide for per-provider infra provision. This will be shifted to the (new) `llm-d-infra-providers` repo.
    2. llm-d SHOULD host the **Infra Conformance Suite** as the source of truth, contributed by each provider. 
        1. Hosting them in llm-d repo ensures a centralized discovery and consistency checking.
        2. These are executable test suites that validate if a cluster is ready to deploy llm-d.
        3.  The conformance suite is a collection of tests, each labeled with applicable dimensions (chip, rdma, dra, etc.). This allows filtering a list of required conformance tests to pass for a given dimensional space.
2. **llm-d-infra-providers (new repo)** 
     
     1.  **Ownership Model: **This is community owned. Create sub-folders for each provider, and each provider is responsible for reviewing PRs for their own sub-folder.
    4. **Existing Documentation**: Move existing [docs/infrastructure](https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d/tree/main/docs/infrastructure) to the new repo. 
    5. **Quality: **The infra provisioning tools should be qualified against the conformance test suite.
This model removes maintenance overhead from core llm-d, and motivates providers to contribute and improve their infra provisioning experience for llm-d users.





### Alternatives Considered

_No response_

### Willingness to Contribute

Yes, I can submit a PR

### Additional Context

For more details please feel free to comment on this doc: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1lBaH8YPRovsjaoJlklISrTyJPW2aczB9kaEEODroEeM/edit?pli=1&tab=t.0#heading=h.wino7477jklf

records.title: docs(optimized-baseline): helm values file variable expansion broken
records.body:
## Problem

The guide at `guides/optimized-baseline/README.md` (lines 143-152) instructs users to define helm values using variables:

```bash
export ROUTER_BASE_VALUES="-f ${REPO_ROOT}/guides/recipes/router/base.values.yaml"
export ROUTER_VALUES="-f ${REPO_ROOT}/guides/${GUIDE_NAME}/router/${GUIDE_NAME}.values.yaml"
```

Then pass them to helm:
```bash
helm install ${GUIDE_NAME}   ${ROUTER_GATEWAY_CHART}   ${ROUTER_BASE_VALUES}   ${MONITORING_VALUES}   ${ROUTER_VALUES}   ...
```

This fails with: `open /Users/.../guides/recipes/router/base.values.yaml: no such file or directory`

## Root Cause

Embedding the `-f` flag inside a shell variable and then expanding it as a positional argument doesn't work reliably with helm. The flag gets mishandled during argument expansion, particularly when there are empty variables like `${MONITORING_VALUES}=""` creating spacing issues.

## Solution

Either:
1. Store only the path in the variable (not the `-f` flag), or
2. Show users to inline the flags directly:

```bash
helm install ${GUIDE_NAME}   ${ROUTER_GATEWAY_CHART}   -f ${REPO_ROOT}/guides/recipes/router/base.values.yaml   -f ${REPO_ROOT}/guides/${GUIDE_NAME}/router/${GUIDE_NAME}.values.yaml   ...
```

## Workaround

Use inline `-f` flags instead of variables.

## Affected File

- `guides/optimized-baseline/README.md` lines 143-152 (and similar patterns in other guides)

records.title: [Incubation] llm-d Semantic Classifier (llm-d-sc)
records.body:
# Proposal: `llm-d-sc` (llm-d Semantic Classifier) as an incubation project

## Summary

`llm-d-sc` will be plug-and-play classifier runtime for inference request routing. It hosts small classifier models, serves them over HTTP and gRPC, and returns calibrated, versioned classification signals that a router or scheduler can use to select a model.

It classifies requests. It does not route them, evaluate policy, or serve inference. Those boundaries are deliberate.

## Why llm-d

llm-d already makes routing decisions, but on infrastructure state: KV cache locality, queue depth, prefill and decode placement, endpoint health. Those signals answer *which replica* should serve a request.

They cannot answer *which model* should serve it, because that depends on what the request contains. Task complexity, domain, and reasoning demand live in the request body, and nothing in llm-d reads them today.

`llm-d-sc` supplies that missing dimension. Content-based signals compose with llm-d's existing infrastructure-based ones rather than competing with them: the classifier narrows the candidate set by capability, and the scheduler picks among what survives on cache and load.

Three further reasons this belongs here rather than standing alone:

**The consumers are inference systems.** The natural callers are inference schedulers, gateways, and proxies. llm-d is where those already live.

**It should be proxy-neutral.** Multiple gateways want this signal. Hosting it inside any one proxy project couples it to that proxy. llm-d is neutral ground. (Praxis, vSR, agentgateway, etc)

**Payload processing precedent exists.** `llm-d-inference-payload-processor` established that body-aware request handling is in scope for this org. This is the classification counterpart.

## Scope

**In scope**

- Classifier runtime: preprocessing, batching, inference, calibration, abstention
- A portable classifier package format, distributed as a signed OCI artifact
- A stable classifier definition contract covering inputs, labels, signals, and output semantics
- HTTP and gRPC APIs returning full score vectors, confidence and calibration state, body coverage, and model lineage
- Reference classifiers with model cards and published benchmarks
- Telemetry and feedback schemas for evaluation and retraining

**Out of scope**

- The final routing decision
- Policy evaluation, authorization, or enforcement
- Inference serving for the models being selected
- Replacing existing training, evaluation, or model registry systems. We provide integration contracts and reference adapters instead

## Why now

Semantic routing works out of the box in roughly 80 to 85 percent of cases. That is unusable in production. At a 20 percent misroute rate, operators run a proof of concept for two weeks and abandon it, and in regulated environments a misroute is an incident rather than an inefficiency.

The gap is that off-the-shelf classifiers are not routing-aware. A general-purpose encoder measures similarity; it has never been taught what task complexity or domain means. That is a fixable problem and nobody is working it as a first-class concern.

## Evidence

A proof of concept fine-tuning the classifier for four-tier complexity classification:

| Metric | Pretrained | Fine-tuned |
|---|---:|---:|
| Accuracy | 80.39% | 98.53% |
| Macro F1 | 0.8009 | 0.9868 |
| Misroute rate | 19.61% | 1.47% |

Cost: 48 seed examples expanded to 805 by synthetic generation, a 23M-parameter encoder, CPU only, under two hours.

The useful finding was that technique mattered far more than data volume. The standard contrastive loss gained 2 points; changing the loss function and enforcing label-aware batch construction gained 18. That means this capability does not require a proprietary dataset, which is what makes it appropriate for an open project.

Pipeline and results: https://github.com/cnuland/hello-chris-sr-finetuned

## Demand

Active requirements from organizations in defence, financial services, energy, cloud service providers, and a national space agency. Two patterns recur:

- **Cost.** Route routine requests to small local models rather than paying frontier prices, without regressing quality.
- **Sovereignty.** Guarantee that sensitive workloads never reach an external provider, with an auditable record of every decision.

A third is emerging with agentic workloads, where average prompt size has grown roughly fourfold and multi-step loops multiply the cost of routing everything to the largest available model.

## First milestone

Deliberately narrow, proving the interface rather than the accuracy:

- One complexity classifier (generic, cost/compexity based)
- HTTP and gRPC endpoints against a frozen API
- CPU execution, bounded batching, full score vectors and version stamping on every response
- One reference integration
- Structured classification events

## Maintainers

- Christopher Nuland (myself, Red Hat)
- TBD

## The ask

Admission as an llm-d incubation project under the name `llm-d-sc`, with a repository, and agreement on the classifier definition and API contract as the first deliverable.

Happy to present this on a community call and to adjust scope based on where maintainers see overlap with existing components.

records.title: [SGLang] GLM-5.2
records.body:
This issue tracks the llm-d and SGLang work to add recipes for serving GLM-5.2 agentic workloads with WideEP.

The [vLLM GLM-5.2 deployment](https://llm-d.ai/blog/serving-glm-5-2-agentic-workloads-on-llm-d) can serve as a deployment reference, but the SGLang work does not target topology or feature parity.

## Goals

- [ ] Benchmark the agentic workload on the target hardware and publish the results.
- [ ] Address the main llm-d and SGLang integration issues needed by the selected WideEP deployment.
- [ ] Add an llm-d SGLang WideEP recipe

## Related integration work

These issues and PRs cover endpoint and routing work relevant to this deployment. They are not a general llm-d and SGLang roadmap.

| # | Category | Item | Issue | PR | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | DP | Support multi-node per-DP-rank endpoints | llm-d/llm-d-router#2296 | sgl-project/sglang#34430, port layout only | 🚧 WIP |
| 2 | P/D | Support SGLang `/generate` requests | — | llm-d/llm-d-router#2525 | 🚧 WIP |
| 3 | P/D | Support SGLang chat and completions requests | — | sgl-project/sglang#33812 | ⬜ TBD |
| 4 | P/D | Support P/D bootstrap on every DP rank | — | sgl-project/sglang#36234 | 🚧 WIP |
| 5 | Metrics | Expose `/metrics` from every SGLang Rust DP server | — | — | ⬜ TBD |
| 6 | KV | Track KV-cache ownership per DP rank for shared endpoints | llm-d/llm-d-router#2306 | llm-d/llm-d-router#2379, adapter propagation only | ⬜ TBD |

General SGLang WideEP guide support is tracked in [llm-d/llm-d#2040](https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d/issues/2040).

## QA

**Why can't llm-d use SGLang as it is today?**

SGLang can serve WideEP on its own. The gap appears because llm-d treats each DP rank as a separate model-server endpoint.
This requires:
- A serving IP and port for each rank.
- P/D support on every rank.
- Per-rank load metrics.
- Cache updates that identify which rank owns the data.

Without these, llm-d cannot reliably use P/D, load-aware routing, or cache-aware routing.

**Why not route all DP ranks through one SGLang frontend?**

We could, but it would require significant SGLang-specific changes in llm-d for a Python frontend that SGLang plans to deprecate in the coming months as it moves to Rust. That integration would be short-lived.

The Rust server already exposes one port per DP rank, which matches how llm-d routes today. Completing the Rust path is the smaller and longer-term solution.

## References

- [Serving GLM-5.2 for Agentic Workloads on llm-d](https://www.lmsys.org/blog/2026-07-13-glm52-optimization)
- [Serving GLM5.2 NVFP4 Agentic Workload with SGLang: Reaching 500 TPS in 2 Weeks](https://llm-d.ai/blog/serving-glm-5-2-agentic-workloads-on-llm-d)

cc @alexnails @JustinTong0323 @Kangyan-Zhou @Jiminator @wisclmy0611 @BHZ-BER @ahg-g @vMaroon @rahulgurnani @nilig @michalmalka @kfirtoledo

records.title: guides: precise prefix-cache routing on wide-EP (LWS/DP) deployments
records.body:
`precise-prefix-cache-routing` currently documents single-port model servers, and `wide-ep-lws` routes with the approximate prefix scorer. Running the precise producer on a wide-EP DP deployment is possible today but requires non-obvious glue that neither guide covers, so users asking for exact-index routing on GLM-class cells (we got this request for a DP example) have no well-lit path.

The DP-specific requirements, validated on a GLM-5.2-FP8 2-prefill + 1-decode LWS cell (DP8 per pod) across two clusters:

- Per-rank KV-event attribution in the EPP (llm-d/llm-d-router#2233) and per-rank ZMQ publisher ports compensated by the pod's start rank (llm-d/llm-d-router#2227), so all `pods x ranks` subscriptions connect.
- A multi-port target `InferencePool`, which needs GIE bundle >= v1.5.0-rc.2 (v1.0.x caps `targetPorts` at 1).
- `podCacheSize` sized to endpoints x tiers, or real holders evict and affinity silently zeroes.
- The render Service fronting the model servers per llm-d/llm-d#2188, selecting prefill pods on a P/D cell (decode port 8000 is the routing-proxy sidecar).
- Verification gates: render returns token IDs, every rank's KV-event socket subscribed, repeated-prefix requests route back to the holder.

Proposal: land this as a router variant inside `wide-ep-lws` - a `router/precise-routing.values.yaml` next to the existing `glm-5.2-overrides.values.yaml`, a README section with the prerequisites and gates above, and a cross-link from `precise-prefix-cache-routing`. That keeps the topology in its canonical guide and avoids duplicating either parent; a new top-level guide would restate both. Working branch with the validated configuration: https://github.com/nilig/llm-d/tree/guides/precise-kv-routing-wide-ep (raw manifests; would be converted to the recipes values overlay for the PR).

Wonder if the `wide-ep-lws` owners agree with that placement, or would rather see it as a topology variant under `precise-prefix-cache-routing`.

records.title: guides: pin router chart to released v0.9.0 instead of the mutable v0 tag (env.sh)
records.body:
## What / Why

[`guides/env.sh:8`](https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d/blob/main/guides/env.sh#L8) sets `ROUTER_CHART_VERSION=v0`, the **mutable rolling** chart tag. Every guide (and the workload-autoscaling nightly) inherits this single source of truth, so they all install bleeding-edge chart and pick up regressions the moment they merge upstream before any release, with no way to pin or reproduce.

This just bit us. [llm-d-router#1681](https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d-router/pull/1681) (merged 2026-08-06) shipped straight into `v0` and broke `llm-d-router-standalone`: the EPP `-epp` Service is never created when `flowControl`/`monitoring` are enabled (`helm template` renders it and `helm install` reports `deployed`, but it never appears at runtime). That makes EPP metrics unscrapeable and breaks the queue-based KEDA+EPP autoscaling guide and its new nightly. The same #1681 also caused the EPP `--config-file` CrashLoop (fixed by [llm-d-router#2322](https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d-router/pull/2322)) and overlaps with the shell-var expansion fix in #2177. The underlying chart bug is tracked upstream as [llm-d-router#2323](https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d-router/issues/2323).

## Evidence - the released artifact is fine, only the rolling tag is broken

Identical standalone install (base + optimized-baseline + monitoring + flowControl values):

| chart version | EPP `-epp` Service | pod |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `v0` (rolling) | **not created** | Ready 2/2, `deployed` |
| `v0.9.0` (release) | **created** | Ready 2/2, `deployed` |

`git compare v0.9.0...main` confirms #1681 is not in `v0.9.0`.

## Proposal

Pin to the latest released chart in `guides/env.sh`, and bump deliberately on each router release:

```diff
-export ROUTER_CHART_VERSION=v0
+export ROUTER_CHART_VERSION=v0.9.0
```

This makes guide walkthroughs and CI reproducible instead of silently tracking `main`, and aligns standalone with how the `llm-d-router-gateway` path is already pinned to `v0.9.0`.

## Safety check (no guide depends on an unreleased feature)

Verified before proposing repo-wide: only two values keys were added on `main` since `v0.9.0` `additional_addresses` (standalone) and `podAnnotations` (routerlib) and **no guide sets either**. The chart features guides actually rely on (`featureGates: [flowControl]`, monitoring) are present and working in `v0.9.0`.

/kind bug

records.title: [Feature]: Cut vLLM startup time in the optimized baseline (model cache PVC + streamed weight load + persistent compile cache)
records.body:
**Feature Area:** Optimized baseline

## Problem Statement

A vLLM replica cannot serve until it has fetched its weights, loaded them, and compiled its graphs. The optimized baseline pays full price for all three on every pod start: no `HF_HOME` or PVC, so each pod re-downloads the model from HuggingFace; no `--load-format`, so shards then load sequentially; and `/.cache` / `/.triton` are `emptyDir` ([patch-vllm.yaml#L73-L78](https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d/blob/main/guides/optimized-baseline/modelserver/gpu/vllm/base/patch-vllm.yaml#L73-L78)), so compile artifacts are thrown away. Together they dominate scale-up latency and rollout time.

## Proposed Solution

Three additions to the NVIDIA GPU vLLM manifests.

**1. Persist the model itself.** The guide currently has no model cache PVC, so weights are pulled from HuggingFace on every pod start. `guides/recipes/modelserver/components/model-cache` already provides this (RWX PVC, `HF_HOME=/model-cache`) but is only wired into the AMD CI overlay. Include it in the GPU overlay so the model downloads once and every later pod skips the download.

**2. Stream the weights.**

```yaml
- "--load-format=runai_streamer"
```

No image, env, or volume change: `runai-model-streamer` is already in the `vllm/vllm-openai` image, and the loader takes an HF model id or a local path.

**3. Persist the compile / CUDA graph cache** by pointing `VLLM_CACHE_ROOT` at a volume that outlives the pod:

```yaml
env:
  - name: VLLM_CACHE_ROOT
    value: /vllm-cache
volumeMounts:
  - { name: vllm-cache, mountPath: /vllm-cache }
volumes:
  - name: vllm-cache
    hostPath: { path: /var/tmp/vllm-compile-cache, type: DirectoryOrCreate }
```

The cache key includes the model config, so any flag change forces a fresh compile. No stale graphs.

These compound: (1) removes the download, (2) speeds up the load that follows it, (3) removes the recompile.

### Measurements

fp8 model, weights already on shared storage, pod start to ready:

| Configuration | Startup | Saved |
| --- | --- | --- |
| baseline | 22 min 13 s | - |
| `--load-format=runai_streamer` | 14 min 11 s | 8 min 02 s |
| streamer + persisted `VLLM_CACHE_ROOT` | 12 min 34 s | 9 min 39 s |

Weight load is 1.68x, bounded by storage bandwidth, not the client. Compile phase is 137 s to 36 s on a cache hit. Both scale with model size and shrink on local NVMe.

### Scope and open questions

- NVIDIA GPU vLLM only. Other accelerators use vendor images that may not carry the streamer.
- The model cache PVC needs an RWX default StorageClass, which is why the component is opt-in today. If that is too strong a requirement for the default guide, it can ship commented out with a note.
- For the compile cache, `hostPath` is what I measured, but it only hits on a node that already compiled that config and some clusters disallow it. An RWX PVC hits anywhere but has replicas writing concurrently on a cold cache, untested. Preference welcome.

## Alternatives Considered

Leaving these to users, or exposing them as tunables. None has a request-path effect or a measured downside on safetensors models, so defaults beat knobs. Users on custom images or non-safetensors checkpoints drop the arg.

## Additional Context

[vLLM Run:ai Model Streamer docs](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/stable/models/extensions/runai_model_streamer/). Prior art: [llm-d-deployer#317](https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d-deployer/issues/317), never landed, repo archived since July 2025.

records.title: CUDA image build fails: sccache fallback in setup-sccache.sh does not disable USE_SCCACHE
records.body:
When `setup-sccache.sh` cannot start sccache it degrades gracefully, but the degrade path is incomplete and every CUDA image build fails at the gdrcopy step.

### What happens

`docker/scripts/common/setup-sccache.sh` deletes the sccache binary and unsets the CMake launcher variables, then returns success:

```bash
if ! /usr/local/bin/sccache --start-server; then
    echo "Warning: sccache failed to start, continuing without cache" >&2
    rm -f /usr/local/bin/sccache || true
    unset CMAKE_C_COMPILER_LAUNCHER CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER_LAUNCHER CMAKE_CUDA_COMPILER_LAUNCHER
    return 0
fi
```

It does not clear `USE_SCCACHE`. Every consumer sources the script and then branches on that original input variable, so they still believe sccache is available:

```bash
. /usr/local/bin/setup-sccache
...
if [ "${USE_SCCACHE}" = "true" ]; then
    export CC="sccache gcc" CXX="sccache g++"   # binary was just deleted
fi
```

gdrcopy builds with a plain Makefile rather than CMake, so unsetting the `CMAKE_*_COMPILER_LAUNCHER` variables has no effect on it, and the hardcoded `sccache` in `CC` is what actually breaks:

```
/usr/local/bin/setup-sccache: line 36: /usr/local/bin/sccache: No such file or directory
Warning: sccache failed to start, continuing without cache
+ export CC='sccache gcc' CXX='sccache g++'
sccache gcc -O2 -fPIC -I ../include -I gdrdrv/ -D GDRAPI_ARCH=ARM64 -c -o gdrapi.o gdrapi.c
make[1]: sccache: No such file or directory
make[1]: *** [<builtin>: gdrapi.o] Error 127
make: *** [Makefile:63: lib] Error 2
```

### Impact

All CUDA-family jobs fail identically at `Dockerfile.cuda` (`build-gdrcopy.sh`), on both architectures and both base OSes:

- `cuda-build-llm-d (linux/amd64, rhel, ubi9)`
- `cuda-build-llm-d (linux/amd64, ubuntu, ubuntu24.04)`
- `cuda-build-llm-d (linux/arm64, rhel, ubi9)`
- `cuda-build-llm-d (linux/arm64, ubuntu, ubuntu24.04)`
- `cuda-build-llm-d-debug (linux/amd64, rhel, ubi9)`
- `gb200-build-llm-d`
- `aws-build-llm-d (linux/amd64, rhel, ubi9)`

Example run: https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d/actions/runs/31362149292

Two more scripts carry the same latent bug and would fail the same way if the build got that far:

- `docker/scripts/cuda/builder/build-ucx.sh:29` — `export CC="sccache gcc" CXX="sccache g++"`
- `docker/scripts/cuda/builder/build-nixl.sh:32` — `export CC="sccache gcc" CXX="sccache g++" NVCC="sccache nvcc"`

And four scripts call bare `sccache --show-stats` after the binary has been removed, which aborts under `set -e`:

- `build-gdrcopy.sh:61`, `build-ucx.sh:62`, `build-lmcache.sh:88`, `build-compiled-wheels.sh:106`

### Why it surfaced now

`detect-changes` lists `docker/common-versions` as a trigger for every platform. PRs that only touch a single platform Dockerfile skip the CUDA jobs entirely, so the bug stays hidden; any PR that edits the shared `common-versions` file turns all platform builds on and hits it immediately.

### Suggested fix

Clear `USE_SCCACHE` in both degrade branches of `setup-sccache.sh`. The script is sourced, so a single change propagates to all consumers, and `build-nvshmem.sh:32` already uses `export USE_SCCACHE="false"` for the same purpose.
records.author: yuanwu2017

records.title: sccache S3 credentials are invalid: every CUDA image build runs with no cache
records.body:
### Summary

The AWS credentials used for the sccache S3 backend are rejected by S3, so **every** CUDA image build compiles from scratch with no cache. This is not intermittent — the credentials are unconditionally invalid, so the fallback path in `docker/scripts/common/setup-sccache.sh` is taken on every run.

### Evidence

Every CUDA builder job logs this while starting the sccache server:

```
sccache: error: Server startup failed: cache storage failed to read:
  PermissionDenied (permanent) at read => S3Error {
    code: "InvalidAccessKeyId",
    message: "The AWS Access Key Id you provided does not exist in our records." }

Context:
   uri: https://s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/vllm-nightly-sccache/llm-d-cache/.sccache_check
   response: Parts { status: 403, ... }
```

Observed in every CUDA job I have looked at, across different days and different PRs:

| run | job | platform |
|---|---|---|
| [31362149292](https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d/actions/runs/31362149292) | 93373145809 | linux/amd64, ubuntu |
| [31364574234](https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d/actions/runs/31364574234) | 93380605080 | linux/amd64, ubuntu |
| [31369626636](https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d/actions/runs/31369626636) | 93395676034 | linux/amd64, rhel/ubi9 |

The secret is present and non-empty — buildx mounts it and the log shows `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=***`, and `[ -f /run/secrets/aws_access_key_id ]` passes. S3 returns `InvalidAccessKeyId`, which means the key ID itself no longer exists in IAM, i.e. it was deleted or rotated rather than merely lacking permissions (that would be `AccessDenied`).

`build-image.yaml` passes these at lines 270, 424, 798 and 1115:

```yaml
secrets: |
  aws_access_key_id=${{ secrets.AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID_S3_BUCKET_ONLY }}
  aws_secret_access_key=${{ secrets.AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY_S3_BUCKET_ONLY }}
```

Both of those repository secrets were created on 2025-08-10 and have never been updated since:

```
AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID_S3_BUCKET_ONLY      created 2025-08-10  updated 2025-08-10
AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY_S3_BUCKET_ONLY  created 2025-08-10  updated 2025-08-10
```

### Impact

The builder stage compiles UCX, NIXL, NVSHMEM, gdrcopy, LMCache and the DeepGEMM/CUTLASS wheels with zero cache hits. In run 31364574234 that stage took **28 minutes** (07:10:15 → 07:38:36) for a single platform/OS combination, and the matrix runs several of them per PR.

Nobody notices the breakage because `setup-sccache.sh` degrades silently: it prints one `Warning: sccache failed to start, continuing without cache` line and returns success. The build still produces a correct image, just slowly.

This also hid a real bug — the degrade path leaves the build in an inconsistent state and breaks the CUDA builds outright once it is exercised. That is #2223, fixed in #2224. The two are independent: #2224 makes the fallback correct, this issue is about not needing the fallback in the first place.

### Notes for whoever picks this up

The bucket is `vllm-nightly-sccache` with key prefix `llm-d-cache/` — that is vLLM's bucket, not llm-d's. So llm-d's build cache depends on credentials issued by another project, and a rotation on their side silently degrades llm-d's CI with no notification. Worth considering whether llm-d should own its own bucket, or at least document who to contact when the key expires.

Two things that would make this self-reporting rather than silent:

1. Have the workflow surface a warning annotation (`::warning::`) when sccache is unavailable, so it shows up in the run summary instead of being buried in build output.
2. Optionally fail the build when sccache is expected but unreachable on protected branches, while still degrading gracefully on PRs from forks (which legitimately have no access to the secrets).

I am happy to send a PR for the annotation part if that is wanted; the credential rotation itself needs someone with access to the AWS account and the repository secrets.

records.title: Add nightly performance benchmark for guides/multimodal-serving
records.body:
As llmd continues to evolve, it is critical that we monitor the performance of our core use cases to catch any potential regressions early.

Currently we don't have a nightly benchmark running against the multimodal-serving guide (guides/multimodal-serving). We need to implement a dedicated nightly benchmark for this specific guide to ensure our multimodal capabilities remain performant.

Goal:
Set up an automated nightly benchmark for the multimodal-serving guide to track performance metrics over time and alert the team to any performance degradation.

Acceptance Criteria:

[ ] Verify the current status of nightly benchmarks for existing multimodal serving guides.

[ ] Create a benchmark test suite specifically for the guides/multimodal-serving implementation.

[ ] Integrate the benchmark into the nightly CI/CD pipeline.

[ ] Ensure benchmark results are logged and any significant performance degradation triggers an alert.

records.author: clubanderson

records.title: [Guides] Model-centric guide entry points
records.body:
## Problem

Guides are organized by capability (optimized-baseline, pd-disaggregation, tiered-prefix-cache, wide-ep-lws, agentic-serving, etc.). Model-specific configuration is scattered across these directories. A user who wants to deploy GLM-5.2 has to find content across `agentic-serving/`, `wide-ep-lws/modelserver/gpu/vllm-glm-5.2/`, and potentially `tiered-prefix-cache/`. The same applies to Qwen3-32B (optimized-baseline, precise-prefix-cache-routing, tiered-prefix-cache) and DeepSeek-V4 (wide-ep-lws, pd-disaggregation).

There is no single place that answers "I want to deploy model X — what are my options?"

## Models currently in guides

| Model | Guides with model-specific config |
|---|---|
| GLM-5.2 | agentic-serving, wide-ep-lws |
| Nemotron-3-Ultra-550B | agentic-serving |
| Qwen3-Coder-480B | agentic-serving (TPU) |
| Qwen3-32B | optimized-baseline, precise-prefix-cache-routing, tiered-prefix-cache |
| Qwen3-VL | multimodal-serving (TPU) |
| DeepSeek-V4 | wide-ep-lws |
| GPT-OSS-120B | optimized-baseline, tiered-prefix-cache |
| Gemma4 | multimodal-serving (TPU) |

Targets in flight: Kimi K3, ...

## Proposal

1. **Per-model landing pages** under `guides/models/<model>/README.md`. Each page describes the model's characteristics relevant to serving (parameter count, attention type, MoE, context length), lists the applicable well-lit paths with links, and provides a recommended starting point per accelerator.

2. **Do not restructure the capability directories.** The existing `optimized-baseline/`, `agentic-serving/`, etc. structure works well for users who start from a capability. Model pages link into them.

3. **Connect to the website's faceted navigation** ([llm-d.github.io#380](https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d.github.io/issues/380)) so the docs site can surface model as a first-class navigation dimension alongside accelerator and engine.

4. **Build on the recipes component pattern** already emerging in `guides/recipes/` (e.g., model-cache PVC component from #2153). Per-model Kustomize overlays remain in their capability directories; the model page is a navigation layer, not a code reorganization.

## Action items

- [ ] Create `guides/models/` directory with a README explaining the pattern
- [ ] Write the first model page (GLM-5.2 is the natural candidate — most content exists)
- [ ] Add model pages
- [ ] Coordinate with llm-d.github.io#380 for website integration
- [ ] Define a template so new model guides follow a consistent structure

## Related

- [llm-d.github.io#380](https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d.github.io/issues/380) — Bring how-to guides into docs site with faceted navigation
- [llm-d.github.io#453](https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d.github.io/pull/453) — First slice of syncing guides to the docs site
- [#2140](https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d/issues/2140) — Improve readability of optimized-baseline guide

records.title: saturation autoscaling guide: EPP flow control never enabled (kubectl apply fails)
records.body:
The experimental saturation-based autoscaling guide (`guides/workload-autoscaling/README.epp-keda-saturation.md`) cannot enable EPP flow control, so `llm_d_epp_flow_control_pool_saturation` is never emitted and the guide is non-functional.

`kubectl apply -k .../keda-epp-saturation/ocp` fails:

```
no matches for kind "EndpointPickerConfig" in version "router.llm-d.ai/v1beta1"
```

**Fix direction:** enable the `flowControl` feature gate through the router (reusing the optimized-baseline EPP plugins) instead of applying a config document - enabling the gate loads default flow-control policies, and `pool_saturation` emits once the pool has a ready endpoint. 

/kind bug

records.title: refactor(single-host): make routing-proxy sidecar args patchable across kustomize layers
records.body:
## Background

During the image component restructure (#2266 / follow-up-kustomize-dry-run-fixes branch), we refactored \`single-host/pd\` and \`single-host/e-pd\` to be engine-agnostic. The intent was to have guide overlays own their engine-specific sidecar args (e.g. \`--kv-connector=nixlv2\` for vLLM, \`--kv-connector=sglang\` for SGLang), with the base only defining port, log level, and security config.

## Problem

Kustomize does not preserve list fields (including \`args:\`) that are set via strategic merge patches in the rendered output. This means a guide overlay cannot patch \`args\` on the routing-proxy init container if those args were introduced by a patch in the base layer — the field simply doesn't exist in the rendered YAML the guide builds on top of.

We confirmed this is a fundamental kustomize constraint: list fields added via strategic merge patches are stripped from rendered output and are not available for child layers to override.

## Current workaround

The \`--kv-connector\` default (\`nixlv2\`) is included directly in \`pd/patch-sidecar.yaml\`. Guides that use a different connector (sglang, mooncake, moriio) override the full args list in their own patch. This works but violates the separation of concerns goal — the base defaults to a specific KV provider.

## Proposed fix

Redefine the routing-proxy init container as part of the actual resource files in the single-host bases rather than via a strategic merge patch. Specifically:

- Create a PD-specific decode resource file (separate from \`single-host/default/decode-deployment.yaml\`) that includes the routing-proxy init container stub with \`args: []\`
- This gives the field a presence in the rendered output that guide overlays can patch onto
- \`single-host/pd\` would reference this new decode resource instead of \`../default\`

This requires duplicating ~1-2 manifest files but cleanly separates the PD architecture definition from engine-specific connector configuration.

## Acceptance criteria

- \`single-host/pd/patch-sidecar.yaml\` contains only port, log level, security config — no \`--kv-connector\`
- \`single-host/e-pd/patch-sidecar.yaml\` contains only port, log level, security config — no \`--ec-connector\`
- Each guide overlay that uses pd/e-pd sets its own complete args list for the routing-proxy
- All existing guide kustomize builds continue to pass

records.title: Cut workload-autoscaling nightlies onto the guide.yaml harness (fold deploy scripts + retire e2e-openshift)
records.body:
**What type of issue:**

/kind feature
/kind cleanup

## Summary

The workload-autoscaling `guide.yaml` migration is complete on the authoring side - every guide now ships a `guide.yaml` (restructure #2264, shared KEDA auth recipe #2265, keda-epp twins #2273, wva #2274, slo-aware + multi-inference-pool + scale-event verify #2278). This issue tracks the **final phase**: making the nightlies run *from* those `guide.yaml`s and deleting the duplicated deploy/validation scripts.

Next step is to do PR 4 and PR 5 together, since PR 4's payoff (guide.yaml as the single source of deploy truth) is only realized once the nightlies actually run via the guide.yaml harness in PR 5.

## Blocked on

1. **llmdbenchmark parsing `guide.yaml`.** The agreement is that llmdbenchmark parses `guide.yaml` (it currently scrapes `README.md`). This work is owned by @Vezio per discussion. Nothing here can land until it exists.
2. **A replacement reusable nightly workflow** that invokes the guide.yaml harness (to replace `reusable-nightly-e2e-openshift.yaml`, which in discussion needs to be retired eventually. @maugustosilva @lionelvillard).

## Scope

**Fold the deploy scripts into `deploy:` (was "PR 4")**
- [ ] Move the deploy logic in `nightly-deploy-ocp-keda-epp.sh`, `nightly-deploy-ocp.sh`, `nightly-deploy-cks.sh` into the guides' `guide.yaml` `deploy:` phases (some deploy-time logic - the `${NS_HASH}` ClusterRoleBinding uniquification, PromQL/namespace patching the transformer can't reach, WVA namespace set - needs to become explicit `deploy:` steps, not static overlays).

records.title: guides: add a well-lit P/D Multi Tier KV cache path
records.body:
P/D Multi Tier works by composing `NixlConnector` and
`OffloadingConnector` through `MultiConnector`: NIXL remains the P/D
transport, while CPU memory extends reusable prefix capacity beyond HBM.

The configuration is functional but still experimental. Users currently need
to determine several non-obvious requirements themselves, so we need one
well-lit path under `guides/pd-disaggregation`.

Scope:

- Add an experimental P/D Multi Tier guide and deployment overlays.
- Keep plain PD NIXL as the baseline.
- Add CPU Multi Tier without a filesystem tier.
- Document CPU capacity as a per-connector budget, including multiplication by
  local DP size.
- Document precise-router CPU backend indexing and matching engine/router block
  sizes.
- Include DP as a supported topology flavor, including per-rank ZMQ binding and
  subscriber validation. The precise DP routing work is tracked by #2201.
- Require mechanism evidence from CPU-to-GPU byte counters; CPU allocation or
  GPU-to-CPU writes alone do not demonstrate useful reuse.
- Include controlled PD NIXL versus PD Multi Tier benchmarks.

Exit criteria:

- The guide deploys plain PD NIXL and CPU Multi Tier from checked-in overlays.
- CPU sizing and DP-specific multiplication are explicit.
- Verification covers ZMQ subscribers, NIXL failures, CPU writes, and CPU
  restores.
- The benchmark keeps router policy, topology, model, and workload identical
  between arms.
- Cleanup instructions remove all deployed resources.
- The feature remains marked experimental until repeated benchmarks and
  additional topology coverage justify promotion.

records.title: The agentgateway router install still carries `monitoring.values.yaml`, so it still fails without the Prometheus Operator
records.body:
# The agentgateway router install still carries `monitoring.values.yaml`, so it still fails without the Prometheus Operator

Follow-up to [#2134](https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d/issues/2134), which
[PR #2138](https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d/pull/2138) (`709a67e2`) closed. That fix is
correct as far as it goes but covered two of the three install commands in
`guides/recipes/router/README.md`. The third still reproduces the original failure.

Verified against `main` at `772fef82` (2026-08-19).

## What is left

`guides/recipes/router/README.md:44-56`, **Standalone with agentgateway**:

```bash
helm install <release-name> \
  ${ROUTER_STANDALONE_CHART} \
  -f ${REPO_ROOT}/guides/recipes/router/base.values.yaml \
  -f ${REPO_ROOT}/guides/recipes/router/features/monitoring.values.yaml \   # <-- line 47
  -f ${REPO_ROOT}/guides/recipes/router/features/agentgateway-proxy.values.yaml \
  -f ${REPO_ROOT}/guides/<your-guide>/router/<your-guide>.values.yaml \
  --set router.proxy.proxyType=agentgateway \
  --set router.inferencePool.create=false \
  --set router.epp.flags.secure-serving=false \
  -n ${NAMESPACE} \
  --version ${ROUTER_CHART_VERSION}
```

`709a67e2` removed that `-f` from the *Standalone with Envoy* block (line 27 pre-patch)
and from the *With Kubernetes Gateway API* block (line 72 pre-patch), and left this one.
It is a miss, not a later regression — the block already carried the flag at `709a67e2^`,
added by [#1719](https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d/pull/1719).

## Why it still fails

Nothing in the agentgateway path suppresses the `ServiceMonitor`.
`features/agentgateway-proxy.values.yaml` only overrides `router.proxy.args`;
`features/monitoring.values.yaml` still sets `router.monitoring.prometheus.enabled: true`.

Rendering the documented command against the published chart confirms it:

```
$ helm template test oci://ghcr.io/llm-d/charts/llm-d-router-standalone --version v0 \
    -f base.values.yaml -f monitoring.values.yaml -f agentgateway-proxy.values.yaml \
    --set router.proxy.proxyType=agentgateway \
    --set router.inferencePool.create=false \
    --set router.epp.flags.secure-serving=false \
    --set router.modelServers.matchLabels.app=demo \
    -n testns | grep -E '^kind:|^apiVersion: monitoring'

apiVersion: monitoring.coreos.com/v1
kind: ServiceMonitor
...
```

So on a cluster without the Prometheus Operator CRDs, `helm install` aborts the same way
#2134 described:

```
Error: unable to build kubernetes objects from release manifest: resource mapping not found
for name: "<release>-epp-monitor" namespace: "<ns>" from "":
no matches for kind "ServiceMonitor" in version "monitoring.coreos.com/v1"
ensure CRDs are installed first
```

The README's own "Enable Prometheus Monitoring (Optional)" section (added by #2138) already
states this dependency — it just isn't reflected in this one command.

## Fix

Delete line 47. The optional section below already covers how to add monitoring afterwards,
and its closing note ("If your cluster already has the Prometheus Operator CRDs installed,
you can also add `-f ...monitoring.values.yaml` to the initial `helm install` command above
instead") applies unchanged.

## Separate, found while rendering the above

That same documented command cannot be templated at all as written:

```
Error: execution error at (llm-d-router-standalone/templates/epp.yaml:2:3):
.Values.router.modelServers.matchLabels is required when
.Values.router.inferencePool.create=false: standalone mode renders the EPP
--endpoint-selector from matchLabels and cannot start with an empty selector
```

`router.inferencePool.create=false` is required for agentgateway (the README's own `NOTE`
block says so), and the chart then requires `router.modelServers.matchLabels`, which
neither the command nor the surrounding text mentions. Presumably it is expected to come
from `<your-guide>.values.yaml`, but that is not stated, and the placeholder guide values
give a reader nothing to infer it from. Worth either setting it in the example or naming
the requirement in the `NOTE`. Happy to split this into its own issue if preferred.

records.title: Pub/Sub quickstart payload carries the Redis InternalRequest envelope, so it decodes to an empty, already-expired request
records.body:
[PR #2133](https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d/pull/2133) (`28ce029c`) fixed the Redis quickstart
payload in `guides/batch-serving/asynchronous-processing/` by wrapping it in the
`InternalRequest` envelope. That fix is correct. The same commit applied the identical change
to the **Pub/Sub** guide, where the consumer does not want an envelope.

Verified against `main` at `b2cb19c8`, with `llm-d-async` at `804a8a3` (2026-08-19).

## Where

`guides/batch-serving/asynchronous-processing/gcp-pubsub/README.md`, *Testing* → *Publish a message*:

```bash
gcloud pubsub topics publish $REQUEST_TOPIC_NAME --message='{"request_kind":"pubsub","internal":{},"data":{"id":"testmsg","created":1700000000,"deadline":1999999999,"payload":{"model":"your-model","prompt":"Hi, good morning"}}}'
```

## Why it is wrong

The Pub/Sub consumer decodes the message body as a bare `api.RequestMessage` and builds the
`InternalRequest` itself, from `msg.ID` and the subscriber ID — `llm-d-async`
`pkg/pubsub/pubsubimpl.go`:

```go
var body api.RequestMessage
err := json.Unmarshal(msg.Data, &body)
...
irout := api.InternalRouting{TransportCorrelationID: msg.ID, RequestQueueName: subscriberID}
...
ir := api.NewInternalRequest(irout, &body)
```

There is no envelope-unwrapping step on this path (unlike the Redis path, which goes through
`InternalRequest.UnmarshalJSON` and rejects a body with no `request_kind`). So `request_kind`,
`internal` and `data` are just unknown fields, `encoding/json` ignores unknown fields by
default, and the decode **succeeds** — producing a zero-valued request. Every real field is
nested one level down under `data`, where nothing reads it.

Decoding each payload exactly as `processMessages` does:

| payload | result |
|---|---|
| before #2133 (`"deadline":"1999999999"`) | **loud failure** — `json: cannot unmarshal string into Go struct field RequestMessage.deadline of type int64` |
| current, enveloped | **silent failure** — `id="" created=0 deadline=0 payload=map[]` |
| bare, numeric `deadline` | OK — `id="testmsg" deadline=1999999999` |

So this command was broken before #2133 too, but the failure mode regressed from an error the
reader sees to a request that is accepted and is already expired (`deadline=0` is 1970).
`gcloud pubsub topics publish` reports success either way, so the guide now looks like it works.

The prose #2133 added above the command is also wrong on this page — it describes the Redis
contract:

> Requests are consumed as an `InternalRequest` envelope: a `request_kind` tag (`pubsub` for
> Pub/Sub) wrapping the caller-visible request under `data`.

Only the second half of that paragraph (numeric `created`/`deadline`, not strings) applies to
Pub/Sub.

## Suggested fix

Revert the payload to the bare numeric form — which this repo's own multitenant guide already
uses at `guides/batch-serving/asynchronous-processing/multitenant/README.md`:

```bash
gcloud pubsub topics publish $REQUEST_TOPIC_NAME --message='{"id":"testmsg","created":1700000000,"deadline":1999999999,"payload":{"model":"your-model","prompt":"Hi, good morning"}}'
```

and reword the paragraph above it to state the Pub/Sub contract: no envelope, the transport
correlation and queue name come from the Pub/Sub message itself, and `created`/`deadline` are
Unix-seconds numbers.

## Why it was not caught

Neither Pub/Sub publish example is exercised by CI. The multitenant one is inside a
`<!-- llm-d-cicd:skip -->` block, and this one needs a real GCP project. The Redis payload,
which is covered, is the one that got fixed correctly.

records.title: [Feature]: Gate guide README rendering in CI with guide.py render --check
records.body:
### Feature Area

CI/CD

### Problem Statement

Guide READMEs are rendered from `guide.yaml` between `<!-- guide:... -->` markers, but no CI job checks that the two files agree. Hand edits inside rendered blocks survive review and are lost on the next render, and stale renders ship broken commands.

Recent examples:

- #2243 re-rendered optimized-baseline and reverted the fix merged in #2177, reintroducing the broken `-f`-in-variable helm pattern tracked in #2176.
- #2260 hand-edited two rendered blocks in the same guide (`PROVIDER_NAME`, `ROUTER_CHART_VERSION`); the next render would have discarded both edits.


### Proposed Solution

Run `scripts/guide.py render --check <dir>` in PR CI for every directory containing a `guide.yaml`, failing the build when a README is stale or a rendered block was hand-edited. #2044 extracts guide rendering into `scripts/render.sh` and may be the right vehicle. `guide.py` declares its pyyaml dependency for `uv run`, so the CI job needs `uv` or an equivalent environment.

### Alternatives Considered

A CI job that re-renders and commits the result instead of failing. Rejected: silent rewrites are the failure mode already observed; #2260's hand edits carried intent (`PROVIDER_NAME=none`) that a machine rewrite would have discarded without anyone deciding.

A pre-commit hook. Insufficient alone: #2243 was a well-formed render whose source was stale, and hooks are opt-in on contributor machines.

### Willingness to Contribute

Yes, with guidance

### Additional Context

Related to #2176, #2177, #2243, #2260, #2044.

records.title: [Bug :bug:]: CRD install URLs break when release versions default to latest
records.body:
### Contact Details

lukevandrie@google.com

### What happened?

PR #2299 added computed URL variables (`GATEWAY_API_URL`, `GAIE_URL`, `ROUTER_RELEASE_URL`) to `guides/env.sh` because GitHub serves release assets at `releases/latest/download/<asset>` for the floating latest release and at `releases/download/<tag>/<asset>` for pinned tags. Several files still build release URLs from the `*_VERSION` variables directly. With the current defaults (`latest`), those URLs return 404.

The flow-control nightly hit the same defect and is fixed separately in #2341. Remaining sites, each confirmed against the `latest` default:

1. `guides/wide-ep-lws/README.precise-prefix-cache-routing.md` line 54 applies `releases/download/${GAIE_VERSION}/v1-manifests.yaml`. A user following the guide with defaults fails on the first CRD install step. The fix is the switch to `${GAIE_URL}`.
2. `guides/recipes/gateway/install-gateway-crds.sh` lines 42 and 48 fall back to `${GATEWAY_API_VERSION:-"v1.5.1"}`, but a shell that has sourced `guides/env.sh` carries `GATEWAY_API_VERSION=latest`, producing the broken URL. The `|| true` on the apply suppresses the 404 and the script prints a success message, so users discover the missing CRDs later as "no matches for kind Gateway" errors. The `|| true` should be removed independently of the URL fix.
3. `guides/coord-disaggregation/README.md` line 123 and `guides/multimodal-serving/e-disaggregation/README.md` line 118 run `kubectl apply -k .../config/crd?ref=${GAIE_VERSION}`, which resolves to `?ref=latest`. The GAIE repo has no `latest` git ref (checked with `git ls-remote`). `GAIE_URL` holds a release download path and cannot serve as a kustomize `ref`, so these sites need a pinned tag or a different install mechanism.
4. `guides/env.sh` recomputes `GATEWAY_API_URL`, `GAIE_URL`, and `ROUTER_RELEASE_URL` unconditionally on every source. A `*_URL` value exported beforehand is silently discarded; only `*_VERSION` overrides take effect. Either guard the URL variables or document that `*_VERSION` is the only supported override.

Expected behavior: every CRD install command in the guides works with the default environment produced by `source guides/env.sh`, and failures are not suppressed.

No CI covers sites 1 through 3, so the breakage surfaces only for users following the guides.

### Version

main (after the v0.9.0 release cut; versions default to `latest`)

### Relevant log output

```shell
error: unable to read URL "https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api-inference-extension/releases/download/latest/v1-manifests.yaml", server reported 404 Not Found, status code=404
```

records.title: [Feature]: Migrate flow-control guide + nightly to the guide.yaml method
records.body:
### Feature Area

CI/CD

### Problem Statement

The flow-control guide runs its nightly on a bespoke lane. `nightly-e2e-flow-control-gke-acc-gpu-vllm-x.yaml` calls `reusable-nightly-e2e-gke.yaml` (llm-d-infra) with `custom_deploy_script: guides/flow-control/scripts/nightly-deploy-gke.sh` and a bespoke validate script at `.github/scripts/e2e/e2e-validate-flow-control.sh`.

There is no `guides/flow-control/guide.yaml`, so `scripts/guide.py` neither renders nor checks the README, and the deploy commands are maintained in three places: the README, the deploy script, and the validate script. These drift. Nightly run #76 (2026-08-20) failed with a 404 on the GAIE CRD manifest because #2299 fixed the CRD URLs in `guides/env.sh` and the README while the deploy script, restored in #1918 before #2299 merged, kept the old hand-built URL.

### Proposed Solution

Adopt the guide.yaml method used by optimized-baseline and fast-model-actuation, in two phases.

**Phase 1 (llm-d repo only): guide.yaml as the single source of truth**

- Author `guides/flow-control/guide.yaml` and re-render the README from it with `scripts/guide.py render`.
- Rewrite `nightly-deploy-gke.sh` to consume the guide-defined commands, so a fix to the guide reaches the nightly without a second edit.
- Hardening that can ride along: pin `GAIE_VERSION` and `ROUTER_RELEASE_VERSION` in the workflow env or log the resolved releases before applying, and add retries to the CRD fetches. Both address nightly failures that have no llm-d commit in the blame window.
- Optionally wire `scripts/guide.py render --check` into CI. `guides/templates/README.md` recommends it and no workflow runs it today.

**Phase 2 (cross-repo): move the nightly to the standardized lane**

The workflow header documents the constraints the bespoke lane exists to satisfy. Phase 2 must resolve each of them:

1. Model detection. The harness's kustomize standup detects the model from `guides/<scenario>/modelserver/<accel>/<backend>/<infra>/`. flow-control keeps no modelserver overlay and borrows optimized-baseline's via `kubectl kustomize | sed`. The flow-control special case in `reusable-ci-nightly-benchmark.yaml` (llm-d-infra) runs after the detection step and never executes. The ordering or the detection fallback needs to change.
2. Variable resolution. llm-d-benchmark's `GuideVariableResolver` does not define `GAIE_URL` or `ROUTER_RELEASE_URL`, and its README parser drops `source guides/env.sh` lines. The guide's CRD install commands do not resolve on that path. Either the resolver learns those variables or the guide exports them in a form the parser harvests.
3. CI-only settings. The nightly overrides `maxConcurrency` from 132 to 4, forces one decode replica, and disables EPP metrics auth so the validate script can scrape `/metrics`. These map to `guideVariableOverrides`, scenario `patches:`, and `extraHelmSets` in llm-d-benchmark's `config/scenarios/guides/flow-control.yaml`. That file exists with `kustomize.enabled: false` and still carries optimized-baseline content.
4. Saturation-driven validation. Flow control is work-conserving and the standard smoke loop never queues, so it exercises none of the feature's behavior. The per-band backpressure and QoS assertions must survive the migration, either as `--extra-validate` or as a harness workload that reliably saturates.

### Alternatives Considered

- Keep the bespoke lane and patch the script when it breaks. The script has broken twice by missing fixes that landed in the guide and env.sh, and every guide fix has to be applied twice.
- Migrate in one shot. Phase 2 needs coordinated changes in llm-d-infra and llm-d-benchmark, while Phase 1 removes the drift within llm-d immediately.

### Willingness to Contribute

Yes, I can submit a PR

### Additional Context

- Failure that prompted the issue: Nightly - Flow Control E2E (GKE GPU) #\76. The immediate URL fix is in a separate PR ("fix(ci): use env.sh release URL vars in flow-control nightly deploy").
- Slack discussion 2026-08-20: Marcio Silva suggested flow-control adopt the guide.yaml method; @Gregory-Pereira raised documenting the support and standardization level of each guide.
- Reference guides already on the method: `guides/optimized-baseline/guide.yaml`, `guides/fast-model-actuation/guide.yaml`.
