records.title: fix: correct argument order in test-dockerfile-lint.sh
records.body:
## Summary

`scripts/test-dockerfile-lint.sh` invokes the linter with reversed arguments. The linter signature is `lint-dockerfile-envvars.py <scripts-dir> <Dockerfile> [...]` (per its own usage banner), but both test calls pass `<Dockerfile> <scripts-dir>`.

With the args reversed, the linter raises `IsADirectoryError` trying to `read_text()` the scripts directory as if it were a Dockerfile. Test 1 is wrapped in `if ... ; then "expected fail" else "passed"`, so the crash gets misread as the expected detection of a missing variable — the test silently passes for the wrong reason. Test 2 fails outright with the same crash.

The script is not currently wired into a CI workflow, which is why this has gone unnoticed since [#324](https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d/pull/324).

## Repro (before fix)

```
$ bash scripts/test-dockerfile-lint.sh
Test 1: Dockerfile missing required variable (should FAIL)
Traceback (most recent call last):
  ...
  IsADirectoryError: [Errno 21] Is a directory: '/tmp/test-scripts'
✓ Test passed: correctly detected missing variable     # ← false positive, was a crash

Test 2: Dockerfile with all required variables (should PASS)
Traceback (most recent call last):
  ...
✗ Test failed: should have passed with all variables declared
exit=1
```

## After fix

```
$ bash scripts/test-dockerfile-lint.sh
Test 1: Dockerfile missing required variable (should FAIL)
/tmp/test-Dockerfile:5: Script 'test-script.sh' in stage 'test' requires:
  - TEST_VAR2 (not declared as ARG or ENV)
✗ 1 error(s) found
✓ Test passed: correctly detected missing variable

Test 2: Dockerfile with all required variables (should PASS)
✓ All Dockerfiles validated successfully
✓ Test passed: all variables declared

All tests passed!
exit=0
```

## Test plan

- [x] Run `bash scripts/test-dockerfile-lint.sh` — both tests now pass for the right reason (Test 1 sees the linter actually flag the missing var, Test 2 sees it accept the fixed Dockerfile)

records.title: fix(make): xpu-prepare must check out VLLM_XPU_COMMIT_SHA
records.body:
## Summary

`make xpu-prepare` clones vLLM and then runs `git checkout $(VLLM_COMMIT_SHA)`, but `VLLM_COMMIT_SHA` is the **CUDA** commit:

- [`docker/common-versions:5`](https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d/blob/main/docker/common-versions#L5) — \`VLLM_COMMIT_SHA=95c0f928... # maps to v0.17.1 tag\`
- [`docker/common-versions:35`](https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d/blob/main/docker/common-versions#L35) — \`VLLM_XPU_COMMIT_SHA=9dd656f0... # maps to v0.18.0rc2 tag for XPU RDMA support\`

The XPU SHA is defined separately and explicitly labelled as required for XPU RDMA support, but the Makefile target ignores it and checks out the CUDA SHA instead. The result is that `make xpu-prepare` produces an XPU build context from the wrong upstream commit.

## Fix

```diff
-	@git -C $(XPU_BUILD_DIR) checkout $(VLLM_COMMIT_SHA)
+	@git -C $(XPU_BUILD_DIR) checkout $(VLLM_XPU_COMMIT_SHA)
```

## Verification

\`make -n xpu-prepare DEVICE=xpu\` before/after:

**Before** — checks out the CUDA commit:
\`\`\`
git -C .cache/vllm-src checkout 95c0f928cdeeaa21c4906e73cee6a156e1b3b995
\`\`\`

**After** — checks out the XPU commit:
\`\`\`
git -C .cache/vllm-src checkout 9dd656f0ea06ba452e1f26666c111ea4909cd488
\`\`\`

## Note (out of scope for this PR)

\`XPU_VLLM_TAG\` in the Makefile is still pinned to \`v0.17.0\` and is used to fetch \`docker/Dockerfile.xpu\` from upstream vLLM (line 10 / 161). After this PR the source checkout is \`v0.18.0rc2\` while the Dockerfile is fetched from the \`v0.17.0\` tag — these may also be intentionally misaligned, or may be a related issue. Happy to follow up in a separate PR if maintainers confirm \`XPU_VLLM_TAG\` should track the XPU SHA.

## Test plan

- [x] \`make -n xpu-prepare DEVICE=xpu\` shows the checkout line resolves to the XPU SHA from \`docker/common-versions:35\`
- [ ] (Maintainer) End-to-end \`make image-build DEVICE=xpu\` on an XPU host

records.title: Remove tokenizer plugin and enable speculativeIndexing in precise-prefix-cache guide
records.body:
## Summary
- Remove `type: tokenizer` plugin from both scheduler configs
- Enable `speculativeIndexing: true` in `precise-prefix-cache-scorer`
- Remove `tokenizer` pluginRef from schedulingProfiles

## Why
The tokenizer plugin and speculative indexing cause double tokenization when both are enabled:
1. `PrepareRequestData` (speculative) runs **before** the tokenizer plugin's `Score()`
2. At that point CycleState is empty, so the scorer tokenizes independently via its own `tokenizersPoolConfig.uds`
3. Then the tokenizer plugin also tokenizes → UDS tokenizer called twice per request

Since `precise-prefix-cache-scorer` has its own tokenizer pool, the tokenizer plugin is redundant for this guide.

records.title: [CI]: nightly security events

root cause:

nightly-build-image.yaml calls the reusable workflow .github/workflows/build-image.yml, but it does not grant all permissions

Since the nightly caller only declared contents: read and  packages: write, GitHub rejected the workflow call due to the missing security-events permission.

records.title: fix: use WORKFLOW_TOKEN for fork PR /test-nightly push
records.body:
## Summary

- Restores `workflows: write` permission that was removed in #1260 (Apr 24)
- This broke `/test-nightly` for **fork PRs** — pushing a temp branch containing `.github/workflows/` files requires the `workflows` permission
- The permission was originally added in #1245 (Apr 23) for exactly this reason

## Root Cause

PR #1260 removed `workflows: write` from the permissions block on Apr 24. After that, any fork PR using `/test-nightly` fails with:

```
refusing to allow a GitHub App to create or update workflow
`.github/workflows/nightly-e2e-*.yaml` without `workflows` permission
```

Non-fork PRs still work because they don't need to push a temp branch.

## Timeline

| Date | Event |
|------|-------|
| Apr 23 | #1245 added `workflows: write` |
| Apr 24 | #1260 **removed** it |
| Apr 28 20:45 UTC | First fork PR failure (PR #1282) |
| May 1 | Reported by Rob via Marcio |

No new secrets needed — just restoring the YAML permission line.
records.author: clubanderson

records.title: fix: remove invalid workflows permission, use WORKFLOW_TOKEN PAT

- Removes `workflows: write` from the permissions block — it's not a valid `GITHUB_TOKEN` permission and caused `Invalid workflow file` on line 37, preventing the workflow from triggering at all
- Switches the fork PR temp-branch push from `GITHUB_TOKEN` to the org secret `WORKFLOW_TOKEN` (a fine-grained PAT with `contents:write` + `workflows` scope)

## Root Cause

PR #1335 added `workflows: write` to fix fork PR pushes, but `workflows` is not a valid permission for `GITHUB_TOKEN`. GitHub rejected the entire workflow file, breaking `/test-nightly` for **all** PRs (not just forks).

The correct fix is a separate PAT with workflows scope, stored as `WORKFLOW_TOKEN`.

## Test plan

- [ ] Comment `/test-nightly simulated-accelerators` on a non-fork PR to verify no regression

- Without this, `actions/checkout` sets an `http.extraheader` with `GITHUB_TOKEN` auth that **overrides** the `git remote set-url` using `WORKFLOW_TOKEN`, causing the push to use `GITHUB_TOKEN` (which lacks `workflows` permission)

## Root Cause

`actions/checkout` defaults to `persist-credentials: true`, which configures a git credential helper using `GITHUB_TOKEN`. This takes precedence over `git remote set-url`, so the `WORKFLOW_TOKEN` PAT (with `repo` + `workflow` scopes) was never actually used for the push.

## Test plan

- [ ] Comment `/test-nightly simulated-accelerators` on a fork PR after merge

## Description

This PR introduces a dedicated `README.tpu.md` for the Prefill/Decode Disaggregation guide.

**Context:**
The TPU implementation for P/D disaggregation diverges from the baseline guide in a few key areas: it targets a different model (`Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8` instead of `gpt-oss-120b`) and requires a specific hardware topology (TPU v7 `2x2x1`). 

Adding these TPU-specific details inline to the main guide would clutter the default GPU path. To provide a better experience for TPU users, this dedicated landing page gives them a clear, unambiguous starting point.

**Changes:**
This `README.tpu.md` acts as a lightweight quick-start guide that:
*   Highlights the specific `2x2x1` topology requirements.

*   Maintains a single source of truth by linking back to the unified `README.md` for all common steps (prerequisites, router deployment, and benchmarking), thereby avoiding documentation duplication.

Adds nightly regression tests for the predicted-latency guide on all three nightly providers (OpenShift, GKE, CoreWeave). Each deploys the optimized-baseline model server pods (the predicted-latency guide reuses these via the llm-d.ai/guide=optimized-baseline selector) plus the predicted-latency scheduler chart.

Beyond the standard e2e-validate.sh smoke test, the new e2e-validate-predicted-latency.sh sends 100 requests and scrapes the EPP /metrics endpoint, asserting

Wired in via a new --predicted-latency flag on e2e-validate.sh, passed through the reusable workflow's existing e2e_validate_args input so the caller workflows stay minimal.

records.title: Fix AWS image
records.body:
## Summary

- Simplify `release-aws-llm-d` to push directly with tags, removing the broken digest-passing mechanism
- Remove `release-aws-success-check` and `release-aws-manifest` jobs
- Update `verify-release-images` dependency from `release-aws-manifest` to `release-aws-llm-d`

## Problem

The `release-aws-manifest` job was silently skipped during the `v0.7.0-rc.1` release, resulting in the AWS image not being tagged.

**Root cause:** The digest-passing mechanism between jobs broke after `actions/upload-artifact` was bumped from v6 to v7 (#1149) and `actions/download-artifact` from v4 to v8 (#1219). With `upload-artifact@v7` (which defaults to `archive: true`) and `download-artifact@v8`, the artifact is downloaded successfully but the files are not extracted into the expected subdirectory structure. The `release-aws-success-check` job's reorganize step (`cp -v "$artifact_dir"/* ...`) finds nothing to copy, reports `any_succeeded=false`, and `release-aws-manifest` is skipped entirely.

This went unnoticed for CUDA because with 4 matrix variants the extraction behaves differently — AWS only has a single artifact (`digests-aws-rhel-amd64`), which triggers the incompatibility.

## Fix

Simplify `release-aws-llm-d` to push directly with tags (like `release-cpu-llm-d`, `release-rocm-llm-d`, and `release-hpu-llm-d` already do), removing the unnecessary `release-aws-success-check` and `release-aws-manifest` jobs. The multi-step digest→manifest pattern only benefits multi-arch builds (like CUDA with 4 platform variants). AWS is single-platform (`linux/amd64`, RHEL-only) so the extra indirection adds complexity with no benefit.

## Test plan

- [ ] Push a new RC tag and verify the `release-aws-llm-d` job pushes the image with the correct tag
- [ ] Verify `ghcr.io/llm-d/llm-d-aws:<tag>` is accessible after the workflow completes
- [ ] Verify `verify-release-images` job passes for the AWS image

`./helpers/local-llm-d-cuda-builder/build-local-llm-d-cuda.sh` has been updated with proper version files

**Test:**

We built on OCP cluster pod (Docker-in-Docker). Spin up a privileged pod with Docker (DinD), clone the repo, and run the build:

 apiVersion: v1

 spec:

 Then:

 # Run with docker (default)
 ./helpers/local-llm-d-cuda-builder/build-local-llm-d-cuda.sh --tag test-fix

  • Fixed a bug where two diagnostics produced within the same millisecond could overwrite each other on disk, causing one of them to be lost. #3852
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.25.3. #3865

v3.35.2

  • The undocumented TRAP cache cleanup feature that could be enabled using the CODEQL_ACTION_CLEANUP_TRAP_CACHES environment variable is deprecated and will be removed in May 2026. If you are affected by this, we recommend disabling TRAP caching by passing the trap-caching: false input to the init Action. #3795
  • The Git version 2.36.0 requirement for improved incremental analysis now only applies to repositories that contain submodules. #3789
  • Python analysis on GHES no longer extracts the standard library, relying instead on models of the standard library. This should result in significantly faster extraction and analysis times, while the effect on alerts should be minimal. #3794
  • Fixed a bug in the validation of OIDC configurations for private registries that was added in CodeQL Action 4.33.0 / 3.33.0. #3807
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.25.2. #3823

v3.35.1

  • Fix incorrect minimum required Git version for improved incremental analysis: it should have been 2.36.0, not 2.11.0. #3781

v3.35.0

  • Reduced the minimum Git version required for improved incremental analysis from 2.38.0 to 2.11.0. #3767
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.25.1. #3773

v3.34.1

  • Downgrade default CodeQL bundle version to 2.24.3 due to issues with a small percentage of Actions and JavaScript analyses. #3762

v3.34.0

  • Added an experimental change which disables TRAP caching when improved incremental analysis is enabled, since improved incremental analysis supersedes TRAP caching. This will improve performance and reduce Actions cache usage. We expect to roll this change out to everyone in March. #3569
  • We are rolling out improved incremental analysis to C/C++ analyses that use build mode none. We expect this rollout to be complete by the end of April 2026. #3584
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.25.0. #3585

v3.33.0

  • Upcoming change: Starting April 2026, the CodeQL Action will skip collecting file coverage information on pull requests to improve analysis performance. File coverage information will still be computed on non-PR analyses. Pull request analyses will log a warning about this upcoming change. #3562 To opt out of this change:
    • Repositories owned by an organization: Create a custom repository property with the name github-codeql-file-coverage-on-prs and the type "True/false", then set this property to true in the repository's settings. For more information, see Managing custom properties for repositories in your organization. Alternatively, if you are using an advanced setup workflow, you can set the CODEQL_ACTION_FILE_COVERAGE_ON_PRS environment variable to true in your workflow.
    • User-owned repositories using default setup: Switch to an advanced setup workflow and set the CODEQL_ACTION_FILE_COVERAGE_ON_PRS environment variable to true in your workflow.
    • User-owned repositories using advanced setup: Set the CODEQL_ACTION_FILE_COVERAGE_ON_PRS environment variable to true in your workflow.
  • Fixed a bug which caused the CodeQL Action to fail loading repository properties if a "Multi select" repository property was configured for the repository. #3557
  • The CodeQL Action now loads custom repository properties on GitHub Enterprise Server, enabling the customization of features such as github-codeql-disable-overlay that was previously only available on GitHub.com. #3559
  • Once private package registries can be configured with OIDC-based authentication for organizations, the CodeQL Action will now be able to accept such configurations. #3563
  • Fixed the retry mechanism for database uploads. Previously this would fail with the error "Response body object should not be disturbed or locked". #3564
  • A warning is now emitted if the CodeQL Action detects a repository property whose name suggests that it relates to the CodeQL Action, but which is not one of the properties recognised by the current version of the CodeQL Action. #3570

v3.32.6

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.24.3. #3548

v3.32.5

  • Repositories owned by an organization can now set up the github-codeql-disable-overlay custom repository property to disable improved incremental analysis for CodeQL. First, create a custom repository property with the name github-codeql-disable-overlay and the type "True/false" in the organization's settings. Then in the repository's settings, set this property to true to disable improved incremental analysis. For more information, see Managing custom properties for repositories in your organization. This feature is not yet available on GitHub Enterprise Server. #3507
  • Added an experimental change so that when improved incremental analysis fails on a runner — potentially due to insufficient disk space — the failure is recorded in the Actions cache so that subsequent runs will automatically skip improved incremental analysis until something changes (e.g. a larger runner is provisioned or a new CodeQL version is released). We expect to roll this change out to everyone in March. #3487
  • The minimum memory check for improved incremental analysis is now skipped for CodeQL 2.24.3 and later, which has reduced peak RAM usage. #3515
  • Reduced log levels for best-effort private package registry connection check failures to reduce noise from workflow annotations. #3516
  • Added an experimental change which lowers the minimum disk space requirement for improved incremental analysis, enabling it to run on standard GitHub Actions runners. We expect to roll this change out to everyone in March. #3498

... (truncated)

Changelog

Sourced from github/codeql-action's changelog.

4.31.5 - 24 Nov 2025

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.23.6. #3321

4.31.4 - 18 Nov 2025

No user facing changes.

4.31.3 - 13 Nov 2025

  • CodeQL Action v3 will be deprecated in December 2026. The Action now logs a warning for customers who are running v3 but could be running v4. For more information, see Upcoming deprecation of CodeQL Action v3.
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.23.5. #3288

4.31.2 - 30 Oct 2025

No user facing changes.

4.31.1 - 30 Oct 2025

  • The add-snippets input has been removed from the analyze action. This input has been deprecated since CodeQL Action 3.26.4 in August 2024 when this removal was announced.

4.31.0 - 24 Oct 2025

  • Bump minimum CodeQL bundle version to 2.17.6. #3223
  • When SARIF files are uploaded by the analyze or upload-sarif actions, the CodeQL Action automatically performs post-processing steps to prepare the data for the upload. Previously, these post-processing steps were only performed before an upload took place. We are now changing this so that the post-processing steps will always be performed, even when the SARIF files are not uploaded. This does not change anything for the upload-sarif action. For analyze, this may affect Advanced Setup for CodeQL users who specify a value other than always for the upload input. #3222

4.30.9 - 17 Oct 2025

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.23.3. #3205
  • Experimental: A new setup-codeql action has been added which is similar to init, except it only installs the CodeQL CLI and does not initialize a database. Do not use this in production as it is part of an internal experiment and subject to change at any time. #3204

4.30.8 - 10 Oct 2025

No user facing changes.

4.30.7 - 06 Oct 2025

  • [v4+ only] The CodeQL Action now runs on Node.js v24. #3169

3.30.6 - 02 Oct 2025

3.30.5 - 26 Sep 2025

  • We fixed a bug that was introduced in 3.30.4 with upload-sarif which resulted in files without a .sarif extension not getting uploaded. #3160

3.30.4 - 25 Sep 2025

  • We have improved the CodeQL Action's ability to validate that the workflow it is used in does not use different versions of the CodeQL Action for different workflow steps. Mixing different versions of the CodeQL Action in the same workflow is unsupported and can lead to unpredictable results. A warning will now be emitted from the codeql-action/init step if different versions of the CodeQL Action are detected in the workflow file. Additionally, an error will now be thrown by the other CodeQL Action steps if they load a configuration file that was generated by a different version of the codeql-action/init step. #3099 and #3100

records.title: Fix/predicted latency duplicate metrics port
records.body:
## Summary

Fixes two failures hit by `nightly-e2e-predicted-latency-{gke,cks,ocp}` after the duplicate-port fix in #1383 unblocked the deploy step. Both failures are in the `e2e-validate-predicted-latency.sh` validate stage that runs after the smoke loop.

### 1. Empty warmup payload (`8937f00`)

The script wrote the request body via:

```bash
kubectl exec -n "$NS" "$POD" -- sh -c "cat > /tmp/payload.json" <<<"$PAYLOAD"
```

`kubectl exec ... -- sh -c "cat > file"` silently produces a **0-byte file** — `cat`'s stdin never receives the herestring through `sh -c`, even when `-i` is passed. The 100 warmup curls then sent empty bodies, vLLM rejected all of them, and the script aborted at:

```
Sending 100 requests with concurrency 8...
Error: zero successful warmup requests — gateway/model server is not serving traffic.
Warmup result: ok=0 fail=100
```

Reproduced on a live cluster:

| pattern | result |
|---|---|
| `kubectl exec -i -- sh -c 'cat > file'` | 0 bytes ❌ |
| `kubectl exec -i -- tee /tmp/file` | 76 bytes ✓ |

Pipe through `tee` instead — when the inner command is the direct stdin consumer (rather than a redirect inside `sh -c`), `kubectl exec -i` delivers stdin reliably.

### 2. EPP `/metrics` rejected by auth (`e70b2dc`)

After the warmup fix, the next failure is the metrics scrape. The chart defaults `--metrics-endpoint-auth=true`, which 401s requests without a service-account bearer token. `e2e-validate-predicted-latency.sh` runs in a generic `curlimages/curl` pod with no token, so `/metrics` returns the 401 body, `sum_histogram_count` finds no histogram lines, and the script aborts with:

```
predicted_ttft_count=0
Error: predicted TTFT histogram is empty after 100 requests.
```

Pass `--set inferenceExtension.monitoring.prometheus.auth.enabled=false` to the chart's `helm install` in all three nightlies (GKE/CKS/OCP). This adds `--metrics-endpoint-auth=false` to the EPP container args (chart helper at [`charts/inference-extension/templates/_deployment.yaml:143-144`](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api-inference-extension/blob/v1.5.0/config/charts/inference-extension/templates/_deployment.yaml#L143-L144)). **CI-only** — the production guide default (auth on) is unchanged.

### Verified locally end-to-end

Ran the patched script against a live cluster (with auth-off applied):

```
Warmup result: ok=100 fail=0
actual_ttft_count=116 predicted_ttft_count=116
✅ Predicted-latency scheduling is active: predictor returned predictions for 116 requests.
```

records.title: optimized-baseline: mount /.triton and /.config emptyDirs for non-root pods
records.body:
Adds emptyDir volumes mounted at `/.triton` and `/.config` to the optimized-baseline modelserver overlay so the manifest runs on clusters that enforce non-root execution by default (OpenShift `restricted-v2` SCC, or plain k8s under PSA `restricted` with a non-root pod security policy).

This is exactly the patch the nightly OpenShift CI applies at runtime via `yq` in `.github/workflows/nightly-e2e-optimized-baseline-ocp.yaml` (you pointed at it on #1430). Baking it into the base manifest matches the existing `/.cache` + `torch-compile-cache` mount precedent already in this file and lets the documented quickstart work on OpenShift without extra runtime patching.

`/.triton` is the fatal one (Triton runtime cache, kills engine init). `/.config` is non-fatal but is the same shape of root-filesystem write and currently logs a `PermissionError` from the `_report_usage_worker` thread on every pod start under `restricted-v2`. Including both in the same change so the manifest is silent on this class of error rather than just non-fatal.

Verified end-to-end on a fresh OpenShift cluster with `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.19.1` and `Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507` on 2× L40S (TP=2):

- Unpatched manifest: CrashLoopBackOff with the exact stack trace from the issue body — `/.config` PermissionError during model load (non-fatal), then `/.triton` PermissionError → `torch._inductor.exc.InductorError` → engine init fails.
- Patched manifest: boots cleanly past Triton kernel compilation, model load, and engine init. Serves chat completions through `/v1/chat/completions`.

Full evidence (crash log + clean-startup log + manifests as applied) at [`fips-agents/examples`](https://github.com/fips-agents/examples/tree/main/retrospectives/2026-05-06_llm-d-scc-pr-validation).

Closes #1430.

1. **Created & Configured GKE LMCache Nightly Workflow:**
   - Added `nightly-e2e-tiered-prefix-cache-cpu-offloading-lmcache-gke.yaml` to test the LMCache CPU offloading connector on GKE (staggered daily at 15:30 UTC with 8 H100 GPUs).

2. **Renamed Native CPU Offloading Workflows for Naming Consistency:**
   - Renamed both GKE and OpenShift (OCP) native workflow files to explicitly include `cpu-offloading` in their filenames, internal names, and concurrency groups:
     - `nightly-e2e-tiered-prefix-cache-gke.yaml` -> `nightly-e2e-tiered-prefix-cache-cpu-offloading-gke.yaml`
     - `nightly-e2e-tiered-prefix-cache-ocp.yaml` -> `nightly-e2e-tiered-prefix-cache-cpu-offloading-ocp.yaml`

3. **Restored Pristine Concurrency Groups:**
   - Retained original concurrency groups to coordinate scheduling and slot occupancy on nightly runners:
     - GKE Native: `nightly-e2e-tiered-prefix-cache-gke`
     - OCP Native: `nightly-e2e-tiered-prefix-cache`

4. **Updated Guide Status Badges:**
   - Updated status badges for vLLM Native (both GKE and OCP) and LMCache (GKE) in `guides/tiered-prefix-cache/README.md` and `guides/tiered-prefix-cache/cpu/README.md` to match the new filenames.

5. **Registered New Nightlies in Slash Test Runner:**
   - Registered all new and renamed workflows in `slash-test-nightly.yaml` to enable on-demand `/test-nightly` triggering.

6. **Fixed GKE GPU Requirements:**
   - Set GKE native and LMCache CPU offloading workflows to request 8 H100 GPUs to ensure Qwen3-32B is tested as-is.

records.title: Supporting Mooncake in llm-d
records.body:
I have been experimenting with adding mooncake support to llm-d. Mooncake has two connectors - mooncake store connector and mooncake connector. The store connector is responsible for a global kv cache pool and is used by the prefillers (read and write) as well as the decoders (write). The mooncake connector does direct gpu to gpu pd transfer. 

This PR enables both the mooncake store connector and the mooncake connector in llm-d.  It added the mooncake store connector (mooncake-master using mooncake terminology) in a pod and updates the vllm pods to start with both connectors using the kv multi connector, similar to how it's done in https://vllm.ai/blog/mooncake-store.  

I have also updated the pd-disaggregation and the tiering guides with instructions on how to enable mooncake.  

Note that this PR is opened as a draft PR.  The mooncake store manager was merged into vllm on Wed and was not in any vllm image when I did this work.  I had to do some ugly repo cloning to get all the code/libraries in place. The mooncake PR should be in the recent vllm 0.21 image and I will update this PR as needed.

records.title: Add Azure Managed Lustre backend guide for tiered prefix cache storage
records.body:
## Summary

Adds an Azure Managed Lustre Filesystem (AMLFS) backend guide and `StorageClass` to `guides/tiered-prefix-cache/storage/manifests/backends/azure/`, matching the existing per-backend layout under `aws/` (EFS) and `lustre/` (GCP Lustre).

Concretely:

- `manifests/backends/azure/storage_class.yaml` — `StorageClass` using the upstream [`azurelustre.csi.azure.com`](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-managed-lustre/use-csi-driver-kubernetes) driver. Dynamic provisioning (AKS creates the AMLFS cluster on PVC bind), `mountOptions: [noatime]`, `AMLFS-Durable-Premium-250` as a reasonable default SKU.
- `manifests/backends/azure/README.md` — Prerequisites / cluster setup / provisioning / PVC verification / performance recommendations / cleanup. Mirrors the structure of `backends/aws/README.md`.
- Updates `guides/tiered-prefix-cache/storage/README.md` to link the new Azure backend guide alongside the existing GCP Lustre and AWS EFS links, and adds `azurelustre-class` to the `STORAGE_CLASS` env-var hint.

## Validation

The provisioning instructions in `backends/azure/README.md` were exercised on an AKS H200 cluster against an existing AMLFS (16 TiB, `mgs-ip-address` + `fs-name` for static, plus the dynamic provisioning path) with the official `azurelustre.csi.azure.com` driver. A two-pod `gpu-vllm-decode` deployment ran the tiered-prefix-cache storage guide end-to-end and produced observable cross-pod KV reuse via the shared Lustre PVC (`External prefix cache hit rate: 69.9%` on a reader pod that never received the writer pod's traffic, with content-addressed block files visible on the AMLFS mount). Full validation evidence will be posted under #1252 separately; that benchmark is intentionally **not** committed here to keep this PR scoped to the per-backend provisioning guide.

## Related

- Per-backend guide pattern established by #1264 (AWS EFS).
- Validates the Azure backend dimension of #1252 ("Validate llm-d with shared storage across multiple vendors").

records.title: [PD] Increase keep-alive timeout in well-lit P/D guides
records.body:
Set VLLM_HTTP_TIMEOUT_KEEP_ALIVE=120 on all prefill server configs in the P/D well-lit paths (wide-ep-lws, experimental-dp-aware, pd-disaggregation HPU)

## Problem
The decode sidecar's Go HTTP transport keeps idle connections in its pool for 90 seconds (IdleConnTimeout: 90 * time.Second in proxy.go), but uvicorn's default keep-alive timeout is only 5 seconds (VLLM_HTTP_TIMEOUT_KEEP_ALIVE=5).

When a prefill connection goes idle for >5s, uvicorn closes it. If the sidecar reuses that connection before its own 90s timeout, the request arrives on a socket that uvicorn is closing — the kernel sees unread data and sends RST.

This was observed under load on GB200 NVL72 with DeepSeek-R1, P2D8 setup, where gaps between consecutive prefill requests on a single connection from time to time exceed 5 seconds.

# Add Customer-Facing Blog: CPU KV Cache Offloading Well-Lit Path

## Summary

Adds a customer-facing blog post for llm-d's **CPU KV Cache Offloading** well-lit path. The post explains how offloading evicted KV cache blocks to host CPU memory supports longer context windows, higher concurrency, and better prefix reuse — without recomputing full prefills.

Tracked under INFERENG-5882. Complements existing deployment guides and avoids duplicating the storage-tier offloading content.

## Changes

- **Added:** `docs/blog/cpu-kv-cache-offloading-well-lit-path.md` (96 lines)
  - Follows the Kubernetes blog post structure (problem → how it works → how to use → how to help)
  - Author: Antonio Cardace, Fahim Uddin
  - Covers vLLM `OffloadingConnector`, tier-aware router configuration, and expected benchmark gains

```
docs/
├── accelerators/
├── api-reference/
├── architecture/
├── assets/
├── blog/                                          ← new
│   └── cpu-kv-cache-offloading-well-lit-path.md   ← added blog (.md)

├── infra-providers/
├── monitoring/
├── proposals/
├── resources/
├── well-lit-paths/
├── infrastructure.md
└── readiness-probes.md
```

## Key Points

- **CPU tier only** — focuses on per-node host DRAM offloading; does not cover shared storage or cross-replica cache sharing
- **Defers deployment details** — link to the (../../guides/tiered-prefix-cache/cpu/README.md) for Helm/Kustomize manifests and verification
- **Avoids duplication** with:
  - [Storage offloading blog](https://llm-d.ai/blog/native-kv-cache-offloading-to-any-file-system-with-llm-d)

- **Benchmark highlights cited** from the CPU guide: ~25% lower mean TTFT and ~21% higher throughput when KV working set exceeds HBM (Qwen3-32B, 4× H100, 100 GB CPU offload)

## Dependencies

records.title: fix(e2e-xpu): pin router chart to v0, not GAIE_VERSION
records.body:
## Summary

The XPU e2e workflows migrated to the new `llm-d-router-standalone-dev` chart in [#1607](https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d/pull/1607) but still passed `--version ${GAIE_VERSION}` (v1.5.0) to `helm install`. That chart only publishes `v0`, so every run fails at the deploy step with:

```
Error: INSTALLATION FAILED: ghcr.io/llm-d/charts/llm-d-router-standalone-dev:v1.5.0: not found
```

(e.g. [run 26633694208](https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d/actions/runs/26633694208/job/78488520241)). `GAIE_VERSION` is still correct for the Gateway API Inference Extension CRD apply — only the helm chart version was wrong.

records.title: Optimized Baseline Architectural Shift & Updated Benchmarks
records.body:
## Summary
This PR transitions the **Optimized Baseline** configuration to a new scheduling strategy that combines the **Token Load Scorer** with **Prefix Cache Affinity Filtering**. This approach optimizes for both backend saturation (via tokens-in-flight) and prefix reuse, resulting in significantly improved throughput and latency profiles compared to standard Kubernetes round-robin. 

While the previous optimized-baseline configuration (based on queue-depth and kv-cache utilization) was hard to generalize across diverse workloads (detailed in [this design doc](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1AdGHoDksnXYI3kA71I5MkH66zPrDsvBzq9aomRXZlpE/edit?tab=t.0#heading=h.p2dtnj3m44at)), this new setup provides a robust "performance floor" that remains vastly superior to stock K8s (+67.8% throughput, -99.5% TTFT). Although we observe a slight decrease in aggregate output tokens per second in this specific benchmark compared to the previous version, this new configuration has proven to work well across a wider range of production workloads.

## Key Architectural Changes
*   **Token-Load Aware Scheduling:** Integrated the `token-load-scorer` as the primary scoring mechanism to balance requests based on real-time token processing load.
*   **Prefix Affinity Overrides:** Implemented the `prefix-cache-affinity-filter` with an automated saturation valve ($\tau$). This ensures sticky routing for prefix cache benefits until a pod reaches a measured load threshold.


## Benchmarking Report Refresh
The `Benchmarking Report` has been updated with final results using this new architecture. The data shows that balancing by token load while respecting prefix affinity provides a superior performance floor compared to standard round-robin.

records.title: guides: add vLLM request draining configuration
records.body:
Configure `--shutdown-timeout` and `terminationGracePeriodSeconds` across all vLLM guides. Values chosen are as follows:
- optimized-baseline, precise-prefix-cache-routing: 30s and 60s
- tiered-prefix-cache: 30s and 60s for all except  (CPU offloading variants — lmcache-connector, offloading-connector) - they have 30s and 130s
- pd-disaggregation: 60s and 90s
- wide-ep-lws: 300s and 330s

Fixes #1525

Reason behind choosing these values:

1. optimized-baseline / precise-prefix-cache-routing → The benchmark reports an ITL mean of 47ms/token for Qwen3-32B on H100s. A 500-token response completes in ~24s, well within 30s. 
2. pd-disaggregation → The benchmark at 5k ISL / 250 OSL shows p99=6.53s and max=11.12s. The guide targets 10k ISL / 1k OSL workloads, which roughly doubles request latency (~20-25s). Additional headroom accounts for RDMA KV transfer cleanup between prefill and decode pods during shutdown.
3. wide-ep-lws → The benchmark at 2k ISL / 2k OSL shows min=137s, mean=175s, and max=259s for DeepSeek-R1. 300s covers the observed maximum of 259s with a ~40s buffer.
4. tiered-prefix-cache → Same compute profile as optimized-baseline. The base patch for  (CPU offloading variants — lmcache-connector, offloading-connector) already had terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 130, which satisfies the >= shutdown-timeout rule; left unchanged to preserve the existing value. The remaining (storage + TPU variants — llm-d-fs-connector, lmcache-connector, tpu-offloading-connector) is set to terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 60.

records.title: Dynamic nightly lists identification
records.body:
## Summary

- Replace hardcoded nightly lists (`E2E_NIGHTLIES`, `OTHER_NIGHTLIES`) with dynamic detection via the GitHub Contents API
- New nightlies are now automatically available to `/test-nightly` as soon as their workflow file is merged to `main` — no manual list updates needed
- Add dispatch fallback: if a workflow doesn't declare `pr_number`/`pr_repo` inputs (e.g. `build-image`), retry the dispatch without inputs instead of failing

## How it works

- **Exact name** (`/test-nightly wva-ocp`): probes for `nightly-e2e-<name>.yaml` then `nightly-<name>.yaml` on `main` using `repos.getContent` (max 2 API calls)
- **Glob pattern** (`/test-nightly *-ocp`): lists all files in `.github/workflows/` on `main`, extracts nightly names from matching filenames, applies the glob filter
- **Error messages**: dynamically list available nightlies by reading the workflow directory, so the help text is always up to date

@llm-d/release-crew

records.title: fix(pd): increase keep-alive timeout in remaining vLLM prefill manifests
records.body:
Issue: 
Deploy P/D disaggregation guides. Decode routing sidecar forwards  requests to prefill server. Connection idle time stays between 5s and 90s.
 Intermittent prefill or inference request failures. Connection terminations via  TCP RST.
 
Root Cause: 
PR #1564 identified HTTP keep-alive timeout mismatch between sidecar  idle timeout (90s) and uvicorn default timeout (5s) but only applied fixes to HPU and select  GPU manifests. Mismatch resides in software layer (vLLM/uvicorn config) and affects all  hardware setups. Remaining hardware-specific manifests lack this uniform alignment.

 Remediation: 
Configure  VLLM_HTTP_TIMEOUT_KEEP_ALIVE: "120"  in patch-prefill.yaml,  patch-prefill.yaml, patch-prefill.yaml, and patch-prefill.yaml.

## What this does

Adds a reusable benchmarking setup and a published results report to the **predicted-latency-routing** guide, plus a few correctness fixes to the router and model-server manifests.

## Changes

**Benchmarking templates** (`benchmark-templates/`)
- `run_benchmark.sh` — reusable orchestration script. Restarts the EPP, provisions a per-run PVC, submits one `inference-perf` Job per concurrency level, waits with early failure detection, then collects results from the PVC via a copy pod. Workload-agnostic via the `WORKLOAD` env var, with overridable `CONCURRENCY_LEVELS`, `MODEL_NAME`, and `EPP_DEPLOYMENT`.
- `bench-job.yaml` — Kubernetes Job template (pinned to `inference-perf:v0.5.0`).
- `workloads/code-generation/code-generation.yaml` — synthetic code-generation workload (conversation replay; long shared/dynamic system prompts; multi-turn; lognormal input/output lengths).

**Model server overlays** (`modelserver/gpu/vllm/{base,gke}`)
- Kustomize overlays that reuse the optimized-baseline model server with a predicted-latency patch (10 decode replicas, TP=2, 131072 context, YARN rope scaling).
- The `gke` overlay includes the `disable-gke-nccl-tuner-patch` component for parity with optimized-baseline.

**Router values** (`router/`)
- `predicted-latency.values.yaml` (routing-only): corrected the header to describe the routing-only setup (predictor trains on end-to-end latency, no SLO headers, no streaming required); fixed the `pluginsConfigFile` key so it matches the provided custom config and the pipeline is actually applied; fixed `prefix-cache-scorer` parameter indentation.
- `predicted-latency-slo.values.yaml` (SLO-aware): corrected `prefix-cache-scorer` indentation / `maxPrefixTokensToMatch` nesting and declared the missing `slo-headroom-tier-filter` plugin.

**README**
- New **Benchmarking** section (workload description, run steps, env-var override table, `<run-id>` clarification).
- New **Benchmarking Report** with the code-generation comparison plot and full per-concurrency data table (predicted-latency routing vs. plain k8s Service).
- Fixed the cleanup step to delete the predicted-latency-routing model-server overlay (was pointing at optimized-baseline).

## Benchmark results

Run on 10 vLLM decode pods (TP=2, 20 × H100), `Qwen/Qwen3-32B`. Predicted-latency routing vs. a plain Kubernetes Service:

| Metric | Δ vs k8s Service |
|---|---|
| Input throughput | **+38.3%** |
| Output throughput | **+40.2%** |
| TTFT p50 | **−13.0%** |
| TTFT p90 | **−46.8%** |

records.title: optimized-baseline: mount /.triton and /.config emptyDirs on non-gpu vllm variants
records.body:
The `vllm/vllm-openai` engine writes a Triton compiler cache to `/.triton` (fatal) and a usage_lib config to `/.config` (non-fatal) at the filesystem root, since `HOME=/` for non-root containers. On clusters that enforce non-root execution (OpenShift restricted-v2 SCC, or k8s under PSA restricted), both writes fail with `PermissionError` and the `/.triton` failure crashes the model server, as reported in #1311.

PR #1450 baked these emptyDir mounts into the gpu variant. The remaining vllm variants of this guide were not updated and still hit the crash under a restricted SecurityContext. This applies the same mounts to amd, cpu, tpu-v6, tpu-v7 and xpu, matching the gpu variant and the precise-prefix-cache-routing guide (which already mounts `/.triton` on all of its variants). hpu already sets `DO_NOT_TRACK=1`, so it does not write `/.config` and only needed the `/.triton` mount. sglang variants are unaffected (they do not write the Triton cache).

Verified with `kustomize build` and `kubectl apply --dry-run` on each variant; the rendered Deployments carry the triton-cache and vllm-config volumes. Worth a maintainer run of `/test-nightly optimized-baseline-ocp`.

Closes #1311

records.title: docs: surface agentgateway as a supported proxyType in standalone router guides
records.body:
Closes #1713

## what this does

the llm-d-router-standalone chart already supports agentgateway as a sidecar proxy (`router.proxy.proxyType=agentgateway`) but none of the guides mentioned it, everything just assumed envoy. this PR adds the agentgateway docs and lines up the install commands with the chart's pseudo-service model (no service.name/service.ports needed anymore).

## changes

**guides/recipes/router/README.md**
- new "Standalone with agentgateway" section next to the existing envoy one, with a working helm install example
- NOTE callout for the required flags (`inferencePool.create=false`, `epp.flags.secure-serving=false`)
- added a Prerequisites section for the env vars used across these guides (REPO_ROOT, NAMESPACE, ROUTER_CHART_VERSION, via guides/env.sh)

**guides/recipes/router/base.values.yaml**
- kept the explicit envoy args here instead of switching to `args: []`. tried that first but the chart preset uses `--cpuset-threads` instead of `--concurrency 8`, and since this pod has no cpu limit that ends up spawning threads off the whole node instead of the tuned value from the v0.8.0 benchmark run. so args stayed as is, agentgateway gets its own args from the features overlay below

**guides/recipes/router/features/agentgateway-proxy.values.yaml** (new)
- sets proxyType: agentgateway + the required flags, swaps out the envoy args for agentgateway's

**guides/optimized-baseline/README.md**
- just points to the router recipes guide for agentgateway now instead of duplicating a whole snippet here, didn't want to add another dimension to an already complex guide

**docs/api-reference/artifacts.md**
- updated the standalone chart description to mention agentgateway as an option

## testing

ran `helm template` against both proxyType=envoy and proxyType=agentgateway for the affected guides.

also did a real e2e run on a fresh kind cluster, not just template. ran the exact helm install commands from `guides/recipes/router/README.md` for both paths:
- standalone with envoy: pod came up 2/2 running, sent a real `/v1/completions` request, got a real completion back
- standalone with agentgateway: same, pod 2/2 running, real completion back

only deviations from the literal guide commands were cpu/memory resource overrides (the guide's defaults are 4 cpu / 8gi per component, meant for real clusters, too big for a kind node) and the agentgateway image tag override, since the chart's built-in default tag doesn't exist in the registry. everything else ran exactly as documented.

## related

- closes #1713

records.title: Normalize the names of "nightly E2E" workflows
records.body:
This PRs does not introduce any changes into the workflows, it merely renames these files in a normalized manner.

The normalized names follow the convention:

`<workflow>-<guide>-<provider>-<offload destination>-<accelerator>-<inference engine>-<cache connector>.yaml`

Where:
`<guide>` is the list provided by `$(find guides/ -maxdepth 2 -name README.md -print | grep -Ev "rollouts|prereqs|recipes|guides/README.md")`

 `<provider>` indicates which companies/members (and teams) are providing hardware resources for testing (currently, `cks`, `gke`, `ibm`, `intel` and `amd`)

`<offload destination>` possible values are `acc` (indicating that no offloading is done, as all blocks are retined within the accelerator), `gpu`, `storage` 

`<accelerator>`: `gpu`, `tpu`, `rocm`, `xpu` and `hpu` 

`<cache connector>`: `x` (for "don't care"/"not defined"), `native` (for `vllm`) and `lmcache`

## Summary

Replace GitHub's native workflow status badges (green/red only) with shields.io endpoint badges backed by GitHub Pages, enabling color-coded status for different failure types in the nightly testing matrix.

- Add a reusable workflow (`.github/workflows/reusable-update-badge.yaml`) that classifies job results and pushes badge JSON to the `gh-pages` branch

## Badge Color Classification

| Status | Color | Badge | Detection |
|--------|-------|-------|-----------|
| Tests pass | `brightgreen` | ![passing](https://img.shields.io/badge/GPU-passing-brightgreen) | `needs.nightly.result == 'success'` |
| Test failure | `red` | ![failing](https://img.shields.io/badge/GPU-failing-red) | Failed step does not match infrastructure keywords |

| Timeout | `yellow` | ![timeout](https://img.shields.io/badge/GPU-timeout-yellow) | Job ran >50 min before cancellation |
| Cancelled | `lightgrey` | ![cancelled](https://img.shields.io/badge/GPU-cancelled-lightgrey) | Cancelled before 50 min threshold |
| Skipped | `lightgrey` | ![skipped](https://img.shields.io/badge/GPU-skipped-lightgrey) | Job was skipped |

The classification uses the GitHub API (`actions: read`) to inspect which step failed in the workflow run, distinguishing infrastructure setup failures from actual test failures without requiring changes to `llm-d-infra`.

records.title: ci: add nightly e2e for the flow-control guide
records.body:
**Problem:**

The flow-control guide is the only well-lit-path guide without nightly CI (Refs #1360). Its smoke test can't catch regressions: flow control is work-conserving, so single sequential requests never queue and never exercise the feature.

**Change:**

A nightly e2e on the existing GKE GPU lane that forces queue contention across the three priority bands and asserts the guarantees that matter: per-band queue isolation and priority-ordered (QoS) dispatch. Hard assertions use cumulative histogram metrics (insensitive to scrape timing); backpressure is made deterministic by lowering `concurrency-detector` `maxConcurrency` (matched by key, with a guard so a future retune can't silently no-op it).

**Maintenance:**

Extends the established #1360 nightly pattern (same `--extra-validate` mechanism as predicted-latency). Owned by the flow-control guide owner. **Nightly only -- does not gate PR merges**; run on demand via `/test-nightly flow-control-gke-acc-gpu-vllm-x`. Cost is one scheduled GPU job/day reusing the optimized-baseline model servers; no new runners or curated inputs.

records.title: [WideEP][AMD] MoRI-IO WideEP
records.body:
Adds an AMD/vLLM **2P2D Wide-EP-16** P/D-disaggregation example for DeepSeek-V3 (global **DP=EP=16, TP=1** across 2 prefill + 2 decode pods) that uses the MoRI-IO KV-transfer connector and the MoRI-EP all-to-all backend. Additive follow-up to the 1P1D DP=EP=8 overlay in this PR: it inherits that base (`../moriio`) unchanged, patches the master Deployments to the DP=16 / dp_local=8 shape, and adds headless prefill/decode child Deployments for the second 8-rank pod on each side. This is the multi-node EP=16 wide-EP case (vs. the single-pod EP=8 base).

Deploys with a single `kubectl kustomize . | kubectl apply` once the `REPLACE_*` placeholders (node hostnames, pod IPs, and the two images) are pinned.

- Masters: `--data-parallel-size=16 --data-parallel-size-local=8 --data-parallel-address=$(POD_IP) --data-parallel-rpc-port=...`, `--api-server-count=8`; children add `--data-parallel-start-rank=8 --headless` (ranks 8..15, no OAI front-end, no sidecar).
- Prefill: `--all2all-backend=mori_high_throughput`, kv_role=kv_producer. Decode: `--all2all-backend=mori_low_latency`, kv_role=kv_consumer.
- Decode routing sidecar multi-pod fan-out: `--moriio-dp-size=16 --moriio-dp-size-local=8 --moriio-remote-hosts=<prefill master,child> --moriio-decode-hosts=<decode master,child>` plus the inherited `--moriio-write-mode / --moriio-parallel-dispatch / --moriio-local-pod-ip`. vLLM resolves `pod_idx = global_dp_rank // dp_size_local`; absent those keys the 1P1D path is unchanged.
- Cross-pod RoCEv2 fabric env (`patch-nccl-env.yaml`) on all 4 pods, `MORI_SHMEM_HEAP_SIZE=16 GiB`, and raised NCCL/engine/handshake timeouts so the DP=16 process group forms over the ~25-min DSV3 cold start.
- `inductor-shim-configmap.yaml`: a sitecustomize shim disabling `torch._inductor` pointwise autotune to avoid a cross-rank benchmark deadlock on the first forward at DP=16.
- `patch-strategy-recreate.yaml`: Recreate strategy on the pinned, hostNetwork, replicas=1 Deployments (RollingUpdate wedges them).
- The shared MoRI-IO ZMQ registration proxy from the base is reused (via `REPLACE_ZMQ_PROXY_IP`); no duplicate proxy.

The PR will address [WideEP]: AMD MI355X MoRI EP Guide for Pollara/Thor-2 NIC #1470 and [P/D][AMD]: Support AMD MoRI-IO #1469.

Signed-off-by: Shiksha Patel <shiksha.patel@amd.com>

records.title: fix(gke): override RDMA resource requests to fix scheduling on H200
records.body:
GKE Warden mutating webhook automatically injects resource requests for both networking.gke.io.networks/rdma-X and networking.gke.io.networks/rdma-X.IP. However, modern GKE H200 (A3 Ultra) nodes only advertise the .IP variant, which prevents pods from scheduling.

Explicitly setting the legacy networking.gke.io.networks/rdma-X limits to 0 prevents the webhook from injecting the resource requests for the non-.IP variant. This resolves the scheduling deadlock on H200 nodes while maintaining compatibility, since the webhook still injects the .IP variant.

records.title: FMA guide
records.body:
## Summary

- Add an end-to-end Fast Model Actuation (FMA) guide integrating FMA with the llm-d router
- Author it in the **structured-guides format** from #1988 (machine-readable `guide.yaml` + README rendered/validated from it, kustomize manifests)
- Demonstrate inference through the router and the sleep/wake lifecycle to showcase FMA's speed benefit
- Verified end-to-end on a real OpenShift GPU cluster (deploy → inference → sleep → wake → teardown)

> [!NOTE]
> **Depends on #1988.** The render/validate scripts (`scripts/guide-{render,check-yaml,check-readme}.py`) and the shared `guides/env.sh` live on that PR. `env.sh` pins `ROUTER_CHART_VERSION=v0.9.0` and the stable `llm-d-router-standalone` chart. This branch rebases on top of #1988 once it merges.

## What this guide covers

1. **Full deployment**: FMA CRDs, controllers (Helm), RBAC, the llm-d router, and the FMA resources (ISC, LauncherConfig, LauncherPopulationPolicy, requesting pods)
2. **Inference verification**: send completions through the llm-d router to the vLLM instances managed by FMA
3. **Sleep/Wake demo**: scale the requesting Deployment to 0 (sleep — vLLM stays resident in GPU memory) and back up (wake — resumes without a cold model reload)
4. **Benchmarking**: `llmdbenchmark` section using the `nop` harness (stands the stack up/validates without driving synthetic load)

## Structured-guide format (#1988)

The guide is no longer hand-maintained prose with inline `kubectl apply -f - <<EOF` heredocs. It now consists of:

- **`guide.yaml`** — the single source of truth for every bash block (`env`, `prerequisites`, `deploy`, `verify`, `benchmark`, `cleanup`).
- **`README.md`** — prose with `<!-- guide:<path> start/end -->` markers; bash blocks are rendered from `guide.yaml` and checked in CI.
- **Kustomize trees** — `rbac/`, `modelserver/` (ISC + LauncherConfig + LPP), `requester/` (the requesting-pods Deployment), so the guide can be stood up with `standup_method: kustomize`.

## Key decisions

- Uses `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B` (public model, no HF token needed) to reduce prerequisites
- Requesting pods are a **Deployment** (not a bare `ReplicaSet`) for compatibility with autoscalers such as WVA
- ISC enables sleep with `--enable-sleep-mode`; `HF_HOME=/tmp/hf_cache` (with a NOTE recommending a PVC for production/benchmarking so weights and compiled graphs persist)
- RBAC: the guide creates the `fma-node-viewer` ClusterRole and a namespace-scoped launcher pod-reader Role/RoleBinding; the **node-viewer ClusterRoleBinding is created by the Helm chart** via `--set global.nodeViewClusterRole=fma-node-viewer`
- `launcherCount: 1` per GPU node — only launchers bound to requesting pods start vLLM
- Documents the OpenShift-specific need for `runtimeClassName: nvidia`

## Tested on

- OpenShift (OCP) cluster with NVIDIA GPUs — deployed from scratch and validated end-to-end, then torn down
- **FMA v0.6.2**; llm-d router **`llm-d-router-standalone@v0.9.0`** (stable chart)
- Completion request served correctly through the router; **sleep/wake verified**: on scale-to-0 the controller unbinds the requester and the launcher keeps vLLM resident (GPU retained); on scale-up it re-binds and serves again without a model reload

## Files changed

- `guides/fast-model-actuation/guide.yaml` — **new**, machine-readable source of truth
- `guides/fast-model-actuation/README.md` — rewritten with `guide:` markers, rendered from `guide.yaml`
- `guides/fast-model-actuation/rbac/` — **new** kustomize tree (ClusterRole + launcher Role/RoleBinding)
- `guides/fast-model-actuation/modelserver/` — **new** kustomize tree (ISC, LauncherConfig, LauncherPopulationPolicy)
- `guides/fast-model-actuation/requester/` — **new** kustomize tree (requesting-pods Deployment)
- `guides/fast-model-actuation/router/fast-model-actuation.values.yaml` — router Helm values (now used with the stable chart)
- `guides/README.md` — add the FMA guide to the index

## Findings from live testing

- **`--enable-sleep-mode` works without `VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1`** — the guide's ISC is simpler than FMA's e2e `mkobjs-openshift.sh` and has no gap; the controller drives sleep/wake without vLLM dev mode
- **ClusterRoleBinding name collision** — the chart creates a cluster-scoped `<release-name>-node-view` binding; two FMA deployments in different namespaces sharing the default release name `fma` collide. Worked around in testing with a unique release name; flagged as an upstream fix
- Image tags are pinned to `v0.6.2` directly in the kustomize manifests (kustomize's `images:` transformer is unreliable against CRD-embedded pod templates); bump them alongside `FMA_VERSION`

## Known limitations (documented in guide)

- Wake only avoids a cold start if the new requesting pod is scheduled onto the same node/GPU as the sleeping instance (scheduler-dependent); most valuable in multi-GPU-per-node setups
- ISC `env_vars` does not support `secretKeyRef` — gated models need alternative secret injection
- The FMA Helm chart still does not ship the `fma-node-viewer` ClusterRole or the launcher pod-reader Role/RoleBinding (created by the guide)

## Follow-up work

- Nightly E2E CI workflow (`standup_method: kustomize`, `scenario_dir: guides`, `standup_scenario: fast-model-actuation`)
- `config/scenarios/guides/fast-model-actuation.yaml` in llm-d-benchmark + README status badge

records.title: agentic-serving with token-load scorer
records.body:
## Summary

Optimizes the **agentic-serving** guide's router configuration for prefix-cache-aware routing on KV-offloaded deployments, and makes the benchmark reproducible per concurrency level. On the agentic code-generation workload (Qwen3-Coder-480B-FP8, 8× TPU v7x), the optimized config sustains **~3× the throughput** (~120K vs ~40K tok/s peak) and **dramatically lower TTFT** vs the plain k8s-Service baseline.

## What changed

- **Router config (`router/agentic-workloads.values.yaml`)** — switch to `token-load-scorer` + `inflight-load-producer` + `approx-prefix-cache-producer` + `prefix-cache-affinity-filter`. The producer's LRU is sized for the **KV-cache offload tier** (`autoTune: false`, `lruCapacityPerServer` set manually); `peakPrefillThroughput` is calibrated for this model/hardware. (See note re: the LRU workaround below.)
- **Chart** — deploy via `llm-d-router-standalone-dev` (`v0`) and add the missing **GAIE CRD install** step.
- **Benchmark template (`benchmark-templates/guide.yaml`)** — parameterize the workload on `${CONCURRENCY_LEVEL}` / `${NUM_REQUESTS}` / `${SEED}` (one stage per run) so each concurrency level is an isolated run; bump the benchmark image to `v0.6.8.1`.
- **Calibration tooling (`calibration/`, new)** — `calibrate.sh` + measurement Job + values template + README to measure `peakPrefillThroughput` (it's hardware/model-specific).
- **Results** — refreshed `benchmark-results/` charts (now through conc=80) and the summary table.

## Why a separate seed per concurrency level

The benchmark uses `conversation_replay` with **`num_conversations = ${CONCURRENCY_LEVEL}`**, and each concurrency level is run as a **separate** benchmark against the **same** running deployment. With a *fixed* seed, the generated conversations are **nested** — the seeded RNG produces conversations `1…N`, so conc=40's prompts are an exact **subset** of conc=80's (the first 40 are identical).

Because the deployment caches prefixes — and with KV-cache offloading those prefixes persist in host memory across runs — a later, higher-concurrency run would hit caches **already warmed by the earlier, lower-concurrency runs** that shared prompts with it. That inflates the prefix-cache hit rate and produces optimistic, **cross-run-contaminated** TTFT/throughput for the higher concurrencies.

Setting a **distinct seed per concurrency** (`SEED = 7 + CONCURRENCY_LEVEL`) makes every run draw an **independent** prompt set, eliminating cross-run cache carryover so each concurrency point is measured cleanly.

records.title: docs: rewrite getting-started intro as combined landing page (mdx) — supersedes #1800
records.body:
## Summary

Replaces `docs/getting-started/README.md` with `README.mdx` so the combined-landing intro page can use Docusaurus's `<Link>` component for its hero CTAs. The `.mdx` conversion plus the clean version-aware paths means clicks on the buttons stay in the current `/docs/<version>/` context instead of doing hard navigations that cross version boundaries (which would 404 against routes that don't exist in the current Docusaurus app).

Supersedes #1800. This PR carries the same hero copy / founders strip / CNCF Sandbox badge / Key capabilities / "Why use llm-d?" benchmarks that #1800 introduced, with the following targeted fixes layered on:

### Diffs from #1800

| Surface | What #1800 has | What this PR ships |
|---|---|---|
| File extension | `README.md` (raw HTML `<a>` for CTAs) | `README.mdx` with `import Link from '@docusaurus/Link';` |
| "Get started" CTA | `<a href="./quickstart">` | `<Link to="/getting-started/quickstart">` |
| "View performance analysis" CTA | `<a href="/docs/guides/optimized-baseline">` | `<Link target="_blank" to="https://prism.llm-d.ai/">` |
| "See all guides" CTA | `<a href="/docs/guides">` text "See all guides" | `<Link to="/well-lit-paths">` text "See all well-lit paths" |
| Key capability: Advanced KV-cache management | `/docs/guides/kv-cache-management` (404) | `/well-lit-paths/tiered-prefix-cache` |
| Key capability: Serving large models | `/docs/guides/serving-large-models` (404) | `/well-lit-paths/pd-disaggregation` |
| Key capability: Operational excellence | `/docs/guides/operational-excellence` (404) | `/well-lit-paths/workload-autoscaling` |
| Key capability: Batch processing | `/docs/guides/batch-processing` (404) | `/well-lit-paths/asynchronous-processing` |

### Why these changes matter

- **Buttons cross version boundaries in #1800.** The raw `<a>` tags do hard browser navigation; clicking from `/docs/dev/getting-started` sends users to `/docs/getting-started/quickstart` (latest stable), not `/docs/dev/getting-started/quickstart`. `<Link>` with a leading-slash path resolves against the current docs `baseUrl` and stays in the current version.
- **`./quickstart` relative URL was 404'ing.** With `trailingSlash: false`, a relative `./` from `/docs/getting-started` (no trailing slash) resolves against the parent directory `/docs/`, not the page itself. So the click went to `/docs/quickstart` which doesn't exist.
- **`/docs/guides/...` is the wrong slug.** The Well-Lit Paths route lives at `/well-lit-paths` (formerly `/guides/`). Most upstream content has been canonicalized already by `sync-docs.sh`'s `Canonicalizing /guides links to /well-lit-paths` step, but the slugs referenced in #1800 don't all have well-lit-paths counterparts. The slugs in this PR match real existing pages.

## Pairs with

- **llm-d/llm-d.github.io#362** (the website-side consolidated PR for chrome + combined landing). That PR's `sync-docs.sh` change prefers `README.mdx` over `README.md` if both exist, so this file lands correctly into `preview/docs/getting-started/index.mdx` on sync.

## Test plan

- [ ] Once merged + synced into the website build, `/docs/dev/getting-started` shows the same combined-landing as #1800.
- [ ] Clicking "Get started" stays in `/docs/dev/` (or the current version) — no hard navigation across versions.
- [ ] "View performance analysis" opens https://prism.llm-d.ai/ in a new tab.
- [ ] "See all well-lit paths" lands on `/docs/dev/well-lit-paths` (or version-equivalent).
- [ ] All 5 Key capabilities bullets resolve to real guide pages with content.

## Supersedes

llm-d/llm-d#1800

records.title: [SGLang]: Increase the memory used for KV cache and update benchmark results in optimized baseline
records.body:
Earlier, benchmarks for SGLang were using mem-fraction-static to be default (~82%) which was causing early saturation for sglang deployment with the same benchmark. The --mem-fraction-static parameter in [SGLang](https://sgl-project.github.io/references/faq.html) controls the portion of available GPU memory dedicated to the static memory pool, which primarily hosts the KV cache.
In this change, the mem-fraction-static is bumped up to 90%. vLLM deployments use 95% as the limit but SGLang deployment at 95% fails with out of memory errors while loading CUDA kernels. 





SGLang [docs](https://docs.sglang.io/docs/advanced_features/hyperparameter_tuning#tune-mem-fraction-static-to-increase-kv-cache-pool-capacity) recommends to gradually increase the mem-fraction-static. I think 90% is a safe spot upon trying different numbers as above 92%, I started seeing OOM errors.

Related issues: #1750 #1749

records.title: Nightly llm-d-router resource usage test
records.body:
This PR creates a new nightly test that runs inference-perf job and records llm-d-router resource usage to a markdown file in the repo.

The test logic is in a python helper file which is used to run inference-perf job against the current kubectl context.

The pipeline supports the following configurable parameters (via manual triggers and environment variables):
- `guide_name` (e.g. `optimized-baseline`): the recipe name to use for llm-d-router configuration.
- `test_name`: the name to use in the output results.
-  `perf_job`: the path to the inference-perf configuration to use for the benchmark job.

records.title: feat: centralize model server images via Kustomize Components
records.body:
## Summary

- Introduces 8 Kustomize Components under `guides/recipes/modelserver/components/images/` (gpu-vllm, gpu-sglang, amd-vllm, amd-sglang, cpu-vllm, xpu-vllm, hpu-vllm, tpu-vllm) that define project-wide default container images per accelerator/engine combination
- Refactors 20 guide overlays across `optimized-baseline`, `precise-prefix-cache-routing`, `pd-disaggregation`, `tiered-prefix-cache`, and `rollouts` to reference components instead of duplicating inline `images:` blocks
- Fixes a silent bug in `precise-prefix-cache-routing` TPU v6/v7 overlays where `newTag` was silently ignored because the base already transformed the image name via `newName`, causing v6/v7 to deploy untagged images (`vllm/vllm-tpu` instead of `vllm/vllm-tpu:v0.11.1`)

### How it works

Each component is a `kind: Component` that sets the default image for `REPLACE_MODEL_SERVER_IMAGE`:

```yaml
# guides/recipes/modelserver/components/images/gpu-vllm/kustomization.yaml
apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1alpha1
kind: Component
images:
  - name: REPLACE_MODEL_SERVER_IMAGE
    newName: vllm/vllm-openai
    newTag: v0.19.1
```

Guide overlays reference the component instead of duplicating the image config:

```yaml
# Before (repeated in every overlay):
images:
  - name: REPLACE_MODEL_SERVER_IMAGE
    newName: vllm/vllm-openai
    newTag: v0.19.1

# After:
components:
  - ../../../../../recipes/modelserver/components/images/gpu-vllm
```

To change the default GPU/vllm image for testing, edit one file. Overlays that intentionally use non-default images (pd-disaggregation gpu/vllm, tiered-prefix-cache gpu/vllm, multimodal-serving, agentic-serving, wide-ep-lws) keep their inline `images:` overrides unchanged.

records.title: fix(wide-ep-lws): use single targetPort for data-parallel-hybrid-lb mode
records.body:
## Summary

Fix `targetPorts` in the wide-ep-lws router config for the two different DP modes:

**Regular wide-ep-lws** (`--data-parallel-hybrid-lb`): Uses a single API server on port 8000 that internally load-balances across all DP ranks. Ports 8001-8007 are not open. Fix: `targetPorts: [{number: 8000}]`.

**Experimental dp-aware** (`--data-parallel-multi-port-external-lb`): Each DP rank listens on its own port (8000-8007). This mode needs all 8 ports. Fix: give dp-aware its own router values file at `experimental-dp-aware/router/wide-ep-lws.values.yaml` with multi-port targetPorts, so it no longer shares the single-port config.

Previously both modes shared `wide-ep-lws/router/wide-ep-lws.values.yaml` with ports 8000-8007, which was correct for dp-aware but caused 87.5% request failures for the regular guide.

Found during v0.9.0-rc.2 release verification.

## Changes

1. `guides/wide-ep-lws/router/wide-ep-lws.values.yaml` — reduce to `targetPorts: [{number: 8000}]`
2. `guides/wide-ep-lws/experimental-dp-aware/router/wide-ep-lws.values.yaml` — new file, keeps multi-port targetPorts (8000-8007)
3. `guides/wide-ep-lws/experimental-dp-aware/README.md` — reference the dp-aware-specific values file

records.title: Add async-processor operations guide
records.body:
## Summary

Adds an operations guide for the **Async Processor** under `docs/operations/`. The focus is **how to size the llm-d async container**, with concurrency as the central decision.

- `docs/operations/async-processor.md` — throughput model, concurrency sizing, container resources, horizontal scaling.
- `docs/operations/README.md` — link entry for the new guide.

## Concurrency sizing is backed by a measured sweep

A closed-loop sweep (each worker holds one in-flight request for its full duration — exactly an Async Processor worker) was run against a live llm-d stack: **Llama-3.1-8B on vLLM (`--max-num-seq 1024`), a single H100-80GB**, ~256-token outputs, dispatched through the inference gateway + EPP.

| Concurrency | Throughput (req/s) | Mean latency (s) | GPU KV used | Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **8 (default)** | **4.2** | 1.9 | <1% | GPU essentially idle |
| 64 | 24.1 | 2.6 | 5% | |
| 128 | 35.8 | 3.6 | 12% | approaching saturation |
| 192 | 40.4 | 4.7 | 16% | knee |
| 256 | 44.3 | 5.8 | 20% | past knee |
| 512 | 61.4 | 9.7 | 51% | unstable (errors recurred) |

Results:
- The **default `concurrency: 8` leaves the GPU ~90% idle** (~4 req/s) — ~10× below what the same hardware sustains.
- The **saturation knee is ~128–192** (16–24× the default).
- **Little's Law held exactly**: `in-flight = throughput × latency` matched the worker count at every stable point, validating `concurrency ≈ throughput × latency × 1.3`.
- A single replica destabilized past ~256 → argues for capping per-replica concurrency and scaling out.

## Notes / open items (WIP)

- CPU/memory figures in the Container Resource Sizing section are **architecture-derived** (clearly labeled), not yet measured from a real async-processor deployment.
- Benchmark covers a single 8B/H100 backend at ~256-token outputs; broader profiles (long-output, large agentic payloads) are extrapolated.

records.title: [TensorRT-LLM] trtllm-serve recipe and optimized baseline guide
records.body:
## Summary

Adds a TensorRT-LLM (`trtllm-serve`) variant to the optimized-baseline guide, so the load-aware and prefix-cache-aware router works with TensorRT-LLM model servers (with `trtllm-serve` frontend) alongside the existing vLLM and SGLang paths.

Fixes #1550.

## What this adds
  - **Model server overlay** `modelserver/gpu/trtllm/{base,gke}`: a `trtllm-serve` Deployment, a ConfigMap with the required perf-metrics flags, and kustomize overlays. Mirrors the vLLM/SGLang footprint (Qwen3-32B, 8 replicas at TP=2).
  - **Router values** `router/optimized-baseline-trtllm.values.yaml`: sets `modelServers.type: trtllm-serve` and scrapes `/prometheus/metrics`.
  - **Guide README** section for the trtllm-serve path and its metric requirements.
  - **Nightly E2E workflow** `nightly-e2e-optimized-baseline-gke-trtllm.yaml`, matching the vLLM GKE nightly (same cluster, H100, footprint).
  - **Docs** update in `docs/architecture/core/model-servers.md` describing the trtllm-serve metric requirements.

  ## TensorRT-LLM requirements (encoded in the overlay)

  - Image v1.3.0rc12 or newer. The iteration-state gauges the load scorers read were added in [TensorRT-LLM PR #12545](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/pull/12545).
  - Server started with `return_perf_metrics: true` and `enable_iter_perf_stats: true`.
  - Metrics scraped at `/prometheus/metrics`, not `/metrics`.

  ## Validation

Deployed verbatim on GKE H100 (4 nodes, 8 GPUs each), 8 replicas at TP=2, standalone mode.
  - 240 of 240 shared-prefix requests succeeded with no failures.
  - Prefix-cache-aware routing sent same-prefix traffic to cache-warm pods, with `trtllm_kv_cache_hit_rate` near 0.80 on the serving pods.
  - The router reads the trtllm gauges (they populate after the first request) and routes on them.

## Problem

The quickstart guide (`docs/getting-started/quickstart.md`) references the
upstream GAIE standalone chart:

    oci://registry.k8s.io/gateway-api-inference-extension/charts/standalone --version v1.5.0

This chart expects `inferenceExtension:` and `inferencePool:` as top-level
value keys, but the values files on `main` (`guides/recipes/router/base.values.yaml`,
`guides/optimized-baseline/router/optimized-baseline.values.yaml`) use the
`router:` key structure introduced with the llm-d Router charts. The mismatch
causes `helm install` to fail with:

    .Values.inferencePool.modelServers.matchLabels is required

Every other guide on `main` already points to the correct llm-d chart
(`oci://ghcr.io/llm-d/charts/llm-d-router-standalone-dev --version v0`);
the quickstart was the only outlier.

## Fix

- Add `ROUTER_CHART_VERSION=v0` environment variable (consistent with all
  other guides).
- Update the `helm install` command to use the llm-d router standalone chart
  at `oci://ghcr.io/llm-d/charts/llm-d-router-standalone-dev`.
- Use `--version ${ROUTER_CHART_VERSION}` instead of `--version ${GAIE_VERSION}`.

`GAIE_VERSION` is retained and still used for CRD installation.

records.title: guides/precise-prefix-cache-routing: run the renderer as a Service, not an EPP sidecar
records.body:
The tokenizer renderer was injected as a per-EPP-pod `vllm-render` sidecar by the standalone chart (`router.tokenizer.enabled: true`). That couples render capacity to the EPP replica count and duplicates the tokenizer in every EPP pod.

Replace it with a standalone, horizontally-scalable render Service:
- Add `render/` kustomize overlay: a `vllm launch render` Deployment (3 replicas)
  + ClusterIP Service, mirroring the chart's sidecar container spec.
- Disable the sidecar (`router.tokenizer.enabled: false`) and point the EPP `token-producer` plugin at the Service (`http://precise-prefix-cache-routing-render:8000`).
- Keep the `llm-d.ai/guide` label off render pods — it is the InferencePool / model-server selector, so labeled render pods would be treated as routable model servers (and the EPP would try to ZMQ-subscribe to their nonexistent :5556 KV-event socket).
- README: document deploying/cleaning up the render Service + the label caveat.

records.title: fix: correct argument order for dockerfile env-var linter invocations
records.body:
## Summary

- Corrects the argument order in two callers of `scripts/lint-dockerfile-envvars.py`

`scripts/lint-dockerfile-envvars.py` takes the scripts directory as its first argument and Dockerfiles after it (`scripts_dir = sys.argv[1]`; usage `lint-dockerfile-envvars.py <scripts-dir> <Dockerfile>`). The `lint-dockerfile-envvars` pre-commit hook already calls it that way via `args: [docker/scripts]` + `pass_filenames: true`.

Two callers had the arguments reversed:

- `scripts/test-dockerfile-lint.sh` (the linter's self-test) called it as `<Dockerfile> <scripts-dir>`, so it read the scripts directory as a Dockerfile and crashed with `IsADirectoryError` before linting. Test 1 reported a false pass (the crash's nonzero exit landed in the failure branch) and Test 2 failed, so `bash scripts/test-dockerfile-lint.sh` exited 1 and exercised none of the linter logic.
- `scripts/ENVVARS.md` documented the same reversed order, so the example commands crash when copied.

Swapping the arguments makes both match the linter's contract. The self-test now exits 0, with Test 1 detecting the missing variable and Test 2 passing.

#1302 fixed the same bug in the test but was closed unmerged; this applies that correction and also fixes the matching commands in `scripts/ENVVARS.md`.

## Test plan

- [x] `bash scripts/test-dockerfile-lint.sh` exits 0 (previously exited 1)
- [x] `pre-commit run --files scripts/test-dockerfile-lint.sh scripts/ENVVARS.md` passes

records.title: Add a guide for LLM Cold Start Optimization
records.body:
This PR introduces a guide for LLM Cold Start Optimization under guides/fast-startup/.

**[Note: GKE only]** This guide demonstrates how to combine GKE Image Streaming and GKE Pod Snapshots to eliminate the two main bottlenecks of LLM container deployment (image pull and model engine initialization). Together, these GKE-exclusive features reduce the total cold-start latency of a LLM container (**meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct** serving via vLLM on a **single NVIDIA L4 GPU**) from **nearly 7 minutes to just 15 seconds** (a 96.3% latency reduction).

Deployment Scenario | Image Pull Time | Model/Engine Initialization | Total Startup Time | Latency Reduction
-- | -- | -- | -- | --
Standard Cold Start (Baseline) | ~214s | ~195s | ~409s (6.8 mins) | Baseline
GKE Image Streaming Only | ~4s | ~195s | ~199s (3.3 mins) | ~51.6%
Pod Snapshots Only | ~214s | ~11s | ~225s (3.8 mins) | ~45%
Optimized Stack (Streaming + Snapshots) | ~4s | ~11s | ~15s (15 seconds) | ~96.3%

This PR includes:
- a detailed README file with overview, benchmarking result above, and instructions on how to optimize cold start problem on GKE.
- a recipe that specifically designed to run with pod snapshot feature on GKE.

Limitations & Plans for future:
- **GPU support**: This guide is tested on single GPU using 1 X NVIDIA L4. Multi-GPU support with inter-GPU communication (TP>1) will be tested and added later (e.g. 8 X NVIDIA L4). There is currently a cuda checkpoint limitation on NCCL P2P and NCCL SHM support so cross-GPU communication with A100 and above is limited. TPUs currently not supported. 
- **Duplicate Weights (affecting performance)**: Before pod snapshot trigger, we remove duplicate model weights from disk to reduce the snapshot size. Currently the recipe is only optimized for model weights downloaded from hugging face. If other source is used, the duplicate model weights removal needs to be adjusted accordingly. We are working on integrating the snapshotting feature in vllm so that users do not need to make adjustment in the future.

records.title: docs(agentic-serving): add TPU v7 disaggregated P/D benchmark results and manifests
records.body:
## Description
This PR introduces experimental Prefill/Decode (P/D) disaggregation serving benchmark results and deployment templates for **Qwen3-Coder-480B-FP8** serving on **Google TPU v7** to the `agentic-serving` guide.
### Key Changes

### TPU disaggregation guide (pd-disaggregation/README.tpu.md):

* Moved the experimental TPU disagg setup here from the agentic-serving guide.

* Updated the guide with the latest benchmark results under the uncapped 262K context agentic workload.
Removed "prefix-aware routing" from the limitations list since it is configured by default.

###  Benchmark Workload Template (agentic-code-gen-disagg.yaml):

* Renamed the template from agentic-code-gen-capped-55k-disagg.yaml to agentic-code-gen-disagg.yaml.
* Removed the 55K context limit, updating the max_model_len to 262144 to match the model's capacity.

---
### Benchmark Findings Summary (at Concurrency 40)
For the uncapped agentic workload (average prompt size ~128K tokens, outputs ~1.1K tokens), the KV cache size grows to ~20GB per request, shifting the bottleneck from prefill compute to decoder HBM capacity.

Under this regime, allocating more TPU capacity to the decode phase (2:6 prefill-to-decode ratio) yields the best performance:
* TTFT Median: 45x faster compared to the 6:2 ratio (7.3s vs. 329.5s) by providing sufficient aggregate HBM to avoid severe queueing.
* Output Throughput: 3.5x higher overall output throughput (295.1 tok/s vs. 84.2 tok/s).
* Error Rate: Maintained at a low 2.8% (compared to 1:7 which has a 10.4% error rate due to prefiller overload).
* _Note: As prefix-aware routing and CPU KV cache offloading are not yet enabled for this TPU setup, overall performance remains below the unified `llm-d-optimized` baseline. These integrations are currently active areas of development._
